    - Key Defender Put In Conflict: LURKER (Floating middle robber/lurker)
    - Why It Works: Quarterbacks facing Flores’ Cover 0 are coached to release the ball in under 1.5 seconds to their primary hot read; dropping 8 turns that hot throw into an interception.
    - Failure Mode / Defensive Counter: QB with exceptional pocket poise who holds the ball, scrambles against the 3-man rush, and finds a late-developing scramble drill opening.

    [SEQUENCING & GAME-PLAN LOGIC]

      * [T=0.7s] 4 Rushers Bail into Short Passing Lanes: At the snap, 4 mugged linebackers bail backward into intermediate zone cushions while only 3 rushers push the pocket, instantly flooding all underneath passing lanes.
      * [T=1.6s] QB Throws Hot Right into Lurker’s Chest: Conditioned to throw in 1.5 seconds against Cover 0, the QB delivers a blind hot slant directly to where LURKER has dropped into the passing window.
      * [T=2.2s] Turnover Forced: Lurk Interception: LURKER intercepts the pass in stride with 8 defenders blanketing every receiver, converting Flores’ psychological pressure into an explosive defensive turnover.

SCHEME FAMILY: VIC FANGIO'S TWO-HIGH SHELL & QUARTERS MATCHING [ID: fangio-two-high-shell]
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Architect / Coach: Vic Fangio
Organization / Team: Philadelphia Eagles / Denver Broncos
Category: DEFENSE
Tree Branch: fangio-two-high
Core Philosophy: The defensive philosophy that reshaped modern NFL game-planning. Built on a static, impenetrable two-high safety shell pre-snap that disguises split-field Cover 6 (Quarter-Quarter-Half), Palms Match Quarters (2-Read), Drop-8 simulated creeper pressures, and lethal boundary corner traps. Paired with light-box 5-1-5 Penny fronts that suffocate explosive passing concepts while matching underneath crossing routes.

PLAYS IN THIS SCHEME:

>>> PLAY: Cover 6 (Quarter-Quarter-Half Split Safety) (ID: cover6-quarter-quarter-half)
    Personnel: Penny 5-1-5 Nickel
    Formation: Penny 5-1-5 vs 11P Gun 2x2 Seams
    Situation: 1st & 10, +45, base down passing look
    Defensive Look: Cover 6 (Quarter-Quarter-Half Split Field) (Penny 5-1-5 Tite 4-Man Rush)
    Animation Duration: 4s
    Direct URL: https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=fangio-two-high-shell&play=cover6-quarter-quarter-half

    [SUMMARY & TACTICAL PURPOSE]
    - Motive: Present an ambiguous 2-high shell pre-snap, then split the field into Quarters to the passing strength and Cover 2 to the boundary to suffocate vertical seams and intermediate outs.
    - Key Defender Put In Conflict: Field Safety (FS) matching #2 seam and Boundary CB (LCB) playing cloud squat on the flat
    - Why It Works: Offenses expect traditional Cover 2 or single-high Cover 3; split-field Cover 6 eliminates the field seam without leaving the boundary corner isolated 1-on-1.
    - Failure Mode / Defensive Counter: Boundary smash route if the safety fails to get over top of the corner squat in time, or interior run if offense checks to draw against the 1-linebacker box.

    [SEQUENCING & GAME-PLAN LOGIC]
    - Sets Up: penny-match-quarters, tite-creeper-drop8, cover8-boundary-trap
    - Plays Off: None
    - Visual Tell Cue: Base split-safety structure: Field safety matches slot seam in Quarters while Boundary safety rolls to deep half.

    [TIMELINE COACHING BEATS]
      * [T=0.0s] Static Two-High Pre-Snap Disguise: Fangio aligns in an unmistakable two-high shell with safeties deep at 12 yards and a light Penny 5-1-5 front, disguising whether the coverage is Quarters, Cover 6, or Cover 8.
      * [T=1.2s] Field Quarters Clamps the Seam: At the snap, Field Safety FS instantly reads Y vertical and clamps his inside hip in Quarters match, while RCB locks down Z on the outside.
      * [T=2.3s] Boundary Cloud Collision & Flat Trap: LCB reroutes X into the boundary and squats on H in the flat, while Boundary Safety BS ranges to the deep half to erase the sideline hole shot.
      * [T=3.5s] Quarterback Hesitation & Pocket Collapse: With the field seam clamped and boundary flat suffocated, the QB double-clutches as ROLB bends the edge for a drive-ending sack.

>>> PLAY: Penny 5-1-5 Match Quarters (Palms / 2-Read) (ID: penny-match-quarters)
    Personnel: Penny 5-1-5 Nickel
    Formation: Penny 5-1-5 vs 11P Gun 2x2 Smash-Out
    Situation: 2nd & 7, +35, medium passing down
    Defensive Look: Cover 4 Match (Palms / 2-Read) (Penny 5-1-5 4-Man Rush)
    Animation Duration: 4s
    Direct URL: https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=fangio-two-high-shell&play=penny-match-quarters

    [SUMMARY & TACTICAL PURPOSE]
    - Motive: Deploy symmetrical 4-deep match (Palms / 2-Read) from the identical 2-high pre-snap shell to jump quick out routes and rob crossing patterns.
    - Key Defender Put In Conflict: STAR (Nickel) reading #2 out-break and BS (Boundary Safety) driving top-down on #1
    - Why It Works: Palms rules allow the underneath nickel/corner to aggressively jump shallow out-breaking routes because the safety is keyed to drive on any inside break by #1.
    - Failure Mode / Defensive Counter: Double moves or Wheel-Post combinations if the safety hesitates on the trigger.

    [SEQUENCING & GAME-PLAN LOGIC]
    - Sets Up: tite-creeper-drop8
    - Plays Off: cover6-quarter-quarter-half
    - Visual Tell Cue: Both safeties trigger top-down at 10-12 yards matching #2 receivers vertical while Star DB plays palms flat.

    [TIMELINE COACHING BEATS]
      * [T=0.0s] Disguised Two-High Safety Stem: Fangio shows the identical two-high safety look as Cover 6. Pre-snap, the QB anticipates soft boundary cushions or Cover 2 holes.
      * [T=1.2s] Palms 2-Read: Star DB Jumps the Out: The moment #2 H breaks on the shallow out route, STAR triggers downhill with full aggression to undercut the flat throw under Palms rules.
      * [T=2.3s] Boundary Safety Drives Top-Down on Post: With STAR taking the out, Boundary Safety BS reads the route distribution and drives downhill from 12 yards to completely erase X on the post.
      * [T=3.5s] Contested Catch Window on Intermediate Dig: The QB resets and fires to Y on the dig, but MIKE and FS close the vice clamp from underneath and over the top to force the incompletion.

>>> PLAY: Tite Creeper Drop-8 Coverage Trap (ID: tite-creeper-drop8)
    Personnel: Penny 5-1-5 Sim Front
    Formation: Penny 5-1-5 Sim Rush vs 11P Gun 2x2 Spacing
    Situation: 3rd & 8, +42, obvious passing down
    Defensive Look: Drop-8 Sim Zone (3-Man Rush / 8-Man Drop) (Penny Sim Drop-8 Front)

    [SUMMARY & TACTICAL PURPOSE]

    - Key Defender Put In Conflict: LOLB & ROLB executing bluff-and-drop into hook-curl passing lanes
    - Why It Works: Offenses rely on quick slants and seams to beat 5-man pressures; dropping 8 turns those hot routes into contested traps with zero open receivers.
    - Failure Mode / Defensive Counter: Three-man rush failing to generate pressure over 4+ seconds, allowing a mobile QB to scramble or break contain.

    [SEQUENCING & GAME-PLAN LOGIC]
    - Sets Up: None
    - Plays Off: cover6-quarter-quarter-half, penny-match-quarters
    - Visual Tell Cue: Both edge rushers bluff penetration then bail into intermediate hook-curl lanes as defense drops 8.

    [TIMELINE COACHING BEATS]

      * [T=1.1s] Edge Linebackers Bail into Passing Lanes: At the snap, both LOLB and ROLB bluff penetration then abruptly bail into the intermediate hook-curl lanes, creating an 8-man coverage shell.
      * [T=2.2s] Hot Reads Completely Blanketed: The QB looks for his hot slant to X and crosser to Y, only to find LOLB and MIKE sitting directly in both throwing windows with no open targets.
      * [T=3.5s] Drop-8 Coverage Sack: With eight defenders blanketing four receivers and nowhere to throw, the 3-man interior rush collapses the pocket for a drive-ending coverage sack.

>>> PLAY: Cover 8 Boundary Corner Trap (ID: cover8-boundary-trap)
    Personnel: Penny 5-1-5 Nickel
    Formation: Penny 5-1-5 vs 11P Gun 2x2 Out-Shot
    Situation: 3rd & 4, +30, boundary passing down

    Animation Duration: 4s

    [SUMMARY & TACTICAL PURPOSE]

    - Key Defender Put In Conflict: LCB (Boundary Corner) timing the trap break and BS (Boundary Safety) capping deep vertical routes
    - Why It Works: Quarterbacks are taught to take the quick boundary out against Quarters off-coverage; Cover 8 trap turns a high-percentage throw into a pick-six.
    - Failure Mode / Defensive Counter: Quarterback pumps the out-route and hits the sideline seam before the safety reaches the deep half.

    [SEQUENCING & GAME-PLAN LOGIC]
    - Sets Up: None
    - Plays Off: cover6-quarter-quarter-half
    - Visual Tell Cue: Boundary corner squats and traps out-route underneath while Boundary safety rotates over top.

    [TIMELINE COACHING BEATS]
      * [T=0.0s] Two-High Safety Shell Disguise: The defense presents the standard 2-high pre-snap look with LCB giving a soft 6.5-yard cushion on X, inviting the quick sideline out throw on 3rd down.
      * [T=1.2s] Boundary Corner Bait & Trap: As X stems to 8 yards and breaks toward the sideline, LCB plants his back foot and undercuts the out-route with full acceleration in Cover 8 trap.
      * [T=2.3s] Safety Caps the Deep Post: Boundary Safety BS rotates over top of the vacated corner to cap H on the vertical post, sealing the deep half against any double-move.
      * [T=3.4s] Underneath Interception Trap: LCB jumps in front of the sideline pass for a game-changing interception and pick-six return as the QB is caught in the split-field trap.

SCHEME FAMILY: JESSE MINTER'S AMOEBA FRONT & SIMULATED CREEPERS [ID: minter-amoeba-creeper]
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Architect / Coach: Jesse Minter
Organization / Team: Baltimore Ravens / Los Angeles Chargers
Category: DEFENSE
Tree Branch: macdonald-pressure
Core Philosophy: A masterclass in pre-snap psychological warfare and simulated pressure architectures. Jesse Minter combines standing 6-up Amoeba fronts, slot corner simulated blitzes (Creepers) dropping athletic defensive ends, disguised Cover 1 Lurk rotations that bait quarterbacks into underneath robber traps, and lethal Double-A mug Cover 0 peel blitzes that neutralize hot reads.

PLAYS IN THIS SCHEME:

>>> PLAY: Amoeba Front 5-Man Fire Zone 3 (ID: minter-amoeba-fire-zone3)

    Animation Duration: 4s
    Direct URL: https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=minter-amoeba-creeper&play=minter-amoeba-fire-zone3

    [SUMMARY & TACTICAL PURPOSE]

    - Key Defender Put In Conflict: WILL (weak A-gap blitzer) & MIKE (Amoeba bail linebacker)
    - Why It Works: Offenses check to quick hot throws against 6-up looks, but the 3-deep 3-under structure floods intermediate passing windows while 5 rushers overwhelm 5 blockers.
    - Failure Mode / Defensive Counter: Quick perimeter smoke screens or max-protect 7-man deep shots that beat 3-deep zone outside the numbers.

    [SEQUENCING & GAME-PLAN LOGIC]
    - Sets Up: minter-slot-blitz-creeper, minter-double-mug-peel

      * [T=0.8s] 5-Man Fire Zone Overload & MIKE Drop: At the snap, Minter sends 5 rushers with WILL blitzing through the weak A-gap, while MIKE bails from his A-gap mug into the strong hook zone.
      * [T=2.2s] Hot Read Slant Trapped: The QB expects Cover 0 and looks to throw his quick hot slant to Y, only to find MIKE occupying the exact throwing window with SS and Nickel bracketing the flats.
      * [T=3.5s] A-Gap Overload Pressure Closes: With the hot throw eliminated, WILL defeats the running back block and collapses the pocket for an emphatic sack.

SCHEME FAMILY: DEMECO RYANS' WIDE-9 ATTACK & MATCH COVERAGE [ID: ryans-wide9-attack]
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Architect / Coach: DeMeco Ryans
Organization / Team: Houston Texans
Category: DEFENSE
Tree Branch: carroll-saleh-wide9
Core Philosophy: An aggressive, downhill defensive system engineered around pure physical dominance and geometric leverage. Features extreme Wide-9 defensive end alignments and Tackle-Wrap stunt games that crush pass protections with 4 rushers, backed by split-field Cover 2 Palms (2-Read) cloud traps, Cover 1 Low-Hole mug looks, and field-overload 5-man fire zones.

PLAYS IN THIS SCHEME:

>>> PLAY: Wide-9 Under Front Tackle-Wrap Stunt (T-E) (ID: ryans-wide9-under-tackle-wrap)
    Personnel: Nickel 4-2-5
    Formation: 4-3 Under Wide-9 Front vs 11P Gun 2x2
    Situation: 2nd & 7, +35, standard pass down with play-action threat
    Defensive Look: Cover 3 Sky Match (Single-High with Wide-9 Rush) (4-3 Under Wide-9 Stunt Front)
    Animation Duration: 4s
    Direct URL: https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=ryans-wide9-attack&play=ryans-wide9-under-tackle-wrap

    [SUMMARY & TACTICAL PURPOSE]
    - Motive: Exploit the Wide-9 alignment by forcing offensive tackles into elongated kick-slides, then executing a Tackle-End (T-E) wrap stunt to create an unblocked interior rush lane for the defensive end.
    - Key Defender Put In Conflict: SDE (looping edge rusher) & 3T (interior spike tackle)
    - Why It Works: The threat of speed rush from the Wide-9 makes offensive tackles over-set outside, creating wide-open interior corridors when paired with an aggressive A-gap spike by the 3-technique.
    - Failure Mode / Defensive Counter: Quick rhythm 3-step slants or screens thrown before the stunt can develop and loop into the backfield.

    [SEQUENCING & GAME-PLAN LOGIC]
    - Sets Up: ryans-cover2-palms-read, ryans-overload-edge-fire
    - Plays Off: None
    - Visual Tell Cue: Wide-9 DE takes an exaggerated outside step before looping sharply inside behind the interior 3-technique spike

    [TIMELINE COACHING BEATS]
      * [T=0.0s] Wide-9 Pre-Snap Alignment: DeMeco Ryans aligns his defensive ends in extreme Wide-9 alignments outside the tackles, forcing the offensive tackles to widen their sets and opening massive interior B-gap corridors.
      * [T=0.8s] T-E Stunt: 3T Spikes Inside, SDE Sells Edge: At the snap, 3T crashes violently into the A-gap, taking the LG and Center with him. SDE takes two hard upfield steps in Wide-9, baiting the RT to overset to the sideline.
      * [T=1.8s] Tackle-Wrap Loop Opens Highway to QB: With the RT overset and the LG pinned inside by the 3T spike, SDE plants his outside foot and wraps tightly into the vacated B-gap untouched.
      * [T=3.2s] SDE Arrives for the Decisive Sack: The QB hits the top of his drop only to find SDE roaring through the interior pocket at full speed for a dominant 4-man pressure sack.

>>> PLAY: Split-Safety Palms (2-Read) Match (ID: ryans-cover2-palms-read)
    Personnel: Nickel 4-2-5
    Formation: Nickel Wide-9 Two-High vs 11P Gun 2x2 Smash
    Situation: 3rd & 6, -40, midfield passing down against 2x2 spread
    Defensive Look: Cover 2 Palms (2-Read / Cloud Trap on #2 Out) (Base 4-Down Wide-9 Front)
    Animation Duration: 4s
    Direct URL: https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=ryans-wide9-attack&play=ryans-cover2-palms-read

    [SUMMARY & TACTICAL PURPOSE]
    - Motive: Obliterate standard Smash and quick-out concepts by using split-field 2-Read (Palms) matching, enabling the cornerback to trap underneath out routes while the safety caps deep corner routes.
    - Key Defender Put In Conflict: LCB (Palms flat trap corner) & SS (over-the-top corner cap safety)
    - Why It Works: Smash concepts are designed to stress standard Cover 2 or Cover 3, but Palms matches the routes in reverse: the corner takes the underneath out, and the safety takes the deep corner.
    - Failure Mode / Defensive Counter: A double-vertical concept (4-Verticals) if the safety hesitates or gets occupied by a tight-end seam route.

    [SEQUENCING & GAME-PLAN LOGIC]
    - Sets Up: ryans-cover1-hole-mug
    - Plays Off: ryans-wide9-under-tackle-wrap
    - Visual Tell Cue: Two-high shell where the cornerback reads the #2 slot receiver and aggressively jumps the out-route while safety carries #1 deep

    [TIMELINE COACHING BEATS]
      * [T=0.0s] Split-Safety Palms Pre-Snap Alignment: DeMeco Ryans shows a balanced two-high safety shell. Cornerbacks align at 6 yards with their eyes locked entirely on the inside #2 slot receivers, using Palms (2-Read) rules.
      * [T=0.8s] 2-Read Key Triggers: #2 Breaks Out: As slot receiver H breaks on an out route (the classic Smash concept), LCB reads the release, instantly abandons X, and drives aggressively downhill to trap the out route.
      * [T=1.8s] Safety Rolls Over Top of Corner Route: Simultaneously, SS sees #2 break out, opens his hips toward the sideline, and walls off X’s deep corner route from over the top, neutralizing the offense’s deep shot.
      * [T=2.6s] LCB Intercepts Out Route for Pick-Six: The QB throws the out route expecting single-high Cover 3 coverage, but LCB jumps the route with full momentum for an interception and touchdown return.

>>> PLAY: Cover 1 Hole with Linebacker A-Gap Mug (ID: ryans-cover1-hole-mug)
    Personnel: Nickel 4-2-5
    Formation: Nickel 4-2-5 Single-Mug Front vs 11P Gun 3x1 Slant/Choice
    Situation: 3rd & 4, +18, red zone critical conversion down
    Defensive Look: Cover 1 Hole (Man-to-Man with Low-Hole MIKE Rat) (A-Gap Mug Front with Wide-9 Edges)
    Animation Duration: 4s
    Direct URL: https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=ryans-wide9-attack&play=ryans-cover1-hole-mug

    [SUMMARY & TACTICAL PURPOSE]
    - Motive: Threaten A-gap pressure to force quick slant/in routes, then drop the mugged linebacker into the low hole to bracket underneath passes while the 4-man Wide-9 front collapses the pocket.
    - Key Defender Put In Conflict: MIKE (A-gap mug low-hole robber) & 3T (interior penetrator)
    - Why It Works: Offensive quarterbacks are coached to throw hot slants against A-gap pressure, throwing the football directly to the low-hole defender who baited the throw.
    - Failure Mode / Defensive Counter: A double-move route (whip/pivot or slant-and-go) that breaks back outside away from the inside low-hole linebacker.

    [SEQUENCING & GAME-PLAN LOGIC]
    - Sets Up: ryans-overload-edge-fire
    - Plays Off: ryans-cover2-palms-read
    - Visual Tell Cue: MIKE mugs the A-gap pre-snap then immediately drops 5 yards into the low hole while corners press and safeties roll into single-high robber

    [TIMELINE COACHING BEATS]
      * [T=0.0s] A-Gap Mug Presentation Pre-Snap: DeMeco Ryans lines up MIKE mugging the A-gap while corners press tight on the perimeter, presenting an aggressive 5-man pressure look in the red zone.
      * [T=0.8s] MIKE Bails to Low Hole, 4-Man Rush Fires: At the snap, MIKE drops into the 5-yard low hole ("Rat in the Hole") while the 4-man defensive line brings ferocious organic pressure led by 3T penetrating inside.
      * [T=1.8s] Slot Slant Choked in Low-Hole Bracket: The QB throws his hot slant to H against what he believed was man-pressure, only for MIKE to wall off the slant lane while NICKEL trails on the outside hip.
      * [T=3.2s] Interior Penetration Finishes the Sack: With the quick throw eliminated, 3T rips past the RG for an unblocked interior sack before the quarterback can scan to his secondary progressions.

>>> PLAY: 5-Man Overload Edge Fire Zone (ID: ryans-overload-edge-fire)
    Personnel: Nickel 4-2-5
    Formation: Overload 5-Up Wide-9 Front vs 11P Gun 3x1 Deep Shot

    [SUMMARY & TACTICAL PURPOSE]

    - Key Defender Put In Conflict: NICKEL (unblocked overload blitzer) & WDE (boundary flat dropper)
    - Why It Works: Offensive slide protections cannot account for both the interior looping linebacker and the perimeter slot DB, ensuring a free rusher to the quarterback.
    - Failure Mode / Defensive Counter: A quick screen to the boundary side if the dropping defensive end fails to get sufficient width to make the tackle.

      * [T=2.0s] Pass Protection Overwhelmed on Field Edge: The running back steps up to pick WILL’s blitz, leaving NICKEL completely unblocked to scream off the field perimeter.
      * [T=3.0s] Strip-Sack Fumble Forced: NICKEL levels the quarterback from the blind side just as he prepares to throw, knocking the football free for a game-changing turnover.

SCHEME FAMILY: CHRIS SHULA'S MATCH QUARTERS & PENNY FRONT SHELL [ID: shula-match-quarters]
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Architect / Coach: Chris Shula
Organization / Team: Los Angeles Rams
Category: DEFENSE
Tree Branch: fangio-two-high
Core Philosophy: A Fangio-lineage two-high quarters system refined for the modern spread era. Chris Shula employs light Tite (4i-0-4i) and Penny (5-1-5) fronts to maintain interior gap integrity with fewer bodies in the box, while presenting a perpetual two-safety shell that disguises Cover 6, Cover 8, and split-field quarters match calls. Creeper blitzes — defenders who simulate pressure but drop into coverage — are the signature deception weapon that renders pre-snap hot-read systems unreliable.

PLAYS IN THIS SCHEME:

>>> PLAY: Tite Front B-Gap Pinch with Match Quarters (ID: shula-tite-b-gap-pinch)
    Personnel: Penny 5-1-5
    Formation: 3-4 Tite Front (4i - 0 - 4i) vs 11P Condensed 2x2
    Situation: 1st & 10, +45, base down run/pass balance
    Defensive Look: Cover 4 Match (Quarters Mod / Sky Safety Support) (3-4 Tite Pinch Front (404 Alignment))
    Animation Duration: 4s
    Direct URL: https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=shula-match-quarters&play=shula-tite-b-gap-pinch

    [SUMMARY & TACTICAL PURPOSE]
    - Motive: Suffocate inside zone and Duo run concepts with a 3-man Tite front (404 alignment) by pinching the B-gaps, spilling the ball carrier into the waiting arms of unblocked edge defenders and downhill safeties.
    - Key Defender Put In Conflict: 4iL (B-gap pinch tackle) & BS (downhill alley-fitting boundary safety)
    - Why It Works: The 4i alignments prevent offensive tackles from climbing to the second-level linebackers, keeping the box clean while allowing the defense to play two-high pass coverage.
    - Failure Mode / Defensive Counter: Quick perimeter Pin-and-Pull or Outside Zone sweep runs that reach the edge before the stand-up linebackers can set the perimeter.

    [SEQUENCING & GAME-PLAN LOGIC]
    - Sets Up: shula-penny-bracket-bunch, shula-boundary-creeper-drop7
    - Plays Off: None
    - Visual Tell Cue: 3-4 Tite front where both 4i interior linemen slant hard into the B-gaps spilling run action to perimeter OLBs and downhill safeties

    [TIMELINE COACHING BEATS]
      * [T=0.0s] Tite Front (404 Alignment) Pre-Snap: Chris Shula aligns in the modern 3-4 Tite front: two 4i-technique defensive tackles over the inside shoulders of the offensive tackles, a 0-tech Nose, and two stand-up edge linebackers in a two-high Quarters shell.
      * [T=0.8s] Double B-Gap Pinch Clamps Inside Run: At the snap, both 4i tackles slant violently inside into the B-gaps while the Nose controls both A-gaps. The interior run lanes are instantly choked off.
      * [T=1.8s] Run Spilled Horizontally to Unblocked LOLB: With no interior crease available, the running back is forced to bounce wide to the weak C-gap, running directly into the unblocked LOLB setting the edge.
      * [T=3.0s] Boundary Safety Fills Alley for Decisive TFL: Triggering on run action from the two-high shell, Boundary Safety (BS) sprints downhill to clean up the tackle for a 3-yard loss in the backfield.

>>> PLAY: Penny 5-1-5 Bracket Coverage vs Condensed Bunch (ID: shula-penny-bracket-bunch)
    Personnel: Penny 5-1-5
    Formation: Penny 5-1-5 Front vs 11P Gun 3x1 Condensed Bunch
    Situation: 3rd & 6, +35, McVay/Shanahan condensed bunch passing down
    Defensive Look: Box / Triangle Bracket Match vs 3x1 Bunch (Penny 5-1-5 Front (5 on line, 1 ILB, 5 DBs))
    Animation Duration: 4s
    Direct URL: https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=shula-match-quarters&play=shula-penny-bracket-bunch

    [SUMMARY & TACTICAL PURPOSE]
    - Motive: Eliminate natural pick and rub routes from condensed bunch sets by employing a 3-over-2 Triangle Bracket match coverage while retaining a disciplined 4-man Penny rush.
    - Key Defender Put In Conflict: STAR (inside bracket DB) & FS (top cap safety)
    - Why It Works: Offenses use condensed bunches to create free releases against man coverage. Triangle matching plays zone distribution based on route directions (in, out, up), eliminating picks entirely.
    - Failure Mode / Defensive Counter: A deep scissors or post-corner combination by the bunch if the safety hesitates between two vertical stems.

    [SEQUENCING & GAME-PLAN LOGIC]
    - Sets Up: shula-cover8-field-quarter
    - Plays Off: shula-tite-b-gap-pinch
    - Visual Tell Cue: Penny 5-1-5 front with STAR, corner, and safety forming a tight triangle bracket over the condensed bunch to exchange routes in-and-out

    [TIMELINE COACHING BEATS]
      * [T=0.0s] Penny 5-1-5 Front & Triangle Bracket Pre-Snap: Chris Shula deploys a 5-man Penny front with a 3-over-2 "Box/Triangle" bracket over the condensed 3x1 bunch, featuring STAR (inside), RCB (outside), and FS (top).
      * [T=0.8s] Triangle Rules Distribute Bunch Releases: As the bunch releases, the defense seamlessly sorts the routes without getting picked: RCB jumps the flat (Y), STAR clamps the shallow in-cut (H), and FS caps the vertical wheel (Z).
      * [T=2.0s] Natural Rubs Neutralized; All Windows Clamped: The offense’s designed pick-plays are completely countered by zone distribution rules. The QB is forced to hold the ball as all three bunch receivers are suffocated.
      * [T=3.5s] 4-Man Penny Front Sacks QB: With nowhere to deliver the football, 4iR breaks free from the interior rush to combine with LOLB for the third-down coverage sack.

>>> PLAY: Split-Field Cover 8 (Quarter-Quarter-Half) (ID: shula-cover8-field-quarter)
    Personnel: Penny 5-1-5
    Formation: Penny 5-1-5 Front vs 11P Gun 2x2 Boundary Out
    Situation: 2nd & 8, +28, open field passing down
    Defensive Look: Cover 8 (Field Quarters Match / Boundary Half Trap) (Penny 5-1-5 Front (Quarter-Quarter-Half Shell))
    Animation Duration: 4s
    Direct URL: https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=shula-match-quarters&play=shula-cover8-field-quarter

    [SUMMARY & TACTICAL PURPOSE]
    - Motive: Exploit tendencies against two-high shells by splitting the field coverage: playing Quarters match to the multi-receiver field side and a hard Cover 2 trap to the boundary to intercept quick out-routes.
    - Key Defender Put In Conflict: LCB (Boundary trap corner) & BS (Boundary deep half safety)
    - Why It Works: Quarterbacks read the pre-snap two-high look and target the boundary receiver on quick outs, unaware that the boundary corner is squatting in Cover 2 while the safety provides deep-half over-the-top support.
    - Failure Mode / Defensive Counter: A double-move (out-and-up) by the boundary receiver if the safety is late getting to deep-half depth.

    [SEQUENCING & GAME-PLAN LOGIC]
    - Sets Up: shula-boundary-creeper-drop7
    - Plays Off: shula-penny-bracket-bunch
    - Visual Tell Cue: Two-high pre-snap shell where boundary corner squats in hard flat while boundary safety rolls over top into deep half

    [TIMELINE COACHING BEATS]
      * [T=0.0s] Two-High Shell Disguise Pre-Snap: Chris Shula presents a balanced two-high safety shell. The offense expects standard Quarters (Cover 4) coverage across the entire field.
      * [T=0.8s] Split-Field Rotation: Cover 8 Structure: At the snap, Shula runs Cover 8 (Quarter-Quarter-Half): Field side (RCB & FS) plays Match Quarters, while Boundary side rotates to Cover 2 with LCB squatting and BS rolling to deep half.
      * [T=1.8s] Boundary Corner Trap Triggered: The QB throws the quick boundary out to X, expecting the soft off-coverage of Quarters, only to find LCB squatting directly in the flat and stepping in front of the throw.
      * [T=2.6s] Interception & Pick-Six Down the Sideline: LCB secures the interception in full stride, taking it all the way down the boundary sideline for a defensive touchdown.

>>> PLAY: Boundary Creeper with Drop-7 Quarter Coverage Shell (ID: shula-boundary-creeper-drop7)
    Personnel: Penny 5-1-5
    Formation: Penny 5-1-5 vs 11P Gun 3x1 Boundary Trips
    Situation: 3rd & 7, +35, passing down conversion
    Defensive Look: Drop 7 — Cover 3 Match with Simulated Edge Creeper (Penny 5-1-5 Front (3-1-7 Drop))
    Animation Duration: 4s
    Direct URL: https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=shula-match-quarters&play=shula-boundary-creeper-drop7

    [SUMMARY & TACTICAL PURPOSE]
    - Motive: Drop 7 defenders into multi-layered zone coverage by disguising a pass rusher as a creeper, then rushing only 3 linemen while flooding all throwing windows.
    - Key Defender Put In Conflict: Left OLB Creeper (Pre-snap Rush Alignment, Post-snap Drop)
    - Why It Works: The LOLB creeper fools the QB's hot-read expectations — the QB expects a 5-man pressure but gets only 3 rushers and 7 coverage defenders. Every intermediate route is bracketed by quarters match rules, leaving only a short check-down under the first-down marker.
    - Failure Mode / Defensive Counter: A mobile QB who scrambles away from the pocket, or a TE on a crossing route that forces the MIKE linebacker out of position before the FS can provide over-the-top help.

    [SEQUENCING & GAME-PLAN LOGIC]
    - Sets Up: None
    - Plays Off: shula-tite-b-gap-pinch, shula-penny-bracket-bunch
    - Visual Tell Cue: LOLB walks up to line in edge rush stance before snap — this is the creeper tell; if he drops, expect a 3-man rush with 7 in coverage.

    [TIMELINE COACHING BEATS]
      * [T=0.7s] 1. LOLB Creeper Disguise: The left outside linebacker aligns in a two-point pass rush stance on the boundary edge, baiting the offensive tackle into a set position. At the snap, he drops into flat zone coverage — creating an extra dropper that confuses the QB's hot-read system.
      * [T=1.5s] 2. 3-Man Rush, 7-Man Drop: Only three linemen rush (4iL, NOSE, 4iR) while 7 defenders drop into deep coverage zones. The defense sacrifices immediate pressure for a coverage umbrella that has no throwing windows anywhere on the field.
      * [T=2.5s] 3. TE Cross Split Zone Read: The TE attempts to split the MIKE and STAR zones on a 10-yard cross. Shula's quarters shell activates zone replacement rules — MIKE sinks with TE, FS rotates over-the-top as a second layer of help, and STAR holds H's hook in quarters match.
      * [T=3.5s] 4. QB Pressured, Check-Down: With 7 defenders in coverage and all primary targets bracketed or covered, the QB is flushed from the pocket. The only outlet is a short RB check-down — Shula's Drop-7 design forces exactly this outcome: a minimal gain on 3rd-and-7.

SCHEME FAMILY: STEVE SPAGNUOLO EXOTIC BLITZ & SIM PRESSURES [ID: spagnuolo-exotic-blitz]
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Architect / Coach: Steve Spagnuolo
Organization / Team: Kansas City Chiefs
Category: DEFENSE
Tree Branch: reid-west-coast
Core Philosophy: Steve Spagnuolo’s championship-winning defensive scheme: aggressive situational blitzing, boundary corner overloads, 4-man creeper simulated pressures dropping interior linemen, 7-man Cover 0 house heat, and disguised inverted split-safety coverages that break standard quarterback protection reads.

PLAYS IN THIS SCHEME:

>>> PLAY: Boundary Corner Blitz (Spags Heat) (ID: spagnuolo-corndog-corner-blitz)
    Personnel: Nickel 4-2-5
    Formation: Nickel Over vs 11P Gun Trips Right
    Situation: 3rd & 6, +38, high-leverage pressure down
    Defensive Look: Cover 2 Invert Roll (Disguised 2-High) (Over Front Slant-Strong)
    Animation Duration: 4s
    Direct URL: https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=spagnuolo-exotic-blitz&play=spagnuolo-corndog-corner-blitz

    [SUMMARY & TACTICAL PURPOSE]
    - Motive: Manufacture an unblockable blindside corner blitz by manipulating offensive protection with an interior DE stunt while rotating the free safety into the vacated flat.
    - Key Defender Put In Conflict: LCB (Boundary Corner Blitz) & FS (Flat Replacement Safety)
    - Why It Works: The offensive tackle is forced to honor the interior B-gap spike by WDE, leaving no eligible blocker to pick up the blitzing boundary cornerback.
    - Failure Mode / Defensive Counter: A quick pre-snap smoke screen or boundary tunnel screen that hits before the free safety can rotate down from 12 yards depth.

    [SEQUENCING & GAME-PLAN LOGIC]
    - Sets Up: spagnuolo-cover0-max-heat
    - Plays Off: spagnuolo-split-safety-invert2
    - Visual Tell Cue: LCB shows press alignment with no safety help over the top, then sprints downhill at snap while FS rotates down

    [TIMELINE COACHING BEATS]
      * [T=0.0s] Two-High Disguise & Press Bluff: Steve Spagnuolo presents a standard 2-high shell with boundary corner LCB pressed tight on isolated receiver X, enticing the offense to set half-slide protection right toward the Trips overload.
      * [T=0.6s] The Crash & Corner Launch: At the snap, WDE aggressively slants inside into the B-gap, pulling the LT down with him. LCB sprints off the perimeter with a free runway directly to the quarterback’s blindside.
      * [T=1.8s] Safety Downhill Rotation Erases Hot Read: The QB looks to punish the vacated corner with a quick hitch/out to X, but Free Safety (FS) is already screaming downhill into the flat window to erase the throw.
      * [T=2.4s] Blindside Strip-Sack Arrival: With the hot window replaced and the blindside tackle pinned inside by the defensive end stunt, LCB crushes the QB before the third step is complete.

>>> PLAY: Cross-Dog Creeper Sim Pressure (ID: spagnuolo-cross-creeper-drop)
    Personnel: Nickel 4-2-5
    Formation: Nickel Odd Over vs 11P Gun 2x2 Spread
    Situation: 2nd & 8, +42, passing situation
    Defensive Look: Cover 3 Match (Simulated 4-Man Creeper) (Odd Mug Sim Overload)
    Animation Duration: 4s
    Direct URL: https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=spagnuolo-exotic-blitz&play=spagnuolo-cross-creeper-drop

    [SUMMARY & TACTICAL PURPOSE]
    - Motive: Generate unblocked pressure with a 4-man simulated rush by replacing a dropping defensive end with a blitzing linebacker into the offense’s slide protection.
    - Key Defender Put In Conflict: WILL (Creeper Linebacker Rusher) & WDE (Dropping Defensive End)
    - Why It Works: The offensive line slides protection to the defensive end who bails, while failing to account for the linebacker shooting the opposite B-gap from second-level depth.
    - Failure Mode / Defensive Counter: A designed perimeter quarterback rollout away from the creeper rush that isolates cornerbacks in man/zone match without edge contain.

    [SEQUENCING & GAME-PLAN LOGIC]
    - Sets Up: spagnuolo-cover0-max-heat
    - Plays Off: spagnuolo-split-safety-invert2
    - Visual Tell Cue: Defensive end steps back into hook drop at snap while off-ball linebacker triggers forward into B-gap

    [TIMELINE COACHING BEATS]
      * [T=0.0s] Mug Front Sim Pressure Alignment: Spagnuolo presents a 5-man line of scrimmage front with MIKE mugged in the A-gap, signaling an all-out pass rush to force 5-man slide protection.
      * [T=0.8s] The Creeper Exchange: At the snap, only 4 defenders rush! Defensive end WDE drops into the shallow hook zone while inside linebacker WILL shoots the strong B-gap on a creeper blitz.
      * [T=2.0s] Hot Window Clogged by Defensive End: The QB expects the blitz and looks to hit H on the shallow crossing hot route, only to find the 260-pound WDE standing directly in the throwing window.
      * [T=3.2s] Unblocked Creeper Sacks Quarterback: With his primary hot route taken away by the dropping defensive lineman, the QB is brought down by WILL blazing through the vacated B-gap.

>>> PLAY: Cover 0 Max All-Out Blitz (ID: spagnuolo-cover0-max-heat)
    Personnel: Nickel 4-2-5
    Formation: 7-Up Zero Mug vs 11P Gun Trips Left
    Situation: 3rd & 11, +45, must-have conversion down
    Defensive Look: Cover 0 Pure Man (Zero Deep Safeties) (7-Man Diamond Pressure Front)
    Animation Duration: 3.5s
    Direct URL: https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=spagnuolo-exotic-blitz&play=spagnuolo-cover0-max-heat

    [SUMMARY & TACTICAL PURPOSE]
    - Motive: Overwhelm 5- and 6-man pass protections on critical 3rd & long downs by sending 7 rushers while playing tight press-man coverage without safety help.
    - Key Defender Put In Conflict: SS (Unblocked 7th Edge Rusher) & FS (Press-Man DB on Slot H)
    - Why It Works: Offensive math guarantees at least 1 free rusher against 6-man protections, arriving at the QB before any route beyond 3 yards can develop.
    - Failure Mode / Defensive Counter: A missed tackle on a quick boundary hitch/fade or an elusive QB breaking the first tackle into a completely vacant secondary.

    [SEQUENCING & GAME-PLAN LOGIC]
    - Sets Up: spagnuolo-split-safety-invert2
    - Plays Off: spagnuolo-corndog-corner-blitz, spagnuolo-cross-creeper-drop
    - Visual Tell Cue: All 7 front defenders rush at snap with DBs pressing at 1 yard depth and no safety retreating deep

    [TIMELINE COACHING BEATS]
      * [T=0.0s] 7-Up Diamond Alignment (No Deep Safety): Spagnuolo crowds the line with 7 potential rushers and zero deep safeties, forcing a pure 1-on-1 man match across the field and demanding an immediate hot throw from the QB.
      * [T=0.6s] All 7 Rushers Ignite Simultaneously: Every defender at the line rushes! With the offensive line and RB only able to account for 6 blockers, Strong Safety (SS) bursts completely unblocked off the edge.
      * [T=1.5s] Man-Press Suffocates All Hot Routes: The QB looks to release the ball instantly on a quick slant, but FS and RCB have aggressive inside press-man positioning, giving the receivers zero immediate separation.
      * [T=2.2s] Violent QB Collapse & Incompletion: SS and WILL crush into the quarterback in under 1.6 seconds, forcing a fluttering, off-balance throw that hits the dirt harmlessly.

>>> PLAY: Split-Safety Invert Cover 2 Trap (ID: spagnuolo-split-safety-invert2)
    Personnel: Nickel 4-2-5
    Formation: Disguised Single-High vs 11P Gun 2x2
    Situation: 2nd & 7, +30, red zone / four-down territory
    Defensive Look: Cover 2 Invert (Corners Deep Half, Safeties Underneath) (Even 4-Man Under Front)
    Animation Duration: 4s
    Direct URL: https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=spagnuolo-exotic-blitz&play=spagnuolo-split-safety-invert2

    [SUMMARY & TACTICAL PURPOSE]
    - Motive: Deceive the quarterback by disguising a two-deep shell as single-high, inverting cornerbacks into deep halves while safeties trigger downhill to trap intermediate seams and out routes.
    - Key Defender Put In Conflict: FS (Downhill Invert Safety) & LCB (Deep-Half Sinking Corner)
    - Why It Works: Quarterbacks read the cornerback bailing deep and assume Cover 3, missing the safety driving downhill from 12 yards depth directly into the passing lane.
    - Failure Mode / Defensive Counter: A deep post route between the sinking cornerbacks that exploits the vacant middle of the field if the safety triggers too aggressively downhill.

    [SEQUENCING & GAME-PLAN LOGIC]
    - Sets Up: spagnuolo-corndog-corner-blitz, spagnuolo-cross-creeper-drop
    - Plays Off: None
    - Visual Tell Cue: Corners sprint backwards into deep halves at snap while both safeties drive downhill into underneath curl/flat zones

    [TIMELINE COACHING BEATS]
      * [T=0.0s] Single-High Disguise Alignment: Steve Spagnuolo shows a classic single-high Cover 1/3 look before the snap, encouraging the quarterback to work the weak slot out/seam route against presumed off coverage.
      * [T=0.8s] The Invert Rotation: At the snap, both cornerbacks bail aggressively to deep halves, while Free Safety (FS) screams downhill into the weak intermediate flat to spring the trap.
      * [T=2.0s] The Trap Sprung (Interception): The QB throws to H expecting a soft Cover 3 flat void, but FS steps directly in front of the pass with downhill momentum for the interception.
      * [T=3.2s] Pick-Six Return Underway: With both outside cornerbacks already capping the deep boundaries, FS takes the turnover down the sideline for a game-changing score.

SCHEME FAMILY: DAN QUINN COVER 3 PRESS-BAIL & UNDER FRONT [ID: quinn-cover3-press]
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Architect / Coach: Dan Quinn
Organization / Team: Washington Commanders / Seattle Seahawks
Category: DEFENSE
Tree Branch: carroll-saleh-wide9
Core Philosophy: Dan Quinn’s definitive single-high defensive system: physical press-bail cornerback mechanics, 4-3 Under front overloads generating organic 4-man speed rush with the LEO defensive end, Cover 1 Rat-in-the-Hole lurking underneath crossers, and lethal safety Sky fire zone pressures.

PLAYS IN THIS SCHEME:

>>> PLAY: Cover 3 Press-Bail (Legion Foundation) (ID: quinn-cover3-press-bail)

    - Why It Works: Press-bail eliminates quick boundary throws without conceding deep vertical separation, buying time for the 4-man defensive line rush to collapse the pocket.
    - Failure Mode / Defensive Counter: Four verticals concepts attacking both seams simultaneously if the single-high free safety gets held by an eye-manipulating quarterback.

      * [T=0.8s] Press-Bail Transition & Sky Rotation: At the snap, both cornerbacks use disciplined side-saddle press-bail footwork to glide into deep thirds, while Strong Safety (SS) inserts aggressively downhill into the strong flat (Sky force).
      * [T=2.2s] Deep Thirds Capped, Windows Clamped: The QB wants to take a deep vertical shot vs press, but LCB and FS completely cap the boundary Go and field Post routes with zero daylight.
      * [T=3.2s] LEO Strip-Sack from Blindside: With all initial passing concepts locked down by the 7-man coverage shell, the unassisted 4-man rush arrives as LEO rips past the left tackle to strip the football.

>>> PLAY: Cover 1 Rat-in-the-Hole (Lurk Crosser) (ID: quinn-cover1-rat-in-hole)

SCHEME FAMILY: TODD BOWLES CREEPER BLITZ & PSYCHO FRONT [ID: bowles-creeper-blitz]
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Architect / Coach: Todd Bowles
Organization / Team: Tampa Bay Buccaneers
Category: DEFENSE
Tree Branch: belichick-flores
Core Philosophy: Todd Bowles’ fearsome defensive scheme: Dual A-gap cross-dog interior stunts, boundary corner overloads attacking pass protection slides, Drop-8 Tampa 2 traps with the middle linebacker running the deep pole, and 4-man simulated pressures with edge peel rules.

PLAYS IN THIS SCHEME:

>>> PLAY: Dual A-Gap Cross-Dog Blitz (ID: bowles-dual-a-gap-cross-blitz)
    Personnel: Base 3-4 / Nickel 2-4-5
    Formation: Double-A Mug 6-Up vs 11P Gun 2x2
    Situation: 3rd & 7, +40, high-leverage money down
    Defensive Look: Cover 1 Man-Free (Cross-Dog Heat) (Double-A Gap Cross-Dog Stunt)
    Animation Duration: 3.8s
    Direct URL: https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=bowles-creeper-blitz&play=bowles-dual-a-gap-cross-blitz

    [SUMMARY & TACTICAL PURPOSE]
    - Motive: Create immediate interior pressure against slide protections by sending a two-man A-gap cross-dog stunt where the first linebacker picks the center and the second loops untouched to the quarterback.
    - Key Defender Put In Conflict: WILL (Looping A-Gap Blitzer) & MIKE (Penetrating Center Picker)
    - Why It Works: Offensive linemen cannot pass off interior stunt crosses in tight A-gap spacing, and running backs struggle to adjust to looping rush tracks.
    - Failure Mode / Defensive Counter: A quick slip screen or tunnel screen that catches the interior rushers vacating the second level.

    [SEQUENCING & GAME-PLAN LOGIC]
    - Sets Up: bowles-peel-zone-sim-pressure
    - Plays Off: bowles-drop8-tampa2-lurk
    - Visual Tell Cue: Both inside linebackers mug A-gaps at snap, with MIKE charging first and WILL crossing behind his back into opposite gap

    [TIMELINE COACHING BEATS]
      * [T=0.0s] Double-A Mug 6-Up Presentation: Todd Bowles mugs both inside linebackers (MIKE and WILL) directly into the A-gaps, forcing the offensive line into a man-to-man 5-0 protection check.
      * [T=0.6s] The Cross-Dog Exchange: At the snap, MIKE slams into the left shoulder of the Center to occupy him, while WILL executes a delayed cross-loop behind him into the opposite A-gap.
      * [T=1.6s] The Running Back Whiffs, Gap Opens: The running back expects a direct blitz and is caught off-guard by the looping angle of WILL, leaving the A-gap wide open as WILL accelerates into the backfield.
      * [T=2.2s] Interior Sack in Under 2.2 Seconds: WILL buries the quarterback before he can hit his hot slant against tight press-man coverage, delivering a vintage Todd Bowles drive-ending sack.

>>> PLAY: Boundary Overload Fire Blitz (ID: bowles-overload-boundary-fire)

      * [T=1.8s] Safety Replaces the Void: Free Safety (FS) screams downhill from two-high depth into the boundary flat, taking away the quarterback’s immediate hot answer to X.
      * [T=2.2s] Violent Blindside Turnover: LCB drills the quarterback from behind at full speed, knocking the ball loose for a drive-ending strip-sack.

>>> PLAY: Drop-8 Tampa 2 Middle Lurk Trap (ID: bowles-drop8-tampa2-lurk)

      * [T=0.8s] The Great Drop-8 Retreat: At the snap, only 3 rushers engage! Four front defenders instantly bail backwards into coverage, while MIKE sprints full-speed down the deep middle pole (Tampa 2).
      * [T=2.0s] Hot Read Baited into Turnover: The QB throws his designated hot seam to Y expecting an empty middle, only to find the sprinting MIKE linebacker undercutting the ball for an interception.
      * [T=3.2s] Escorted Return Downfield: With 8 defensive backs and linebackers already deployed across the field, MIKE is escorted by a wall of blockers on a huge turnover return.
