--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
SCHEME FAMILY: DON CORYELL'S AIR CORYELL VERTICAL FAMILY [ID: coryell-vertical]
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Architect / Coach: Don Coryell
Organization / Team: San Diego Chargers (1978-86)
Category: OFFENSE
Tree Branch: coryell-vertical
Core Philosophy: The original vertical passing tree. Coryell stretched defenses with five-step drops, seam-post strokes, and layered deep crossers, forcing single-high safeties to defend the whole field while tight ends occupied the middle hole. Every modern timing-based passing game descends from these four calls.

PLAYS IN THIS SCHEME:

>>> PLAY: Seam-Post Double Stroke (ID: coryell-seam-post-double-stroke)
    Personnel: 11
    Formation: One-Back Pro, Slot Left
    Situation: 1st & 10, midfield, base down
    Defensive Look: Cover 3 Buzz (4-3 Over front)
    Animation Duration: 4s
    Direct URL: https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=coryell-vertical&play=coryell-seam-post-double-stroke

    [SUMMARY & TACTICAL PURPOSE]
    - Motive: Attack the deep middle with two synchronized seam-post strokes that force the single-high safety to pick a side.
    - Key Defender Put In Conflict: Free Safety (middle-third defender)
    - Why It Works: Identical outside stems freeze both corners on the fake fades, and the TE middle-hole stretch removes any underneath help, isolating the free safety between two posts.
    - Failure Mode / Defensive Counter: Corners sit on the stems instead of bailing, or the safety splits the double post with depth and takes away both throws.

    [SEQUENCING & GAME-PLAN LOGIC]
    - Sets Up: coryell-deep-out-comeback, coryell-cross-country-drag
    - Plays Off: None
    - Visual Tell Cue: Both outside receivers take identical vertical stems before breaking — the stroke only happens after the stems have sold pure fades.

    [TIMELINE COACHING BEATS]
      * [T=0.6s] 1. The Five-Step Drop and Outside Stems: The quarterback takes his full five-step Coryell drop while both outside receivers hammer hard outside stems, convincing soft-bailing corners that fades are coming.
      * [T=1.5s] 2. The Double Stroke: At twelve yards both receivers stroke inside off their stems simultaneously. Both corners are still leaning on the fake fades, leaving the seams open behind them.
      * [T=2.4s] 3. The Middle Hole Stretch: The TE climbs to fourteen and settles in the middle hole while the slot pressures the weak seam, forcing the free safety to defend three deep threats alone.
      * [T=3.2s] 4. The Frazee Shot Delivery: The quarterback throws the seam-post away from the safety's lever. Whichever post he chooses, the backside post runs free down the middle of the field.

>>> PLAY: Deep Out & Comeback (ID: coryell-deep-out-comeback)
    Personnel: 11
    Formation: Pro Set, Strong Left
    Situation: 2nd & 6, +35, vs press coverage
    Defensive Look: Cover 1 Robber (4-3 Under front)
    Animation Duration: 4.2s
    Direct URL: https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=coryell-vertical&play=coryell-deep-out-comeback

    [SUMMARY & TACTICAL PURPOSE]
    - Motive: Force a press corner to defend two throws at one landmark: the 18-yard deep out first, then the 16-yard comeback.
    - Key Defender Put In Conflict: Right Corner (press corner on the flanker)
    - Why It Works: The deep out forces the corner to open and sprint; once he commits to erasing the out, the comeback breaks back into space he has vacated.
    - Failure Mode / Defensive Counter: The corner plays trail technique with inside help over the top, or the free safety refuses to commit to the deep-out bracket.

    [SEQUENCING & GAME-PLAN LOGIC]
    - Sets Up: coryell-seam-post-double-stroke
    - Plays Off: coryell-z-snap-move-screen
    - Visual Tell Cue: The flanker runs a pure vertical stem past twelve yards before any break — the throw is always late-breaking at the top of the route.

    [TIMELINE COACHING BEATS]
      * [T=0.7s] 1. Press Release Battles: Both corners are pressed to the receivers' chests because there is no help over the top. The flanker fights for an outside stack while the split end grinds out an inside release.
      * [T=1.8s] 2. The Deep-Out Window Opens: The quarterback hits his fifth step and looks at the 18-yard deep out. The corner is still in phase, but the receiver has leverage — this is the primary read if it stays open.
      * [T=2.6s] 3. The Progression Flip: The corner sits on the out-break and closes the window. The quarterback hitches and flips his eyes to the backside comeback, where X has stacked his press corner.
      * [T=3.6s] 4. The Comeback Completion: X snaps down at sixteen while the free safety is committed to the deep-out help. The comeback is thrown where only X can catch it along the boundary.

>>> PLAY: Cross-Country Drag Series (ID: coryell-cross-country-drag)
    Personnel: 11
    Formation: One-Back Pro, Twins Right
    Situation: 2nd & 8, own 40, base down
    Defensive Look: Cover 3 Sky (4-3 Over front)
    Animation Duration: 4.2s
    Direct URL: https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=coryell-vertical&play=coryell-cross-country-drag

    [SUMMARY & TACTICAL PURPOSE]
    - Motive: Flood the middle of the field with two staggered deep crossers so zone drops cannot cover both layers.
    - Key Defender Put In Conflict: Mike Linebacker (middle hook drop)
    - Why It Works: Vertical stems remove the corners and hooks first; the crossers then arrive offset in time and depth, so whichever defender takes layer one abandons layer two.
    - Failure Mode / Defensive Counter: The Mike sits in the middle hole without chasing either crosser, or man coverage lets defenders trade the crossers cleanly at the mesh point.

    [SEQUENCING & GAME-PLAN LOGIC]
    - Sets Up: coryell-z-snap-move-screen
    - Plays Off: coryell-seam-post-double-stroke
    - Visual Tell Cue: Both inside receivers release instantly vertical and only break after passing twelve yards — shallow drags never appear in this series.

    [TIMELINE COACHING BEATS]
      * [T=0.8s] 1. The Vertical Stems Set the Table: The slot and flanker fire pure vertical releases, pinning the corners deep and forcing both hooks to turn their backs to the middle before any crossing route shows.
      * [T=1.9s] 2. Layer One Departs: At twenty yards the split end breaks off his stem into the deep cross-country lane. The free safety must now honor the deepest threat in his middle third.
      * [T=2.8s] 3. Layer Two Crosses Underneath: Four yards deeper and four seconds later, the tight end drives his fourteen-yard crosser directly beneath the first. The Mike is caught between layers.
      * [T=3.6s] 4. The Distribution Throw: With the free safety committed to the deep crosser and the Mike dragged to the boundary, the second crosser runs free across the middle for an easy completion.

>>> PLAY: Z-Snap Move Screen (ID: coryell-z-snap-move-screen)
    Personnel: 11
    Formation: One-Back Pro, Strong Right
    Situation: 3rd & 4, +42, expecting pressure
    Defensive Look: Cover 2 Zone (4-3 Over front)
    Animation Duration: 3.6s
    Direct URL: https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=coryell-vertical&play=coryell-z-snap-move-screen

    [SUMMARY & TACTICAL PURPOSE]
    - Motive: Punish Cover 2 flat defenders who sit on the short routes created by the vertical passing game.
    - Key Defender Put In Conflict: Sam Linebacker (strong-flat defender)
    - Why It Works: The snap move steals the corner's leverage and the pump freeze delays the flat defender exactly long enough for the wall to form in front of the catch.
    - Failure Mode / Defensive Counter: The flat trigger fires immediately on the guard release and meets the receiver at the catch point before any wall can form.

    [SEQUENCING & GAME-PLAN LOGIC]
    - Sets Up: coryell-seam-post-double-stroke
    - Plays Off: coryell-cross-country-drag
    - Visual Tell Cue: Z's alignment move happens before the ball is out of the quarterback's hand — a true vertical shot has no pre-break stem move.

    [TIMELINE COACHING BEATS]
      * [T=0.5s] 1. The Snap Move: The flanker takes a hard two-step inside move that snaps the corner's eyes and leverage down into the route, while the line sells a full pass-protection look.
      * [T=1.1s] 2. The Constraint Releases: With the corner leaning inside, Z snaps back outside for width and the near guards release to build the screen wall. The defense still reads pure dropback.
      * [T=1.8s] 3. The Freeze Pump: The quarterback pumps vertically, freezing the Mike and the deep-half safeties for one critical beat while the wall blockers get their heads on pursuers.
      * [T=2.4s] 4. The Screen Catch and Turn: The screen arrives with Z already facing upfield behind three escorts. The flat defender is stalk-blocked and the corner is recovering from the wrong lever.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
SCHEME FAMILY: BILL WALSH'S CLASSIC WEST COAST OFFENSE [ID: walsh-classic-wco]
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Architect / Coach: Bill Walsh
Organization / Team: San Francisco 49ers (1979-88)
Category: OFFENSE
Tree Branch: shanahan-kubiak
Core Philosophy: The timing-and-leverage passing system that replaced the vertical bomb with surgical rhythm throws designed to run like the sweep. Every call answers a leverage question in under two seconds, and every answer sets up the next question through sequencing.

PLAYS IN THIS SCHEME:

>>> PLAY: Slant-Flat Combo (ID: walsh-slant-flat-combo)
    Personnel: 21
    Formation: Split Backs Pro Right
    Situation: 2nd & 5, own 35, vs off coverage
    Defensive Look: Cover 2 Zone (4-3 Over front)
    Animation Duration: 3.6s
    Direct URL: https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=walsh-classic-wco&play=walsh-slant-flat-combo

    [SUMMARY & TACTICAL PURPOSE]
    - Motive: Turn an off-coverage corner's cushion into free yardage with a timed slant-flat stretch.
    - Key Defender Put In Conflict: Right Corner (Cover 2 flat defender)
    - Why It Works: The flat route forces the corner to choose; whichever way he leans, one receiver occupies him while the other runs into the space he vacated.
    - Failure Mode / Defensive Counter: The corner sits on the slant instead of widening, or press coverage disrupts the timing before the three-step drop can finish.

    [SEQUENCING & GAME-PLAN LOGIC]
    - Sets Up: walsh-curl-flat-flood, walsh-play-action-deep-cross
    - Plays Off: None
    - Visual Tell Cue: The flanker releases flat on his first step and the ball is out within 1.2 seconds — anything slower means the defense triggered correctly.

    [TIMELINE COACHING BEATS]
      * [T=0.5s] 1. The Rhythm Drop: The quarterback takes his three big steps without ever leaving his footwork rhythm. The play is designed to be thrown at the top of the drop no matter what.
      * [T=1.1s] 2. The Leverage Question: The flanker shoots the flat instantly, putting the Cover 2 corner in a bind: widen with the flat or sit on the slant lane. He chooses the flat.
      * [T=1.7s] 3. The Slant Window Opens: As the corner widens, X snaps downfield and drives at the guard's outside hip — exactly where both linebackers are a beat late to close.
      * [T=2.3s] 4. The Catch on the Move: The ball arrives in stride at the top of the drop. X is running north with blockers ahead — the West Coast philosophy made physical: a pass that runs like a run.

>>> PLAY: Sprint Right Option (ID: walsh-sprint-right-option)
    Personnel: 21
    Formation: Pro Set, Strong Right
    Situation: 3rd & 3, own 30, must convert
    Defensive Look: Cover 3 Sky (4-3 Over front)
    Animation Duration: 4.2s
    Direct URL: https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=walsh-classic-wco&play=walsh-sprint-right-option

    [SUMMARY & TACTICAL PURPOSE]
    - Motive: Use the sprint to displace the entire defense horizontally so the primary corner route or the naked flat checkdown comes open.
    - Key Defender Put In Conflict: Sam Linebacker (strong-flat defender)
    - Why It Works: The corner route removes the deep help and the sprint pulls every linebacker away from the line of scrimmage, leaving the flat completely undefended.
    - Failure Mode / Defensive Counter: The flat defender stays home instead of chasing the sprint, closing the checkdown window before the quarterback can set his feet.

    [SEQUENCING & GAME-PLAN LOGIC]
    - Sets Up: walsh-curl-flat-flood
    - Plays Off: walsh-slant-flat-combo
    - Visual Tell Cue: The quarterback leaves the launch point horizontally within half a second — no drop step ever occurs.

    [TIMELINE COACHING BEATS]
      * [T=0.6s] 1. The Sprint Begins: The quarterback takes the snap under center and drives full speed for the right sideline while the line slides with him. The defense's pass rush lanes are instantly misaligned.
      * [T=1.6s] 2. The Corner Route Climbs: Z wins his release and sells pure vertical before snapping to the corner at twelve. The bail corner must turn and run, and the sky safety rotates over the top.
      * [T=2.6s] 3. The Bracket Forms: The corner route is bracketed by the corner and safety — exactly as designed. Both defenders are now staring at Z, and the sprint has dragged every linebacker sideways.
      * [T=3.5s] 4. The Checkdown Escape: With Z consuming two defenders and the linebackers chasing the sprint, the fullback is alone in the flat. The sprinting quarterback sets and delivers the easy completion.

>>> PLAY: Curl-Flat Flood (ID: walsh-curl-flat-flood)
    Personnel: 21
    Formation: Split Backs Strong Right
    Situation: 2nd & 7, own 42, base down
    Defensive Look: Cover 3 Sky (4-3 Over front)
    Animation Duration: 3.8s
    Direct URL: https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=walsh-classic-wco&play=walsh-curl-flat-flood

    [SUMMARY & TACTICAL PURPOSE]
    - Motive: Vertically stretch one flat defender with three routes at three depths until he must give up a leg of the flood.
    - Key Defender Put In Conflict: Right Corner (Cover 3 sky flat dropper)
    - Why It Works: The seam threat removes the hook linebacker and the deep third holds the safety high, leaving the corner alone to cover both an inside breaker and a flat runner.
    - Failure Mode / Defensive Counter: The Sam refuses to carry the TE vertical and walls the curl while the corner takes the flat, erasing all three windows.

    [SEQUENCING & GAME-PLAN LOGIC]
    - Sets Up: walsh-sprint-right-option
    - Plays Off: walsh-slant-flat-combo
    - Visual Tell Cue: All three flood legs release to one side within the first second — a true flood never distributes to both sides.

    [TIMELINE COACHING BEATS]
      * [T=0.7s] 1. The Three-Level Flood Forms: To the right, three receivers attack three depths at once: the TE climbs past fifteen, the flanker works eight at the numbers, and the fullback swings into the flat.
      * [T=1.7s] 2. The Seam Threat Drags the Hook: The TE's vertical stem forces the Sam linebacker to carry him up the seam, vacating the very curl window the flood is designed to hit underneath.
      * [T=2.4s] 3. The High-Low Question: The quarterback reads the sky safety against the curl. The safety stays above the fifteen-yard break, so the curl window is open if the corner does not close it.
      * [T=3.1s] 4. The Corner Loses the Flood: The flat-drop corner sat on Z's inside break, and now the fullback runs free behind him in the flat. The quarterback throws down to the shallowest open leg.

>>> PLAY: Play-Action Deep Cross (ID: walsh-play-action-deep-cross)
    Personnel: 21
    Formation: Split Backs Pro Right
    Situation: 1st & 10, own 30, after a big slant-flat gain
    Defensive Look: Cover 2 Zone (4-3 Over front)
    Animation Duration: 4.2s
    Direct URL: https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=walsh-classic-wco&play=walsh-play-action-deep-cross

    [SUMMARY & TACTICAL PURPOSE]
    - Motive: Exploit the slant-flat success by freezing the second-level defenders with run action and shooting the vacated middle.
    - Key Defender Put In Conflict: Mike Linebacker (run-fit linebacker)
    - Why It Works: Two simultaneous fakes force both linebackers into run fits; the twenty-yard crosser attacks the exact grass they leave when the pass reveals itself.
    - Failure Mode / Defensive Counter: Linebackers play run-pass split discipline and keep their eyes on the receivers, staying attached to the crosser.

    [SEQUENCING & GAME-PLAN LOGIC]
    - Sets Up: walsh-slant-flat-combo
    - Plays Off: walsh-slant-flat-combo
    - Visual Tell Cue: The fullback crosses the line of scrimmage carrying the fake — on the real slant-flat he never leaves the pocket.

    [TIMELINE COACHING BEATS]
      * [T=0.6s] 1. The Bite: The fullback's dive and the halfback's sweep path present two run threats at once. The Mike triggers downhill and the free safety rocks up — the whole shell tilts to the run.
      * [T=1.6s] 2. The Ball Comes Out: The quarterback pulls the ball from the mesh and resets to his drop while the linebackers are still in their run fits with their backs to the routes.
      * [T=2.8s] 3. The Crosser Departs: X breaks inside at twenty yards exactly as the Mike begins his recovery scramble. The post behind him pins both deep-half defenders.
      * [T=3.7s] 4. Behind the Frozen Hooks: The crosser runs free through the space the linebackers occupied during the bite. The throw arrives where only the recovering free safety can contest it.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
SCHEME FAMILY: JUNE JONES'S RUN AND SHOOT [ID: run-and-shoot]
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Architect / Coach: June Jones
Organization / Team: Houston Oilers (1989-93) / Hawaii
Category: OFFENSE
Tree Branch: coryell-vertical
Core Philosophy: Four-wide spread passing built on read routes instead of fixed breaks. Every receiver carries a conversion rule keyed to defender leverage, so the same four calls attack man, zone, and blitz differently. The Oilers' run-and-shoot stretched single-high shells with switch releases, mesh traffic, and perimeter wheels — the direct ancestor of modern spacing-option passing games.

PLAYS IN THIS SCHEME:

>>> PLAY: Switch Verticals vs Man (ID: rns-switch-verticals)
    Personnel: 10
    Formation: Gun One-Back, 4-Wide Spread
    Situation: 2nd & 7, +38, expecting man coverage
    Defensive Look: Cover 1 Robber (Nickel 4-2-5)
    Animation Duration: 4s
    Direct URL: https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=run-and-shoot&play=rns-switch-verticals

    [SUMMARY & TACTICAL PURPOSE]
    - Motive: Force man-coverage defenders into crossed releases that convert into a two-man rub, freeing a vertical behind single-high coverage.
    - Key Defender Put In Conflict: Free Safety (last line in man free)
    - Why It Works: Crossed releases make defenders trail through each other's lanes, and the far-side go routes strip the safety of any help he might offer to the rub side.
    - Failure Mode / Defensive Counter: Corners jam both releases apart before they can cross, or the robber collision-calls the switch and jumps the outside climber.

    [SEQUENCING & GAME-PLAN LOGIC]
    - Sets Up: rns-mesh-read-route, rns-post-wheel-leverage-read
    - Plays Off: None
    - Visual Tell Cue: The releases cross below four yards before either stem develops — a true double-vertical keeps both receivers on parallel outside tracks.

    [TIMELINE COACHING BEATS]
      * [T=0.6s] 1. The Switch Release: X slams an inside release while H bursts outside behind him, exchanging lanes before either stem develops. Both defenders are forced to open in opposite directions.
      * [T=1.6s] 2. Converting to Verticals: Both receivers convert upfield simultaneously. The corner is dragged inside by the slam while the nickel trails through the crossing traffic — a natural rub neither can fight.
      * [T=2.5s] 3. The Single-High Conflict: The right-side go routes pin the free safety and hold the robber. The two left climbers attack the middle hole from opposite shoulders with no help coming.
      * [T=3.3s] 4. The Throw to the Winner: The quarterback delivers to whichever climber wins leverage. The outside release is live because the nickel is trailing — H stacks him and runs free behind the defense.

>>> PLAY: Mesh Read-Route (ID: rns-mesh-read-route)
    Personnel: 10 Empty
    Formation: Gun Empty, Slots Crossed
    Situation: 3rd & 5, +45, must-have down
    Defensive Look: Cover 2 Man Under (4-3 Over front)
    Animation Duration: 4s
    Direct URL: https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=run-and-shoot&play=rns-mesh-read-route

    [SUMMARY & TACTICAL PURPOSE]
    - Motive: Create a natural rub with two shallow crossers and let each receiver convert off the defender's leverage rather than a fixed break point.
    - Key Defender Put In Conflict: Mike Linebacker (middle-hole wall)
    - Why It Works: Crossers force man defenders to exchange or collide through traffic, and the read-route rules guarantee one receiver is always working away from his coverage.
    - Failure Mode / Defensive Counter: Defenders pass off the crossers cleanly pre-snap, or a blitz disrupts the timing before the mesh point develops.

    [SEQUENCING & GAME-PLAN LOGIC]
    - Sets Up: rns-go-route-stab
    - Plays Off: rns-switch-verticals
    - Visual Tell Cue: The crossers never stop until they feel a defender's leverage — a called mesh with set breaks settles at the same spot every snap regardless of coverage.

    [TIMELINE COACHING BEATS]
      * [T=0.6s] 1. The Vertical Stems Sell Out: Both crossers release on pure vertical stems while X and Y push the corners deep, convincing the safeties that this is a four-vertical shot.
      * [T=1.7s] 2. The Mesh Point: The crossers converge at midfield within a yard of each other. Man defenders must either exchange or collide, and the linebackers cannot communicate fast enough.
      * [T=2.6s] 3. Reading the Leverage: The chase-over forces M to settle into the soft hole between the linebacker levels, while Z feels trail leverage and speeds up, climbing away from SAM.
      * [T=3.3s] 4. The Window Throw: The quarterback hits Z climbing up the far seam in front of a free safety whose eyes never left the corner route.

>>> PLAY: Post-Wheel Leverage Read (ID: rns-post-wheel-leverage-read)
    Personnel: 10
    Formation: Gun One-Back, 4-Wide Spread
    Situation: 1st & 10, +35, soft corners showing
    Defensive Look: Cover 3 Sky (4-3 Over front)
    Animation Duration: 4s
    Direct URL: https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=run-and-shoot&play=rns-post-wheel-leverage-read

    [SUMMARY & TACTICAL PURPOSE]
    - Motive: Punish soft bail coverage by selling a post stem and converting into a wheel that attacks the vacated outside third behind the corner's back.
    - Key Defender Put In Conflict: Left Corner (soft bail with eyes on QB)
    - Why It Works: The post stem freezes both the corner and the middle-third safety toward the middle, so the wheel breaks into space no defender is watching.
    - Failure Mode / Defensive Counter: The corner plays with true outside leverage instead of bailing soft, squeezing the wheel against the sideline before it can build speed.

    [SEQUENCING & GAME-PLAN LOGIC]
    - Sets Up: None
    - Plays Off: rns-switch-verticals, rns-go-route-stab
    - Visual Tell Cue: The receiver plants off an inside stem and accelerates away from the numbers — a called post never leaves its diagonal track.

    [TIMELINE COACHING BEATS]
      * [T=0.7s] 1. The Pre-Snap Leverage Read: X aligns and sees a soft-bail corner with eyes for the quarterback rather than a press shadow. The wheel is live before the snap; the post is only the sales pitch.
      * [T=1.5s] 2. The Post Stem Sells the Middle: X pushes an aggressive inside stem that reads like a post, pulling the free safety's attention and confirming the corner's belief that help is not needed outside.
      * [T=2.3s] 3. The Conversion to Wheel: Reading the corner still flat-footed and staring at the QB, X plants off the stem and wheels outside into the void behind the bail.
      * [T=3.2s] 4. The Sideline Shot: The five-step timing arrives exactly as X rounds the wheel. The throw goes over the corner's late turn with the middle-third safety leaning the wrong way.

>>> PLAY: Go-Route Stab Adjustment (ID: rns-go-route-stab)
    Personnel: 10
    Formation: Gun One-Back, 4-Wide Spread
    Situation: 2nd & 6, +42, quarters shell aligned
    Defensive Look: Cover 4 Quarters Bail (4-3 Over front)
    Animation Duration: 4s
    Direct URL: https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=run-and-shoot&play=rns-go-route-stab

    [SUMMARY & TACTICAL PURPOSE]
    - Motive: Use the outside go as bait for a bailing corner and convert the inside stab into a climb that attacks the vacated seam between the coverage levels.
    - Key Defender Put In Conflict: Right Corner (bail technique with back to the slot)
    - Why It Works: The go route empties the entire right third, and the stab-to-climb conversion puts the slot in the one window no quarters defender owns once the corner turns and runs.
    - Failure Mode / Defensive Counter: The corner plays with inside-eye discipline on No. 2 instead of bailing pure, squeezing the converted climb before it reaches the window.

    [SEQUENCING & GAME-PLAN LOGIC]
    - Sets Up: None
    - Plays Off: rns-mesh-read-route, rns-post-wheel-leverage-read
    - Visual Tell Cue: The slot plants at six yards before accelerating — a called seam or vertical never breaks stride below eight.

    [TIMELINE COACHING BEATS]
      * [T=0.7s] 1. The Go-and-Stab Stems: Z releases pure vertical while Y builds toward a six-yard stab plant. The quarters corners bail reading their No. 1 receivers, exactly as the pre-snap look promised.
      * [T=1.5s] 2. The Bail Read Trigger: Y plants his stab and reads the corner: still bailing deep over the top of Z with his back turning. That bail is the trigger — the stab is now dead.
      * [T=2.2s] 3. The Conversion Upfield: Y converts off the plant and climbs into the void behind the bailing corner, working the seam the go route is emptying while the right-quarter safety sinks toward Z.
      * [T=3.2s] 4. The Between-Levels Delivery: The quarterback delivers between the sunk safety and the turned corner. The dig and drag below have stripped every underneath defender from the window.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
SCHEME FAMILY: PAUL JOHNSON'S FLEXBONE TRIPLE OPTION [ID: flexbone-triple-option]
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Architect / Coach: Paul Johnson
Organization / Team: Georgia Tech / Navy
Category: OFFENSE
Tree Branch: option-spread
Core Philosophy: The modern flexbone: two slotbacks in pitch relationships, a fullback on the midline, and a quarterback who reads one unblocked defender per snap. Every call is a math problem — dive, keep, or pitch — and the defense must be right three times to stop it once. Paul Johnson's Georgia Tech and Navy teams turned this into college football's most efficient rushing attack.

PLAYS IN THIS SCHEME:

>>> PLAY: Midline Triple Option (ID: flexbone-midline-triple)
    Personnel: Flexbone Base
    Formation: Flexbone Right, Twin Slots
    Situation: 2nd & 4, own 40, base down
    Defensive Look: Cover 3 Buzz (4-3 Over front)
    Animation Duration: 4.2s
    Direct URL: https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=flexbone-triple-option&play=flexbone-midline-triple

    [SUMMARY & TACTICAL PURPOSE]
    - Motive: Attack the interior read defender with a three-phase conflict — take the dive and lose the keeper, squeeze the keeper and surrender the pitch.
    - Key Defender Put In Conflict: 3-Tech Defensive Tackle (unblocked dive-read key)
    - Why It Works: Any aggressive squeeze by the read key opens the keep lane behind a scoop-and-climb guard, and the arc block forces the end into a pure pitch relationship he cannot win.
    - Failure Mode / Defensive Counter: The read key stays square and two-gaps, or the force corner refuses the pitch trigger and closes on the quarterback instead.

    [SEQUENCING & GAME-PLAN LOGIC]
    - Sets Up: flexbone-inside-veer-triple
    - Plays Off: None
    - Visual Tell Cue: The dive hits the exact midline of the guard-center gap and the quarterback reads an interior defender — veer reads the end instead.

    [TIMELINE COACHING BEATS]
      * [T=0.6s] 1. The Seatbelt Ride: The quarterback reverse-pivots and seats the ball in B's belly at the midline hole while keeping both hands free and eyes locked on the uncovered 3-tech.
      * [T=1.4s] 2. The Squeeze Gives It Away: The 3-tech slants hard down into B's dive path. By taking the dive himself he vacates the keep lane — the ball comes out of B's belly instantly.
      * [T=2.4s] 3. Bend Off the Reach: The quarterback bends behind the tackle's arc block while the end constricts. The guard has scooped the Mike, so the keep lane is two defenders wide and empty.
      * [T=3.4s] 4. The Pitch Phase: With the end forcing width and the corner triggering, the quarterback extends the third phase. A takes the pitch with full momentum around the constriction.

>>> PLAY: Rocket Toss Pitch Series (ID: flexbone-rocket-toss-pitch)
    Personnel: Flexbone Base
    Formation: Flexbone Right, Rocket Motion
    Situation: 1st & 10, own 25, perimeter speed advantage
    Defensive Look: Cover 3 Sky (4-3 Over front)
    Animation Duration: 4.2s
    Direct URL: https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=flexbone-triple-option&play=flexbone-rocket-toss-pitch

    [SUMMARY & TACTICAL PURPOSE]
    - Motive: Attack the perimeter with a full-speed motion back so the pitch arrives at maximum velocity before the defense can reset its force geometry.
    - Key Defender Put In Conflict: Strong Safety (perimeter force player)
    - Why It Works: The motion outruns defensive flow calls, and sequential kick-outs on end, linebacker, and safety force every edge defender outward while the carrier turns north.
    - Failure Mode / Defensive Counter: The force safety squeezes the pitch track instead of taking the kick-out, or the ends spill the blockers and funnel the sweep back inside.

    [SEQUENCING & GAME-PLAN LOGIC]
    - Sets Up: flexbone-midline-triple
    - Plays Off: None
    - Visual Tell Cue: The pitch is extended laterally to a moving back at full speed — option triples hand or ride stationary before reading.

    [TIMELINE COACHING BEATS]
      * [T=0.5s] 1. Rocket Motion at Full Speed: The slot crosses the formation at a dead sprint instead of shimmy-shifting. By the time the defense diagnoses direction he is already even with the tackles.
      * [T=1.2s] 2. The Extended Pitch: The quarterback reverse-pivots and extends the pitch all the way to the edge, handing the ball to H at top gear without breaking his stride.
      * [T=2.2s] 3. Kick-Out Geometry: B kicks the end inside while the guard leads on the linebacker and A climbs to the force safety. Every defender who could squeeze the edge is being blocked outward.
      * [T=3.4s] 4. The Perimeter Edge: With the force player kicked out and both corners stalked, H turns upfield into grass with escorts leading him to the numbers.

>>> PLAY: Inside Veer Triple (ID: flexbone-inside-veer-triple)
    Personnel: Flexbone Base
    Formation: Flexbone Right, Twin Slots
    Situation: 3rd & 3, +45, must-have down
    Defensive Look: Cover 3 Buzz (4-3 Over front)
    Animation Duration: 4.2s
    Direct URL: https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=flexbone-triple-option&play=flexbone-inside-veer-triple

    [SUMMARY & TACTICAL PURPOSE]
    - Motive: Make the playside end choose between the dive and the keep, then punish any third defender who joins with the pitch phase.
    - Key Defender Put In Conflict: Playside Defensive End (unblocked read key)
    - Why It Works: The veer mesh makes the end's crash feel mandatory, and once he commits the geometry guarantees either a free keep lane or an untouched pitch around displaced force.
    - Failure Mode / Defensive Counter: The end squeezes and spilles simultaneously while the force corner stays flat-footed, collapsing all three phases into one gap.

    [SEQUENCING & GAME-PLAN LOGIC]
    - Sets Up: flexbone-midline-play-action-shot
    - Plays Off: flexbone-midline-triple
    - Visual Tell Cue: The dive aims at the B-gap behind the down-blocked tackle and the read is the wide end — midline reads interior and dives at the guard-center seam.

    [TIMELINE COACHING BEATS]
      * [T=0.7s] 1. Ride and Read the End: The quarterback seats the ball on B's hip riding the veer mesh while staring at the playside end — the one defender left unblocked on the entire play.
      * [T=1.4s] 2. The End Crashes Down: The end shoots inside across B's face to make the dive tackle. By taking the dive he hands the quarterback a free pull and an empty C-gap.
      * [T=2.4s] 3. The Pitch Relationship: The keep bends off the down-blocked 3-tech while A mirrors from the perimeter. Their spacing forces every second-level defender to declare before the ball moves.
      * [T=3.5s] 4. Pitch and Perimeter Finish: When the force corner triggers upfield, the pitch goes out. A takes it around the kick-out with the safety and free safety both committed inside.

>>> PLAY: Midline Play-Action Shot (ID: flexbone-midline-play-action-shot)
    Personnel: Flexbone Base
    Formation: Flexbone Right, Twin Slots
    Situation: 2nd & 8, +42, off triple-tendency
    Defensive Look: Cover 3 Buzz (4-3 Over front)
    Animation Duration: 4.4s
    Direct URL: https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=flexbone-triple-option&play=flexbone-midline-play-action-shot

    [SUMMARY & TACTICAL PURPOSE]
    - Motive: Weaponize the triple-option run identity to vacate the deep middle, then attack it with a post shot off an identical midline fake.
    - Key Defender Put In Conflict: Free Safety (middle-third defender)
    - Why It Works: Option teams force safeties to trigger on every mesh; this fake sends both second-level defenders and the buzz safety downhill before the quarterback even looks downfield.
    - Failure Mode / Defensive Counter: The safety plays run-pass split discipline instead of triggering, keeping his shoulders square to the post route developing behind the crosser.

    [SEQUENCING & GAME-PLAN LOGIC]
    - Sets Up: None
    - Plays Off: flexbone-inside-veer-triple
    - Visual Tell Cue: The slot releases upfield instead of running a pitch track, and the tackle arcs then resets to pass set — live option plays never do either.

    [TIMELINE COACHING BEATS]
      * [T=0.8s] 1. Identical Midline Action: Every tell from the midline triple is present: the same reverse pivot, the same seatbelt ride, the guard scooping past his key, and B driving the dive fake into the second level.
      * [T=1.7s] 2. The Safety Trigger: The buzz safety fires downhill on run action while the Mike triggers onto the diving back. Both vacate the middle of the field before the ball is ever thrown.
      * [T=2.7s] 3. Rising Off the Fake: The quarterback sells one more keep stride, then rises off the fake with a clean launch point. The crosser is dragging the free safety's eyes toward the boundary.
      * [T=3.6s] 4. The Post Behind the Frozen Third: Z breaks off his vertical into the post lane behind a middle-third defender who never recovered from the run fit. The shot lands over the trailing corner.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
SCHEME FAMILY: MIKE LEACH'S AIR RAID FAMILY [ID: air-raid]
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Architect / Coach: Mike Leach
Organization / Team: Texas Tech / Washington State / Mississippi State
Category: OFFENSE
Tree Branch: air-raid
Core Philosophy: The purest expression of spread passing: a handful of simple, repeatable concepts thrown from gun at high volume. Every play answers one leverage question, and the quarterback is taught to throw the open receiver rather than force landmarks.

PLAYS IN THIS SCHEME:

>>> PLAY: Mesh Concept (ID: airraid-mesh-concept)
    Personnel: 10
    Formation: 10P Gun 2x2
    Situation: 2nd & 6, own 38, base down
    Defensive Look: Cover 1 Robber (4-3 Over front)
    Animation Duration: 4s
    Direct URL: https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=air-raid&play=airraid-mesh-concept

    [SUMMARY & TACTICAL PURPOSE]
    - Motive: Create guaranteed separation against man coverage through two crossing shallow routes that naturally screen each other's defenders.
    - Key Defender Put In Conflict: Nickel (defender on the inside slot)
    - Why It Works: Man defenders must turn and chase crossing routes, which means they cannot see the second crosser arriving — the collision at the mesh point is structural, not luck.
    - Failure Mode / Defensive Counter: Zone coverage lets defenders pass off the crossers without turning their heads, keeping two bodies in every shallow window.

    [SEQUENCING & GAME-PLAN LOGIC]
    - Sets Up: airraid-shallow-distribution-drive
    - Plays Off: None
    - Visual Tell Cue: Both inside receivers take identical one-step vertical fakes before breaking at exactly six yards.

    [TIMELINE COACHING BEATS]
      * [T=0.7s] 1. The Crossers Depart: Both inside receivers sell one vertical step before snapping down into the six-yard lanes. In man coverage, both defenders must turn their backs to the quarterback to chase.
      * [T=1.8s] 2. The First Read Is Taken Away: The boundary crosser's defender stays attached. The quarterback rides without panic — the Air Raid rule is simple: never throw a covered receiver.
      * [T=2.6s] 3. The Rub Forms: The second crosser arrives exactly where the first was defended. The chasing nickel is screened by the first crosser's body — an unavoidable natural pick.
      * [T=3.3s] 4. The Pitch and Catch: With the nickel picked and the Mike sorted too late, the second crosser comes open in stride. The quarterback delivers and the chain moves.

>>> PLAY: Y-Cross (ID: airraid-y-cross)
    Personnel: 11
    Formation: 11P Gun 2x2
    Situation: 2nd & 8, own 25, base down
    Defensive Look: Cover 3 Sky (4-2-5 Nickel front)
    Animation Duration: 4s
    Direct URL: https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=air-raid&play=airraid-y-cross

    [SUMMARY & TACTICAL PURPOSE]
    - Motive: Use the stick as bait to occupy the nickel and Will, then attack the vacated middle with the tight end's twelve-yard crosser.
    - Key Defender Put In Conflict: Mike Linebacker (middle hook dropper)
    - Why It Works: The vertical clearouts remove corner help, the stick removes the nickel, and the crosser arrives in the middle hole exactly as both linebackers are facing the wrong way.
    - Failure Mode / Defensive Counter: The Mike sinks deeper instead of opening flat, keeping his body between the quarterback and the crosser's climbing lane.

    [SEQUENCING & GAME-PLAN LOGIC]
    - Sets Up: airraid-stick-naked-constraint
    - Plays Off: airraid-mesh-concept
    - Visual Tell Cue: The tight end releases inside immediately — on mesh both crossers come from slots; here only one crosser ever appears.

    [TIMELINE COACHING BEATS]
      * [T=0.8s] 1. The Clearouts Leave First: Both outside receivers fire instant vertical releases, pinning each corner in his deep third so no underneath help exists on the perimeter.
      * [T=1.5s] 2. The Stick Draws the Nickel: The slot breaks his five-yard stick with outside leverage, and the nickel sits on it perfectly. The quarterback acknowledges but does not force it.
      * [T=2.5s] 3. The Crosser Climbs Underneath: The tight end wins inside and climbs to twelve yards, breaking down directly through the Mike's face while the Sam is still turned chasing him vertically.
      * [T=3.4s] 4. Behind the Free Safety's Shoulder: With both corners held deep and the hooks trailing, the crosser works into the soft spot behind the free safety's break for a big intermediate gain.

>>> PLAY: Stick-Naked Constraint (ID: airraid-stick-naked-constraint)
    Personnel: 10
    Formation: 10P Gun 3x1 Left
    Situation: 3rd & 4, own 42, must convert
    Defensive Look: Cover 2 Quarters (4-2-5 Nickel front)
    Animation Duration: 3.8s
    Direct URL: https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=air-raid&play=airraid-stick-naked-constraint

    [SUMMARY & TACTICAL PURPOSE]
    - Motive: Double-cover the stick deliberately so the naked swing constraint runs free behind over-committed flat defenders.
    - Key Defender Put In Conflict: Sam Linebacker (weak-flat defender)
    - Why It Works: Quarters rules force the flat player to sink with the stick; the running back's swing path occupies precisely the grass both defenders abandoned.
    - Failure Mode / Defensive Counter: The flat defender keeps outside-in leverage on the running back instead of sinking with the stick, taking away the constraint at its origin.

    [SEQUENCING & GAME-PLAN LOGIC]
    - Sets Up: airraid-y-cross
    - Plays Off: airraid-shallow-distribution-drive
    - Visual Tell Cue: The running back never blocks — he releases across the backfield on his first step, which no true stick play does.

    [TIMELINE COACHING BEATS]
      * [T=0.6s] 1. The Trips Distribution: Trips floods the weak side with three simultaneous threats: a seam clearout, a five-yard stick, and a bubble fake. The flat defender must pick one immediately.
      * [T=1.4s] 2. The Stick Bites Both Defenders: Both the nickel and the flat linebacker sink on the stick route, doubling a five-yard throw that was never meant to be caught.
      * [T=2.2s] 3. The Naked Swing Appears: With every defender staring at the trips distribution, the running back swings out of the backfield completely uncovered behind their shoulders.
      * [T=3.0s] 4. The Constraint Pays: The quarterback flips to the naked swing, the top of trips escorts the first tackler, and the conversion is made in space against zero defenders.

>>> PLAY: Shallow Distribution Drive (ID: airraid-shallow-distribution-drive)
    Personnel: 10
    Formation: 10P Gun 2x2
    Situation: 2nd & 9, own 20, backed up
    Defensive Look: Cover 3 Sky (4-3 Over front)
    Animation Duration: 4s
    Direct URL: https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=air-raid&play=airraid-shallow-distribution-drive

    [SUMMARY & TACTICAL PURPOSE]
    - Motive: Distribute the ball to whichever shallow receiver wins his individual leverage race, reading defenders rather than landmarks.
    - Key Defender Put In Conflict: Mike Linebacker (middle hook dropper)
    - Why It Works: Two staggered crossing layers mean any defender who covers one has turned his back on the other; the quarterback simply throws to the uncovered lever.
    - Failure Mode / Defensive Counter: Zone defenders trade assignments without turning their heads, keeping a fresh body square to the quarterback in both lanes.

    [SEQUENCING & GAME-PLAN LOGIC]
    - Sets Up: airraid-mesh-concept
    - Plays Off: airraid-stick-naked-constraint
    - Visual Tell Cue: The two crossers never converge at one point — they stay four yards apart in depth for the entire route.

    [TIMELINE COACHING BEATS]
      * [T=0.7s] 1. The Verticals Clear the Stage: Both slots fire instant seams while the flanker pins the corner, dragging every deep and hook defender away from the middle of the field.
      * [T=1.5s] 2. The Near Shallow Departs: The split end drives his six-yard shallow across the formation. The Mike takes one step with it — exactly the bait the Air Raid wants.
      * [T=2.4s] 3. The Deep Layer Crosses Behind: Four yards deeper, the drive route crosses directly beneath the first. The nickel who chased Y vertically is now trailing by a full body.
      * [T=3.3s] 4. Leverage Read Complete: With the near layer defended over the top and the deep layer trailed from behind, the quarterback throws to whichever shallow ran away from its leverage.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
SCHEME FAMILY: TUBBY RAYMOND'S DELAWARE WING-T [ID: delaware-wing-t]
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Architect / Coach: Harold "Tubby" Raymond
Organization / Team: Delaware (1966-2001)
Category: OFFENSE
Tree Branch: delaware-wing-t
Core Philosophy: The Delaware Wing-T is a series-based system where every play looks identical for the first two steps. Guard-pull Buck Sweep forces the perimeter to defend numbers it does not have, and Waggle, Counter Crisscross, and the Wingback Trap all feed off that single picture. Tubby Raymond ran this offense at Delaware for thirty-five years, winning three national championships.

PLAYS IN THIS SCHEME:

>>> PLAY: Buck Sweep w/ Guard Pull (ID: wingt-buck-sweep-guard-pull)
    Personnel: Wing-T Base
    Formation: Wing-T Strong Right, SE Left
    Situation: 1st & 10, own 35, base down
    Defensive Look: Cover 3 Sky (4-3 Over front)
    Animation Duration: 4.2s
    Direct URL: https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=delaware-wing-t&play=wingt-buck-sweep-guard-pull

    [SUMMARY & TACTICAL PURPOSE]
    - Motive: Get two blockers on the perimeter before the ball carrier arrives, collapsing contain inward so the sweep can turn upfield.
    - Key Defender Put In Conflict: Right Corner (perimeter force player)
    - Why It Works: The double pull attacks the edge with sequential kick-out and lead blocks, and the wing's arc removes the last force player exactly as the ball turns the corner.
    - Failure Mode / Defensive Counter: The end spills the kick-out and funnels the sweep inside, or the force safety squeezes the arc instead of taking the kick.

    [SEQUENCING & GAME-PLAN LOGIC]
    - Sets Up: wingt-waggle-flood, wingt-wingback-trap-gut
    - Plays Off: None
    - Visual Tell Cue: Both guards leave their gaps at the same instant — no other Wing-T series moves both interior linemen horizontally on the snap.

    [TIMELINE COACHING BEATS]
      * [T=0.6s] 1. The Double Pull: Both guards pull in opposite roles: the playside guard kicks flat toward the end while the backside guard pulls as the lead through the hole. The entire defense's eyes snap to the backfield.
      * [T=1.3s] 2. Kick-Out and Deep Handoff: The quarterback reverse-pivots and extends the handoff to B at depth while the guard logs the end inside. The sweep lane is now two gaps wide.
      * [T=2.3s] 3. The Perimeter Block Sequence: The wing kicks the force corner out just as the pulling guard arrives on the linebacker. Every defender who could squeeze the edge is being blocked outward.
      * [T=3.3s] 4. Turn Upfield Behind Escorts: With containment collapsed inward and force displaced, B turns north at the numbers with escorts leading him into the open grass.

>>> PLAY: Waggle Pass Off Sweep Fake (ID: wingt-waggle-flood)
    Personnel: Wing-T Base
    Formation: Wing-T Strong Right, SE Left
    Situation: 2nd & 5, own 40, off sweep tendency
    Defensive Look: Cover 3 Sky (4-3 Over front)
    Animation Duration: 4.4s
    Direct URL: https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=delaware-wing-t&play=wingt-waggle-flood

    [SUMMARY & TACTICAL PURPOSE]
    - Motive: Use the most convincing run action in football to move an entire defense one direction, then attack the vacated half with a three-level flood.
    - Key Defender Put In Conflict: Free Safety (deep middle)
    - Why It Works: Linebackers and the force safety trigger on the sweep and cannot recover, leaving the deep in isolated between a flat-watching corner and a flooded safety.
    - Failure Mode / Defensive Counter: The spill-and-contain call keeps linebackers home, or the corner plays with depth instead of dropping flat, crowding the deep-in window.

    [SEQUENCING & GAME-PLAN LOGIC]
    - Sets Up: wingt-counter-crisscross
    - Plays Off: wingt-buck-sweep-guard-pull
    - Visual Tell Cue: The quarterback reverses direction after the mesh instead of extending the handoff — live sweeps never send the ball carrier and passer to opposite halves.

    [TIMELINE COACHING BEATS]
      * [T=0.6s] 1. The Sweep Sell: Both guards pull exactly like Buck Sweep, the quarterback meshes with the sweeping halfback, and the entire second level starts flowing to its right.
      * [T=1.7s] 2. The Waggle Boot Away: Instead of following the sweep, the quarterback reverses out to the left behind the fullback's edge block while the defense keeps chasing the fake.
      * [T=2.6s] 3. Three Levels Flooding Left: The flood builds: the wing holds the flat, the tight end drives the crosser through the middle, and the split end climbs to the deep in.
      * [T=3.4s] 4. Deep In Behind Flowed Coverage: The waggle arrives with the deep in breaking behind a flat-dropping corner whose eyes never left the quarterback and a safety still leaning toward the sweep.

>>> PLAY: Counter Crisscross (ID: wingt-counter-crisscross)
    Personnel: Wing-T Base
    Formation: Wing-T Strong Right, SE Left
    Situation: 2nd & 6, own 30, after perimeter success
    Defensive Look: Cover 3 Sky (4-3 Over front)
    Animation Duration: 4.4s
    Direct URL: https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=delaware-wing-t&play=wingt-counter-crisscross

    [SUMMARY & TACTICAL PURPOSE]
    - Motive: Exploit Buck Sweep's tendency with an opposite-direction counter whose backfield action crossfaces every flow defender.
    - Key Defender Put In Conflict: Will Linebacker (flow reader)
    - Why It Works: The crisscross puts a ballcarrier fake moving both directions simultaneously, and the trey pullers arrive on the real play's edge before anyone redirects.
    - Failure Mode / Defensive Counter: Disciplined spill-and-scrape linebackers stay home on the crossface, letting them meet the counter in the hole with the pullers still trailing.

    [SEQUENCING & GAME-PLAN LOGIC]
    - Sets Up: wingt-buck-sweep-guard-pull
    - Plays Off: wingt-waggle-flood
    - Visual Tell Cue: The quarterback reverses his shoulder mid-play to hand off backward — live sweeps and boots never change the ballcarrier after the initial mesh.

    [TIMELINE COACHING BEATS]
      * [T=0.6s] 1. The Crisscross Backfield: The quarterback opens right and fakes the sweep to B while the wing loops behind him the other way — two backs crossing paths directly in front of every linebacker's key.
      * [T=1.6s] 2. The Trey Pullers: The guard pulls to kick the end while the tackle wraps behind him as the leader — identical footwork to Buck Sweep pointed the other direction.
      * [T=2.4s] 3. Crossfacing Chaos: The Will, Sam, and strong end are all chasing decoys to the right while the hidden handoff hits the counter hole behind them.
      * [T=3.4s] 4. The Counter Hits Left: The wing bursts through the kick-out seam behind the wrapping tackle. Only the Mike read it correctly — and the puller buries him anyway.

>>> PLAY: Wingback Trap-Gut (ID: wingt-wingback-trap-gut)
    Personnel: Wing-T Base
    Formation: Wing-T Strong Right, SE Left
    Situation: 3rd & 2, own 42, vs slanting fronts
    Defensive Look: Cover 3 Sky (4-3 Over front)
    Animation Duration: 4.2s
    Direct URL: https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=delaware-wing-t&play=wingt-wingback-trap-gut

    [SUMMARY & TACTICAL PURPOSE]
    - Motive: Punish aggressive interior slants by trapping the penetrating lineman under complete Buck Sweep disguise.
    - Key Defender Put In Conflict: 3-Tech Defensive Tackle (slanting trap target)
    - Why It Works: The full sweep sell sends every perimeter defender wide while the trap converts the slant's own momentum into a kicked-open B-gap.
    - Failure Mode / Defensive Counter: The tackle two-gaps instead of slanting, or linebackers play slow-to-the-ball discipline and meet the gut before the lead block lands.

    [SEQUENCING & GAME-PLAN LOGIC]
    - Sets Up: None
    - Plays Off: wingt-buck-sweep-guard-pull, wingt-counter-crisscross
    - Visual Tell Cue: The playside guard pulls flat then reverses direction mid-step — true sweep pullers never come back to the interior.

    [TIMELINE COACHING BEATS]
      * [T=0.5s] 1. The Sweep Footwork Sell: The quarterback pivots off the Buck Sweep mesh while both guards show their signature pull steps and B presses the edge — every perimeter trigger fires.
      * [T=1.2s] 2. The Trap Springs: The slanting 3-tech penetrates himself into the trap as the guard whirs back and kicks him out of the very gap he was shooting.
      * [T=2.0s] 3. Downhill Through the B-Gap: The wing takes the hidden exchange and hits the vacated seam full speed behind the redirecting lead guard, who buries the filling linebacker.
      * [T=3.2s] 4. The Perimeter Still Sold: The force corner and safety are still chasing the sweep fake at the numbers while the gut gains vertically between the hashes.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
SCHEME FAMILY: VINCE LOMBARDI'S T-FORMATION POWER SWEEP [ID: t-formation-power-sweep]
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Architect / Coach: Vince Lombardi
Organization / Team: Green Bay Packers (1959-67)
Category: OFFENSE
Tree Branch: power-gap-duo
Core Philosophy: The most sequenced run system in football history. The double-pull sweep ran dozens of times a game, and every companion play — counter-boot, fullback blast, and flood bootleg — borrowed its exact picture so defenses could never trust what they saw.

PLAYS IN THIS SCHEME:

>>> PLAY: Power Sweep Left (ID: sweep-power-sweep-left)
    Personnel: 21
    Formation: T Formation, Ends Both Sides
    Situation: 2nd & 4, own 45, base down
    Defensive Look: Cover 3 Sky (4-3 Over front)
    Animation Duration: 4s
    Direct URL: https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=t-formation-power-sweep&play=sweep-power-sweep-left

    [SUMMARY & TACTICAL PURPOSE]
    - Motive: Run outside the tackles behind two pulling guards so the defense's edge structure collapses inward and the perimeter belongs to the offense.
    - Key Defender Put In Conflict: Will Linebacker (weak-side flow linebacker)
    - Why It Works: The double pull forces every defender to re-fit mid-play; the kick-out removes force and the lead block plus downfield escorts guarantee one clean running lane.
    - Failure Mode / Defensive Counter: The force defender beats the kick-out block outside, or the backside pursuit angles close the lane before the escorts arrive.

    [SEQUENCING & GAME-PLAN LOGIC]
    - Sets Up: sweep-fullback-blast, sweep-sweep-pass-bootleg
    - Plays Off: None
    - Visual Tell Cue: Two linemen leave the line of scrimmage immediately in opposite directions — no Lombardi companion play shows this picture.

    [TIMELINE COACHING BEATS]
      * [T=0.6s] 1. The Double Pull Begins: Both guards pull simultaneously — the first leads through the lane while the second wraps to kick out the force player. The defense sees pulling linemen and must re-route its fits instantly.
      * [T=1.2s] 2. The Deep Handoff: The quarterback extends the ball at full depth so the halfback receives it already moving sideways at the sideline landmark, never slowing his momentum.
      * [T=2.4s] 3. The Force Player Is Kicked Out: The wrapping guard arrives at the force corner and drives him inside. The entire defensive edge collapses inward while the sweep lane stays wide.
      * [T=3.3s] 4. The Downfield Escort: With the force kicked out and the alley blocked, the halfback turns upfield behind three escorts — including a flanker who has crossed the formation to stalk the last pursuer.

>>> PLAY: Power Sweep Right w/ Boot Fake (ID: sweep-power-sweep-right-boot-fake)
    Personnel: 21
    Formation: T Formation, Ends Both Sides
    Situation: 1st & 10, own 32, after a sweep left gain
    Defensive Look: Cover 3 Sky (4-3 Over front)
    Animation Duration: 4.2s
    Direct URL: https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=t-formation-power-sweep&play=sweep-power-sweep-right-boot-fake

    [SUMMARY & TACTICAL PURPOSE]
    - Motive: Use the sweep's identical picture to drag all eleven defenders right, then attack the abandoned backside with a counter-bootleg.
    - Key Defender Put In Conflict: Free Safety (split-field safety)
    - Why It Works: The carry-out fake holds every run-fit defender for two seconds; when the quarterback reverses, the backside contains are chasing the sweep and cannot recover.
    - Failure Mode / Defensive Counter: The backside end stays home instead of chasing the sweep, meeting the bootleg in the lane before the quarterback can set.

    [SEQUENCING & GAME-PLAN LOGIC]
    - Sets Up: sweep-power-sweep-left, sweep-fullback-blast
    - Plays Off: sweep-power-sweep-left
    - Visual Tell Cue: The quarterback keeps the ball after the mesh — on the true sweep he is empty-handed within one step.

    [TIMELINE COACHING BEATS]
      * [T=0.7s] 1. The Identical Sweep Picture: Both guards pull and the halfback crosses for the same deep handoff as the base Power Sweep Left — the defense has no pre-snap reason to expect anything different.
      * [T=1.5s] 2. The Full Carry-Out: The quarterback pulls the ball only after selling the complete mesh, keeping his shoulders square to the sweep for two full steps while every linebacker flows right.
      * [T=2.3s] 3. The Counter Reversal: The quarterback plants and reverses into the boot lane behind the left end's hinge. The entire defensive flow is now running away from the ball.
      * [T=3.5s] 4. Open Grass Behind the Flow: The quarterback sets his feet in the vacated backside with the free safety still recovering — every receiver-side option is now against single coverage.

>>> PLAY: Fullback Blast (ID: sweep-fullback-blast)
    Personnel: 21
    Formation: T Formation, Ends Both Sides
    Situation: 3rd & 1, own 40, short yardage after sweep success
    Defensive Look: Cover 1 Robber (4-3 Over front)
    Animation Duration: 3.6s
    Direct URL: https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=t-formation-power-sweep&play=sweep-fullback-blast

    [SUMMARY & TACTICAL PURPOSE]
    - Motive: Punish defenses that over-play the sweep by handing to the fullback between the tackles off identical footwork.
    - Key Defender Put In Conflict: Will Linebacker (flow linebacker)
    - Why It Works: The sweep fake removes both flow defenders while the ISO combo physically removes the Mike, leaving one uncovered gap for the fullback.
    - Failure Mode / Defensive Counter: Linebackers stay home on the sweep look and the Mike defeats the combo block before the fullback reaches the hole.

    [SEQUENCING & GAME-PLAN LOGIC]
    - Sets Up: sweep-power-sweep-right-boot-fake
    - Plays Off: sweep-power-sweep-left
    - Visual Tell Cue: The fullback takes the ball instead of leading it — every true sweep shows the fullback blocking on the perimeter.

    [TIMELINE COACHING BEATS]
      * [T=0.6s] 1. Identical Sweep Footwork: The quarterback opens with the exact same steps as Power Sweep Left and the halfback crosses on the same path. Every linebacker keys the sweep flow immediately.
      * [T=1.3s] 2. The Ball Changes Direction: At the last moment the quarterback pulls the ball back and hands to the fullback diving up the middle. The Will and weak corner are already committed left.
      * [T=2.0s] 3. The ISO Combo Arrives: The guard and center climb off their double-team directly onto the Mike linebacker — the classic isolation block that defines this companion play.
      * [T=2.9s] 4. Through the Filled Hole: With the Mike driven off the ball and both flow defenders chasing the decoy, the fullback falls forward through the vacated A/B gap for the conversion.

>>> PLAY: Sweep-Pass Bootleg (ID: sweep-sweep-pass-bootleg)
    Personnel: 21
    Formation: T Formation, End Right, Flanker Right
    Situation: 2nd & 7, own 38, after two sweep gains
    Defensive Look: Cover 3 Sky (4-3 Over front)
    Animation Duration: 4.2s
    Direct URL: https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=t-formation-power-sweep&play=sweep-sweep-pass-bootleg

    [SUMMARY & TACTICAL PURPOSE]
    - Motive: Convert sweep credibility into a moving-pocket flood throw against defenders frozen by run fits.
    - Key Defender Put In Conflict: Sam Linebacker (strong-hook defender)
    - Why It Works: Every run-fit defender commits left for two seconds; when the quarterback reverses, the flood presents three levels against a defense running the wrong way.
    - Failure Mode / Defensive Counter: The backside contain refuses the sweep bait and squeezes the rollout lane, forcing the throw early or forcing a scramble.

    [SEQUENCING & GAME-PLAN LOGIC]
    - Sets Up: sweep-power-sweep-left, sweep-power-sweep-right-boot-fake
    - Plays Off: sweep-power-sweep-left
    - Visual Tell Cue: The tight end releases vertically instead of blocking — no true Lombardi sweep shows an end running a pass route.

    [TIMELINE COACHING BEATS]
      * [T=0.7s] 1. The Perfect Sweep Picture: Both guards pull, the fullback dives, and the halfback crosses for the handoff — an identical copy of the play that has already gained yards twice.
      * [T=1.6s] 2. The Full Carry-Out Left: The quarterback completes the fake at depth and carries it two full steps toward the weak sideline while Will, the Mike, and the corner all chase left.
      * [T=2.6s] 3. The Flood Forms Behind Him: As the quarterback reverses into his rollout right, three receivers are already stacked at fifteen, ten, and minus-two depths — a full high-to-low flood.
      * [T=3.7s] 4. The High-Low Answer: The sky safety is pinned above the TE's deep route, so the quarterback throws to the ten-yard out where the Sam arrives a half-second late.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
SCHEME FAMILY: CHRIS AULT'S PISTOL READ-OPTION [ID: pistol-read-option]
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Architect / Coach: Chris Ault
Organization / Team: Nevada Wolf Pack
Category: OFFENSE
Tree Branch: option-spread
Core Philosophy: The Pistol marries gun spacing with under-center run physics: the quarterback lines up four yards deep with the back directly behind him, so every zone and gap run hits downhill at full pad level while still carrying a quarterback keep threat. Chris Ault invented the formation at Nevada, where Colin Kaepernick turned it into a 2,000-yard rushing attack.

PLAYS IN THIS SCHEME:

>>> PLAY: Pistol Inside Zone Read (ID: pistol-inside-zone-read)
    Personnel: 11
    Formation: Pistol Right Slot, TE Right
    Situation: 1st & 10, own 30, base down
    Defensive Look: Cover 3 Buzz (4-3 Over front)
    Animation Duration: 4s
    Direct URL: https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=pistol-read-option&play=pistol-inside-zone-read

    [SUMMARY & TACTICAL PURPOSE]
    - Motive: Put the backside end in an instant give-or-keep conflict using downhill pistol run physics.
    - Key Defender Put In Conflict: Backside Defensive End (unblocked read key)
    - Why It Works: The pistol keeps the back moving forward at the mesh, so any aggressive crash by the read key surrenders the A-gap before the defense can reroute pursuit.
    - Failure Mode / Defensive Counter: The end squeezes and spilles simultaneously while staying square, clogging both branches until help arrives.

    [SEQUENCING & GAME-PLAN LOGIC]
    - Sets Up: pistol-pa-deep-shot
    - Plays Off: None
    - Visual Tell Cue: The running back is directly behind the quarterback at six yards and hits the line downhill — gun reads develop a half-yard deeper.

    [TIMELINE COACHING BEATS]
      * [T=0.6s] 1. The Pistol Mesh and Read: The pistol alignment puts the back downhill at the snap. The quarterback seats the mesh while staring at one man — the unblocked backside end.
      * [T=1.1s] 2. The Crash Gives It Away: The end shoots inside hunting the quarterback. By attacking the keep he hands the give branch an empty A-gap, and the ball comes out instantly.
      * [T=2.0s] 3. Downhill Through the A-Gap: The back presses downhill behind the scoop-and-climb guard while the quarterback carries the boot fake the other way, freezing the pursuit.
      * [T=3.0s] 4. Second-Level Finish: With the Mike scooped and the safety taking a bad alley angle, the back finishes vertically into the open middle field.

>>> PLAY: Pistol Power-O Read (ID: pistol-power-o-read)
    Personnel: 11
    Formation: Pistol Right Slot, TE Right
    Situation: 2nd & 5, own 38, gap-run tendency
    Defensive Look: Cover 3 Buzz (4-3 Over front)
    Animation Duration: 4s
    Direct URL: https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=pistol-read-option&play=pistol-power-o-read

    [SUMMARY & TACTICAL PURPOSE]
    - Motive: Combine gap-scheme power blocking with a read of the backside end so the defense must defend both the pull and the keep.
    - Key Defender Put In Conflict: Backside Defensive End (unblocked read key)
    - Why It Works: The pull is irresistible bait for the end, and once he chases it the wrap blocker owns the second level while the kick-out has already collapsed the edge.
    - Failure Mode / Defensive Counter: The end stays home and squeezes the pull instead, forcing the quarterback to pull the ball into an unblocked C-gap with nowhere to go.

    [SEQUENCING & GAME-PLAN LOGIC]
    - Sets Up: pistol-speed-option
    - Plays Off: pistol-inside-zone-read
    - Visual Tell Cue: A guard pulls while the quarterback still reads a defender — pure power-o hands the ball immediately with no ride phase.

    [TIMELINE COACHING BEATS]
      * [T=0.6s] 1. The Pull and the Read: The guard kicks flat toward the edge while the quarterback seats the pistol mesh with eyes locked on the unblocked backside end.
      * [T=1.2s] 2. The End Chases the Puller: The end bites on the pull and sprints inside chasing it. His edge is gone, so the give branch is declared before the ball even arrives.
      * [T=2.2s] 3. Kick-Out and Wrap: The guard logs the playside end inside while the wrapping tackle rises into the hole hunting the Mike linebacker.
      * [T=3.2s] 4. Off-Tackle Behind the Leader: The back presses off-tackle behind the wrap block, turning upfield through a seam where both second-level defenders have been displaced.

>>> PLAY: Pistol PA Deep Shot (ID: pistol-pa-deep-shot)
    Personnel: 11
    Formation: Pistol Right Slot, TE Right
    Situation: 1st & 10, +40, off run tendency
    Defensive Look: Cover 1 Robber (Nickel 4-2-5)
    Animation Duration: 4.2s
    Direct URL: https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=pistol-read-option&play=pistol-pa-deep-shot

    [SUMMARY & TACTICAL PURPOSE]
    - Motive: Weaponize the pistol run identity to vacate the deep middle, then attack it with a post shot off a half-roll.
    - Key Defender Put In Conflict: Free Safety (middle-third defender)
    - Why It Works: The downhill mesh forces both second-level defenders and the robber to trigger before the quarterback ever looks downfield, isolating the middle third against two routes.
    - Failure Mode / Defensive Counter: The safety plays run-pass split discipline instead of triggering, keeping his shoulders square to the post developing behind the crosser.

    [SEQUENCING & GAME-PLAN LOGIC]
    - Sets Up: None
    - Plays Off: pistol-inside-zone-read
    - Visual Tell Cue: The slot releases across the formation instead of arcing to kick a linebacker, and the line finishes with pass-set feet — live runs never do either.

    [TIMELINE COACHING BEATS]
      * [T=0.7s] 1. The Identical Zone-Read Sell: Every cue from the pistol inside zone read is present: the same mesh, the same line footwork, the back carrying the ball downhill into the second level.
      * [T=1.6s] 2. The Safety Trigger: The robber fires down on the run action while the Mike triggers onto the diving back. Both vacate the middle of the field before the ball moves.
      * [T=2.4s] 3. Roll-Out Flood Builds: The quarterback half-rolls off the fake as the flood develops: the crosser drags the free safety's eyes while the tight end releases late into the hole.
      * [T=3.3s] 4. Post Behind the Frozen Third: Z breaks off his go route into the post lane behind a middle-third defender who never recovered from the run fit. The shot lands over the trailing corner.

>>> PLAY: Pistol Speed Option (ID: pistol-speed-option)
    Personnel: 11
    Formation: Pistol Right Slot, TE Right
    Situation: 2nd & 4, +45, perimeter numbers call
    Defensive Look: Cover 3 Buzz (4-3 Over front)
    Animation Duration: 4.2s
    Direct URL: https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=pistol-read-option&play=pistol-speed-option

    [SUMMARY & TACTICAL PURPOSE]
    - Motive: Force the perimeter force player into an instantaneous declare so the pitch punishes any aggressive trigger.
    - Key Defender Put In Conflict: Field Corner (force player)
    - Why It Works: The arc plus pitch-track spacing makes the quarterback pitchable only when the corner commits upfield, converting his aggression directly into a numbers advantage.
    - Failure Mode / Defensive Counter: The corner squeezes and stays square, keeping both phases alive until help arrives over the top of the option.

    [SEQUENCING & GAME-PLAN LOGIC]
    - Sets Up: None
    - Plays Off: pistol-power-o-read, pistol-pa-deep-shot
    - Visual Tell Cue: The quarterback never rides a mesh before arcing — every other pistol run seats the ball for at least a full step.

    [TIMELINE COACHING BEATS]
      * [T=0.8s] 1. The Arc and Flow: The quarterback arcs flat off the pistol mesh while the slot sprints across to get ahead of the ball — the entire defense starts flowing to its right.
      * [T=1.8s] 2. Force Declares: The pitch track puts F even with the arc as both men read one defender: the force corner. Whatever he does next decides the football.
      * [T=2.5s] 3. Pitch on the Trigger: The corner triggers upfield hunting the quarterback — exactly the cue that makes him pitchable. The ball goes out with F already at full speed.
      * [T=3.4s] 4. Perimeter Finish: The safety arrives a beat late and gets led-on by the crossing slot while F turns north at full stride behind the displaced force.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
SCHEME FAMILY: ART BRILES' BAYLOR VERTICAL CHOICE SPREAD [ID: baylor-choice]
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Architect / Coach: Art Briles
Organization / Team: Baylor Bears (2008-15)
Category: OFFENSE
Tree Branch: option-spread
Core Philosophy: The Baylor vertical choice spread weaponized run action into touchdown shots. Every call starts with an inside-zone read, jet sweep, or screen picture that forces the second level to defend the box, then punishes whichever safety leans with single-word choice routes and doubled posts over the top. Defenses had to guard the entire deep field on every snap or concede six.

PLAYS IN THIS SCHEME:

>>> PLAY: Slot Choice Shot (ID: baylor-slot-choice-shot)
    Personnel: 11
    Formation: 11P Gun, Slot Left
    Situation: 1st & 10, own 35, vs two-high shell
    Defensive Look: Cover 2 Zone (4-3 Over front)
    Animation Duration: 4s
    Direct URL: https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=baylor-choice&play=baylor-slot-choice-shot

    [SUMMARY & TACTICAL PURPOSE]
    - Motive: Use simple inside-zone action to freeze the second level while the slot runs a leverage-based vertical shot for a touchdown.
    - Key Defender Put In Conflict: Nickel (run-fit defender on the slot)
    - Why It Works: One word triggers the whole play: the run action buys the linebackers, the choice stem punishes whichever way the nickel leans, and both corners are cleared out.
    - Failure Mode / Defensive Counter: The nickel plays pure man from the snap instead of fitting run, staying attached to the slot's hip throughout the climb.

    [SEQUENCING & GAME-PLAN LOGIC]
    - Sets Up: baylor-iz-read-choice-double-post, baylor-bubble-go-glance
    - Plays Off: None
    - Visual Tell Cue: The slot releases instantly vertical with no stem variation — a true option route adjusts mid-route; this one never breaks.

    [TIMELINE COACHING BEATS]
      * [T=0.7s] 1. The Run Picture Sells: Five linemen fire inside-zone steps and the quarterback rides the give. Both linebackers trigger downhill and the nickel steps toward the box.
      * [T=1.7s] 2. The Nickel Loses His Feet: The slot takes his CHOICE release straight upfield off outside leverage. The nickel, mid-run-fit, must stop his feet and turn — losing two critical yards.
      * [T=2.6s] 3. The Safety Picks a Seam: With both corners pinned and the TE stretching the middle, the free safety must choose between the boundary seam and the field-side window. He picks wrong.
      * [T=3.4s] 4. The Single-Word Shot Pays: The whole call was one word — the slot's choice route ran itself off leverage. The quarterback delivers over the top of the still-triggering defense.

>>> PLAY: IZ Read + Choice Double-Post (ID: baylor-iz-read-choice-double-post)
    Personnel: 11
    Formation: 11P Gun, Slot Left
    Situation: 2nd & 6, own 30, vs single-high shell
    Defensive Look: Cover 3 Zone (4-3 Over front)
    Animation Duration: 4s
    Direct URL: https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=baylor-choice&play=baylor-iz-read-choice-double-post

    [SUMMARY & TACTICAL PURPOSE]
    - Motive: Pair a true zone-read pull with a double-post shot so the run action buys the second level while the safety is forced to defend both deep middles alone.
    - Key Defender Put In Conflict: Free safety (single-high, caught between two posts)
    - Why It Works: The read makes the edge defend the quarterback, which freezes the linebackers on run fits, while two converging choice posts guarantee the lone deep defender picks the wrong lever.
    - Failure Mode / Defensive Counter: The end squeezes rather than crashes, keeping the quarterback in the box, and the safety splits the posts from depth instead of committing.

    [SEQUENCING & GAME-PLAN LOGIC]
    - Sets Up: baylor-bubble-go-glance
    - Plays Off: baylor-slot-choice-shot
    - Visual Tell Cue: The ball stays in the quarterback's hands after the mesh — a pure zone-read RPO would throw immediately off the read instead of pulling and climbing to set feet.

    [TIMELINE COACHING BEATS]
      * [T=0.7s] 1. The Read Sells the Give: Five linemen fire inside-zone steps and the quarterback rides the mesh. The linebackers trigger downhill and even the nickel tips toward the box.
      * [T=1.6s] 2. The Pull Punishes the Crash: The read end crashes on the running back and the quarterback pulls instantly. With the edge vacated, he escapes clean and looks downfield.
      * [T=2.5s] 3. Two Posts, One Safety: Both boundary receivers climb vertically off choice releases and bend to the middle deep at staggered depths. The single-high safety has run eyes and two stems entering his vision.
      * [T=3.4s] 4. The Deep Middle Surrenders: The safety commits to the outside post and the inside post crosses free behind him. The quarterback delivers off the pulled read over the frozen second level.

>>> PLAY: Bubble-Go Glance (ID: baylor-bubble-go-glance)
    Personnel: 11
    Formation: 11P Gun, Slot Right Strong
    Situation: 3rd & 3, own 42, vs man-coverage nickel look
    Defensive Look: Cover 1 Man (4-3 Over front)
    Animation Duration: 3.8s
    Direct URL: https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=baylor-choice&play=baylor-bubble-go-glance

    [SUMMARY & TACTICAL PURPOSE]
    - Motive: Sell the bubble-screen picture to trigger the force defenders uphill, then convert the slot to a glance vertical that attacks the vacated seam.
    - Key Defender Put In Conflict: Nickel (the screen trigger)
    - Why It Works: Every offensive cue screams screen — the arc, the flare, the arm flash — so the nickel abandons his deep responsibility at full speed and cannot recover once the slot plants behind him.
    - Failure Mode / Defensive Counter: The nickel stays patient and sinks rather than triggers, playing the slot's hips through the plant and staying attached to the glance.

    [SEQUENCING & GAME-PLAN LOGIC]
    - Sets Up: baylor-speed-sweep-constraint
    - Plays Off: None
    - Visual Tell Cue: The slot's first two steps carry him toward the sideline like a true bubble — but a real bubble keeps flattening; this one plants and climbs at the numbers.

    [TIMELINE COACHING BEATS]
      * [T=0.6s] 1. The Bubble Picture Is Painted: The slot bubbles outside while the back flares into the flat and the quarterback flashes his screen arm. Every cue points to a perimeter throw.
      * [T=1.4s] 2. The Trigger Commits: The nickel bites fully, sprinting up to strangle the screen at the numbers. The flat defender follows the picture instead of sinking with the slot.
      * [T=2.2s] 3. The Plant Converts: At full bubble speed the slot plants and converts straight upfield, passing behind the committed trigger. The corner is already cleared by the go route.
      * [T=3.2s] 4. The Glance Over the Top: The quarterback transfers from the fake posture and delivers the glance over the hook linebacker. The post safety is leaning the wrong way as it lands.

>>> PLAY: Speed Sweep Constraint (ID: baylor-speed-sweep-constraint)
    Personnel: 11
    Formation: 11P Gun, Slot Left (jet across)
    Situation: 2nd & 5, own 38, vs quarters look with aggressive force
    Defensive Look: Cover 2 Zone (4-3 Over front)
    Animation Duration: 4s
    Direct URL: https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=baylor-choice&play=baylor-speed-sweep-constraint

    [SUMMARY & TACTICAL PURPOSE]
    - Motive: Force both perimeter defenders to defend the sideline honestly so they cannot cheat toward the choice shots this family lives on.
    - Key Defender Put In Conflict: Nickel (the force player)
    - Why It Works: Jet speed forces the nickel to commit as force pre-exchange, the tight end kicks him out at the perfect landmark, and the stalk removes the corner — leaving only a safety making a hopeless alley tackle.
    - Failure Mode / Defensive Counter: The nickel plays off the kickout with leverage instead of taking it head-on, spilling the carrier inside where the scraping linebacker waits.

    [SEQUENCING & GAME-PLAN LOGIC]
    - Sets Up: baylor-iz-read-choice-double-post
    - Plays Off: None
    - Visual Tell Cue: The ball changes hands to a full-speed receiver crossing the formation — no other call in this family puts the ball on the perimeter before the second level moves.

    [TIMELINE COACHING BEATS]
      * [T=0.7s] 1. The Jet Stretches the Edge: The slot jets across at full speed while the line reaches right and the back fakes weak. The nickel must declare himself as force before the exchange even lands.
      * [T=1.4s] 2. The Kickout Erases the Force: The tight end kicks the nickel head-on exactly where he must be. With force eliminated, the safety inherits an alley fill he cannot make in time.
      * [T=2.4s] 3. The Corner Is Stalked: The flanker stalks the sweep-side corner as the carrier presses the numbers. Both primary force defenders are now accounted for without throwing a pass.
      * [T=3.3s] 4. The Perimeter Pays: The carrier bends up off the kickout with the whole defense flowing laterally behind him. This is the constraint that makes every choice shot credible.
