SCHEME FAMILY: URBAN MEYER'S SPREAD OPTION [ID: meyer-spread-option]
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Architect / Coach: Urban Meyer
Organization / Team: Florida / Ohio State (2001-18)
Category: OFFENSE
Tree Branch: option-spread
Core Philosophy: The Meyer spread option pairs zone-read runs and inverted veer with snag-triangle passing, all built on one principle: make the defense defend the quarterback as a runner on every snap. Perimeter jet motion and reverse constraints stretch the field horizontally while the read game attacks it vertically. Two national championships were built on this foundation.

PLAYS IN THIS SCHEME:

>>> PLAY: Inside Zone Read Give (ID: meyer-inside-zone-read-give)
    Personnel: 11
    Formation: Gun Spread Right Slot, TE Right
    Situation: 1st & 10, own 32, base down
    Defensive Look: Cover 3 Buzz (4-3 Over front)
    Animation Duration: 4s
    Direct URL: https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=meyer-spread-option&play=meyer-inside-zone-read-give

    [SUMMARY & TACTICAL PURPOSE]
    - Motive: Make the backside end choose between the quarterback and the A-gap, then punish the crash with an instant downhill give.
    - Key Defender Put In Conflict: Backside Defensive End (unblocked read key)
    - Why It Works: Spread spacing forces the end to declare immediately, and his aggression toward the keeper opens the exact lane the offset back is already attacking.
    - Failure Mode / Defensive Counter: The end squeezes square and spills, clogging the give while staying connected enough to contest a late pull.

    [SEQUENCING & GAME-PLAN LOGIC]
    - Sets Up: meyer-inverted-veer-power-read
    - Plays Off: None
    - Visual Tell Cue: The ball leaves the quarterback's hands before his shoulders ever turn — a true keep rides through the mesh point.

    [TIMELINE COACHING BEATS]
      * [T=0.6s] 1. The Read and the Crash: The quarterback seats the mesh with eyes locked on the unblocked backside end. The end fires inside hunting the keeper instead of squeezing the gap.
      * [T=1.1s] 2. The Give Branch: The crash declares the answer instantly: the ball goes into the belly of a back who is already at full forward lean through the vacated A-gap.
      * [T=2.0s] 3. Downhill Finish: The back presses downhill behind the scoop-and-climb guard while the quarterback sells the boot fake the other way, pinning the pursuit.
      * [T=3.0s] 4. The Boot Fake Sells: With the Mike scooped and both safeties triggering on the fake keeper, the give finishes vertically through the open middle field.

>>> PLAY: Inverted Veer Power Read (ID: meyer-inverted-veer-power-read)
    Personnel: 11
    Formation: Gun Spread Right Slot, TE Right
    Situation: 2nd & 3, own 40, jet-sweep tendency set
    Defensive Look: Cover 3 Buzz (4-3 Over front)
    Animation Duration: 4.2s
    Direct URL: https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=meyer-spread-option&play=meyer-inverted-veer-power-read

    [SUMMARY & TACTICAL PURPOSE]
    - Motive: Use a jet sweep presentation to displace the playside end, then attack the vacated interior with a quarterback pull.
    - Key Defender Put In Conflict: Playside Defensive End (unblocked read key)
    - Why It Works: Full-speed motion makes the sweep credible enough to move the end laterally, and the inverted geometry means his displacement opens the box instead of the edge.
    - Failure Mode / Defensive Counter: The end squeezes down on the flip instead of chasing width, sitting exactly where the pull wants to go.

    [SEQUENCING & GAME-PLAN LOGIC]
    - Sets Up: meyer-snag-triangle-spacing
    - Plays Off: meyer-inside-zone-read-give
    - Visual Tell Cue: The ballcarrier crosses the formation before the mesh ever happens — classic zone reads have no motion at the snap.

    [TIMELINE COACHING BEATS]
      * [T=0.8s] 1. Jet Sweep Sets the Trap: The slot crosses at dead sprint and the quarterback flips him the sweep look. The playside end cannot resist widening to chase the perimeter threat.
      * [T=1.4s] 2. The End Chases the Motion: With the end committed outside-in on the sweep, the entire B-gap and A-gap collapse inward with nobody home to defend them.
      * [T=2.1s] 3. Pull Into the Vacated Box: The quarterback pulls the ball off the jet flip and keeps it inside, where the offset back is already kicking the Mike out of his path.
      * [T=3.2s] 4. Inside Finish Behind the Lead Block: The keeper climbs through the scooped A-gap while both safeties trigger late, finishing upfield through the middle of the defense.

>>> PLAY: Snag Triangle Spacing (ID: meyer-snag-triangle-spacing)
    Personnel: 11
    Formation: Gun Spread Right Slot, TE Right
    Situation: 3rd & 4, +42, off run tendency
    Defensive Look: Cover 3 Sky (4-3 Over front)
    Animation Duration: 4s
    Direct URL: https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=meyer-spread-option&play=meyer-snag-triangle-spacing

    [SUMMARY & TACTICAL PURPOSE]
    - Motive: Attack Cover 3 with three-layer spacing that puts every single defender in an impossible high-low conflict.
    - Key Defender Put In Conflict: Sam Linebacker (strong curl-flat defender)
    - Why It Works: The run-action freeze delays every underneath drop exactly long enough for the triangle layers to establish separation in their three separate windows.
    - Failure Mode / Defensive Counter: Linebackers play slow-to-the-ball discipline through the run fake, keeping their drops intact and crowding both underneath windows.

    [SEQUENCING & GAME-PLAN LOGIC]
    - Sets Up: None
    - Plays Off: meyer-inside-zone-read-give, meyer-speed-option-reverse
    - Visual Tell Cue: The running back releases to the flat instead of carrying a dive fake — live read-option plays never send the back away from the mesh.

    [TIMELINE COACHING BEATS]
      * [T=0.7s] 1. Run Action Freezes the Box: The identical zone-read mesh sends every linebacker and the robber triggering downhill while the quarterback resets his feet to throw.
      * [T=1.5s] 2. The Triangle Builds: Three receivers stack vertically on the right at three depths: the back in the flat, the tight end settling at five, and the wideout breaking the corner at twelve.
      * [T=2.3s] 3. Snag Wins vs the Hook: The Mike's eyes were frozen by run action, so the snag settles directly behind his drop while he chases depth he can never recover.
      * [T=3.1s] 4. High-Low Finish: If the flat defender drives on the catch, the corner route is open behind him; if he sinks, the snag is easy money. The triangle guarantees one is free.

>>> PLAY: Speed Option w/ Reverse Constraint (ID: meyer-speed-option-reverse)
    Personnel: 11
    Formation: Gun Spread Right Slot, TE Right
    Situation: 2nd & 5, +45, perimeter speed call
    Defensive Look: Cover 3 Buzz (4-3 Over front)
    Animation Duration: 4.2s
    Direct URL: https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=meyer-spread-option&play=meyer-speed-option-reverse

    [SUMMARY & TACTICAL PURPOSE]
    - Motive: Attack the perimeter with a speed option while a reverse-constraint motion freezes the backside from pursuing.
    - Key Defender Put In Conflict: Field Corner (force player)
    - Why It Works: The reverse motion makes backside pursuit hesitate at the snap, so the only defenders who can make the play are the ones the option geometry already beats.
    - Failure Mode / Defensive Counter: The backside end plays the mesh instead of the motion, keeping his contain shoulder free to squeeze the arc from behind.

    [SEQUENCING & GAME-PLAN LOGIC]
    - Sets Up: None
    - Plays Off: meyer-snag-triangle-spacing
    - Visual Tell Cue: Motion moves away from the run direction at full sprint — normal speed-option motions always move toward the play.

    [TIMELINE COACHING BEATS]
      * [T=0.8s] 1. Reverse Motion Constraint: The slot sprints leftward selling a reverse receipt. The backside end and Will freeze on it while the actual option geometry develops to the right.
      * [T=1.8s] 2. The Arc Against Frozen Pursuit: The quarterback arcs off the fake exchange with half the defense still keyed left. The Mike is already a full recovery behind the play.
      * [T=2.5s] 3. Pitch on the Force Trigger: The force corner triggers upfield hunting the quarterback — the exact cue that makes him pitchable — and the stalk removes his recovery angle.
      * [T=3.4s] 4. Perimeter Finish: The pitch is taken at full speed around displaced force while the backside remains frozen by a reverse threat that never existed.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
SCHEME FAMILY: BUDDY RYAN'S 46 DEFENSE [ID: buddy-46-defense]
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Architect / Coach: Buddy Ryan
Organization / Team: Chicago Bears (1982-85)
Category: DEFENSE
Tree Branch: buddy-46
Core Philosophy: The most aggressive defense in NFL history. Ends aligned head-up at tight-end width, tackles shaded inside, three linebackers bunched at 2-3 yards, and BOTH safeties walked into an eight-man box with zero deep-middle help. Corners survive on islands in press-man. The base picture alone forces offenses to abandon their blocking rules; the mad-dog mug, E-X-T combo, and free blade blitzes turn that confusion into sacks.

PLAYS IN THIS SCHEME:

>>> PLAY: Base 46 vs Pro I-Form (ID: b46-base-i-form)
    Personnel: Base 46 Front
    Formation: 46 Front vs Pro I-Form Strong Right
    Situation: 1st & 10, +35, base down
    Defensive Look: Press-Man Zero (No Deep Safety) (46 Front (Head-Up Ends, Bunched LBs, Walked Safeties))
    Animation Duration: 4s
    Direct URL: https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=buddy-46-defense&play=b46-base-i-form

    [SUMMARY & TACTICAL PURPOSE]
    - Motive: Commit nine defenders to the box with walked safeties and bunched linebackers so any base run is met at or behind the line of scrimmage with a blocker-free defender.
    - Key Defender Put In Conflict: SS at 5 yards — the extra force player who turns every one-gap run into a two-hat fit
    - Why It Works: Offensive blocking rules cannot account for both walked safeties; the FB kick meets a squeezing end instead of a linebacker, and the ball carrier runs into a pre-built pile.
    - Failure Mode / Defensive Counter: Any completion beats zero coverage: with no deep safety, a double move or quick slant against isolated press corners is a touchdown threat.

    [SEQUENCING & GAME-PLAN LOGIC]
    - Sets Up: b46-mad-dog-double-a, b46-free-blade-weak-blitz
    - Plays Off: b46-ext-strong-combo
    - Visual Tell Cue: Both safeties aligned INSIDE the tackles at 5 and 8 yards — the pure 46 picture has no safety deeper than the linebackers’ original depth.

    [TIMELINE COACHING BEATS]
      * [T=0.0s] 1. The Eight-Man Box Picture: Both safeties are walked into the box at 5 and 8 yards with all three linebackers bunched at 2.5 yards. There is no deep-middle defender anywhere — the offense sees nine hats within 6 yards of the ball.
      * [T=1.0s] 2. Head-Up Ends Refuse to Be Reached: The 46 ends align head-up rather than shaded, so neither tackle nor the tight end can reach an outside shoulder. Both ends strike and squeeze, spilling any kick-out back into the bunched linebackers.
      * [T=2.2s] 3. NOSE Splits, Linebackers Scrape: The 0-tech nose absorbs the center-guard double team and splits it toward the ball, while MIKE rips over the guard climb and SAM scrapes behind the squeezing end. Every gap has two defenders.
      * [T=3.3s] 4. Ten Hats at the Football: The running back is met at the line by MIKE with SS and FS stacking in behind. The run never touches the second level — the defining picture of Buddy Ryan’s 46.

>>> PLAY: Double A-Gap Mad Dog Overload (ID: b46-mad-dog-double-a)
    Personnel: Base 46 Front (Mad Dog Mug)
    Formation: 46 Mad Dog vs Gun 21 Personnel 2x1 Right
    Situation: 3rd & 6, +38, passing down
    Defensive Look: Man-Free (Single-High Safety, Press Corners) (46 Double A-Gap Overload)
    Animation Duration: 4s
    Direct URL: https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=buddy-46-defense&play=b46-mad-dog-double-a

    [SUMMARY & TACTICAL PURPOSE]
    - Motive: Overload both A-gaps with walked defenders so the offense’s pass-protection slide cannot account for every interior threat, forcing an instant-pressure throw or sack.
    - Key Defender Put In Conflict: SS mugged over the strong A-gap — the blocker assigned to him cannot get depth fast enough
    - Why It Works: A single running back can pick up only one of the two A-gap knives, and the head-up end slant removes the tackle’s ability to help either guard.
    - Failure Mode / Defensive Counter: A quick perimeter throw (slant/flat) released on time beats the press corner before the interior knives arrive.

    [SEQUENCING & GAME-PLAN LOGIC]
    - Sets Up: b46-free-blade-weak-blitz
    - Plays Off: b46-base-i-form
    - Visual Tell Cue: Both A-gap defenders are standing upright at 1.2 yards staring across the line pre-snap — the base 46 keeps its safeties at 5 and 8 yards instead.

    [TIMELINE COACHING BEATS]
      * [T=0.0s] 1. The Mad Dog Picture: WILL and the strong safety stand mugged directly over both A-gaps at 1.2 yards with corners pressing outside. The offense must account for five immediate threats with only six protectors.
      * [T=0.8s] 2. Same-Gap Knives: Both A-gap defenders cross the guards’ inside shoulders simultaneously while the head-up end slants hard off the tight end. The center-guard doubles are left blocking air.
      * [T=1.8s] 3. Hot Window Slams Shut: The QB’s hot slant to X was the escape valve, but the island press corner rides it upfield while the safety blitz arrives before the third step lands.
      * [T=3.2s] 4. Buried Between Both Gaps: The NOSE has driven the center into the QB’s lap and the slanting end closes the scramble lane. Six rushers versus five blockers plus a scanning back ends one way.

>>> PLAY: Strong-Side E-X-T Combo Blitz (ID: b46-ext-strong-combo)
    Personnel: Base 46 Front (E-X-T Stagger)
    Formation: 46 E-X-T Combo vs Pro I-Form Strong Right
    Situation: 2nd & 9, +42, dropback pass
    Defensive Look: Man-Free with Free Hook (Single-High) (46 Strong-Side Combo Overload)
    Animation Duration: 4s
    Direct URL: https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=buddy-46-defense&play=b46-ext-strong-combo

    [SUMMARY & TACTICAL PURPOSE]
    - Motive: Send three staggered strong-side rushers (end-B gap, tackle-C loop, linebacker-edge) so one protection slide always leaves the second-wave looper unblocked.
    - Key Defender Put In Conflict: DT running the loop — his path is invisible until he bursts out of the crashing end’s trash
    - Why It Works: Offensive linemen block the first rusher they see; the crash occupies guard and tight end while the loop and edge arrive together on an uncovered tackle.
    - Failure Mode / Defensive Counter: A max-protect formation with a back releasing to the strong side adds the missing blocker and kills the loop’s timing.

    [SEQUENCING & GAME-PLAN LOGIC]
    - Sets Up: b46-mad-dog-double-a
    - Plays Off: b46-base-i-form, b46-free-blade-weak-blitz
    - Visual Tell Cue: The shaded tackle swings wide behind the crashing end rather than firing straight — pure interior slants never leave the box.

    [TIMELINE COACHING BEATS]
      * [T=0.0s] 1. The E-X-T Stack Call: The end is called into a hard B-gap crash, the shaded tackle is told to loop all the way around him to the outside, and SAM rushes the edge widest. Three staggered waves hit one protection gap.
      * [T=1.0s] 2. First Wave Occupies Two Blockers: The crashing end slams inside off the tight end and engages the right guard, eating both the guard and the tight-end chip while opening the arc behind him.
      * [T=2.2s] 3. The Loop Appears Out of Nowhere: The tackle has sprinted a full circle behind the crash and appears inside the right tackle just as SAM forces that tackle to widen. Protection has nobody left for him.
      * [T=3.4s] 4. Hit While Throwing: The QB feels the free runner and hurries his throw to the corner route; the looping tackle arrives mid-throw and the pass sails incomplete with FS waiting over the top.

>>> PLAY: Weak Free Blade Safety Blitz (ID: b46-free-blade-weak-blitz)
    Personnel: Base 46 Front (Free Blade Call)
    Formation: 46 Free Blade vs Gun 21 Personnel 2x1 Right
    Situation: 3rd & 5, +30, must-have stop
    Defensive Look: Man-Free Rolled (Corner Replaces Blitzing Safety) (46 Free Blade Weak Overload)
    Animation Duration: 4s
    Direct URL: https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=buddy-46-defense&play=b46-free-blade-weak-blitz

    [SUMMARY & TACTICAL PURPOSE]
    - Motive: Trade the free safety for a free weak-side runner while the boundary corner replaces him deep, keeping single-high shell integrity behind a five-man pressure.
    - Key Defender Put In Conflict: FS on the blade — unblocked by design because MIKE’s strong-side walk-up steals the running back’s scan
    - Why It Works: Protection rules send the back toward the walked-up linebacker, the hinge helps strong, and the blade hits the QB’s blind side before the third step.
    - Failure Mode / Defensive Counter: A back who scans weak first, or a max-protect six-man slide, leaves the FB waiting on the blade and turns pressure into a coverage deficit outside.

    [SEQUENCING & GAME-PLAN LOGIC]
    - Sets Up: None
    - Plays Off: b46-mad-dog-double-a, b46-ext-strong-combo
    - Visual Tell Cue: One safety at 8 yards directly over the weak guard with a corner pressed opposite — the base 46 keeps both safeties in the box and no corner ever bails from the middle of the field.

    [TIMELINE COACHING BEATS]
      * [T=0.0s] 1. The Blade Alignment: The free safety stands alone at 8 yards over the weak B-gap with MIKE walking up strong as a decoy. The offense keys MIKE and slides protection away from the real threat.
      * [T=1.0s] 2. Corner Rolls, Safety Fires: At the snap the boundary corner bails over his receiver to take the deep middle while the free safety shoots downhill through the weak B-gap off the guard’s outside hip.
      * [T=2.2s] 3. Hot Answer Walled Off: The QB’s hot slant to X dies instantly because the rolled-down strong safety carries it man-to-man, and the running back has already committed to the walked-up MIKE on the wrong side.
      * [T=3.4s] 4. Blind-Side Takedown: The hinge blocker spins around one full second too late; the blade arrives untouched and the rolled corner owns everything behind him. Zero risk, five-man pressure.

SCHEME FAMILY: DICK LEBEAU'S ZONE BLITZ FIRE ZONE FAMILY [ID: lebeau-fire-zone]
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Architect / Coach: Dick LeBeau
Organization / Team: Pittsburgh Steelers (1995-2014)
Category: DEFENSE
Tree Branch: lebeau-zone-blitz
Core Philosophy: The definitive zone-blitz system: true 5-man pressures where a defensive lineman or safety trades his rush lane for a rat/hook zone while replacement blitzers attack vacated gaps. Every call pairs 3-deep/3-under fire zone coverage behind disguised rotations from Cover 2 and single-high shells, forcing hot answers directly into dropped rushers.

PLAYS IN THIS SCHEME:

>>> PLAY: Triple Inside Fire Zone (ID: fz-triple-inside-fire)
    Personnel: 3-4 Fire Zone Nickel
    Formation: 11P Gun Spread 2x2 vs Odd Front Fire Zone
    Situation: 3rd & 7, midfield, obvious pass
    Defensive Look: Cover 3 Fire Zone (3-Deep / 3-Under) (Odd 50 Triple Fire Zone)
    Animation Duration: 4s
    Direct URL: https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=lebeau-fire-zone&play=fz-triple-inside-fire

    [SUMMARY & TACTICAL PURPOSE]
    - Motive: Generate true 5-man pressure with a double-A linebacker blast while a defensive end secretly trades his rush lane for the rat zone that swallows hot answers.
    - Key Defender Put In Conflict: RDE executing the rat trade drop
    - Why It Works: Offenses must account for six potential rushers with five blockers, so the hot progression fires directly into the vacated defender sitting in the intermediate window.
    - Failure Mode / Defensive Counter: The offensive line slides to pick up both A-gap blasts cleanly, leaving the QB a free boundary flat or the isolated weak-side slant against a one-high shell.

    [SEQUENCING & GAME-PLAN LOGIC]
    - Sets Up: fz-nose-drop-nasco
    - Plays Off: None
    - Visual Tell Cue: The strong end loosens his stance and takes a lateral first step rather than an upfield punch, signaling the trade before the ball is even thrown.

    [TIMELINE COACHING BEATS]
      * [T=0.4s] 1. The Double-A Blast: Both mugging linebackers trigger at full speed into opposite A-gaps. The Center and guards must split two simultaneous interior charges with no backside help committed.
      * [T=1.1s] 2. The Rat Trade: While five defenders swarm the pocket, the strong defensive end exits his rush lane on a smooth backward arc, trading his pass-rush rep for the free-release rat zone.
      * [T=2.3s] 3. The Dig Into the Teeth: The QB climbs the pocket and trusts his 12-yard dig to Z, unaware the vacated rusher is already squatting exactly where the route breaks.
      * [T=3.4s] 4. Interior Convergence Sack: With WILL occupying the running back protector, MIKE and NT converge on the step-up lane and bury the QB before the dig can develop.

>>> PLAY: Safety Rotate Fire Zone (ID: fz-safety-rotate-fire)
    Personnel: 3-4 Fire Zone Nickel
    Formation: 11P Gun Slot Right vs Two-High Disguise Shell
    Situation: 2nd & 8, +38, passing down
    Defensive Look: Cover 3 Rotation Fire Zone (3-Deep / 3-Under) (Odd Front Cover 2 Show)
    Animation Duration: 4s
    Direct URL: https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=lebeau-fire-zone&play=fz-safety-rotate-fire

    [SUMMARY & TACTICAL PURPOSE]
    - Motive: Show a static Cover 2 shell to bait quick-game answers, then rotate to single-high Cover 3 fire zone coverage behind five-man pressure.
    - Key Defender Put In Conflict: Strong safety executing the downhill rotation
    - Why It Works: Quick-game timing assumes two-deep help; when the shell rotates and an extra dog comes, the QB is squeezed between a disappearing window and a free blitzer.
    - Failure Mode / Defensive Counter: The offense tags a hot throw to the boundary flat before the rotation finishes, hitting the void left by the rolling safety.

    [SEQUENCING & GAME-PLAN LOGIC]
    - Sets Up: fz-safety-blitz-smoke
    - Plays Off: fz-triple-inside-fire
    - Visual Tell Cue: Both safeties start at equal nine-yard depths like true Cover 2 halves; the tell is the strong safety leaning forward in his pedal at the snap instead of backpedaling.

    [TIMELINE COACHING BEATS]
      * [T=0.3s] 1. The Cover 2 Illusion: Both safeties split the field at nine-plus yards and both corners press, painting a textbook two-deep shell that invites the quick slant-flat game.
      * [T=1.0s] 2. The Rotation Trigger: At the snap the strong safety sprints downhill while the free safety backpedals to the post and both corners flip their hips into a three-deep bail.
      * [T=2.0s] 3. The Five-Man Surge: With four linemen charging plus the WILL dogging the weak A-gap, the running back is caught scanning the wrong side and the interior gives way.
      * [T=3.2s] 4. Hit in the Rotation Window: The QB hesitates between his crosser and comeback, and the unblocked WILL arrives exactly in the gap created by the safety rotation.

>>> PLAY: Nose Drop Nasco (ID: fz-nose-drop-nasco)
    Personnel: 3-4 Fire Zone Base
    Formation: 21P Offset-I Right vs Odd Front Run Look
    Situation: 2nd & 6, red zone top, run-heavy tendencies
    Defensive Look: Cover 3 Fire Zone behind Nasco Exchange (Odd Front Nasco Slant Package)
    Animation Duration: 4s
    Direct URL: https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=lebeau-fire-zone&play=fz-nose-drop-nasco

    [SUMMARY & TACTICAL PURPOSE]
    - Motive: Bait a run-first protection with a light odd front, exchange the nose for an A-gap blitzing linebacker plus two inside-slanting OLBs, and cover the deep middle with the dropped nose himself.
    - Key Defender Put In Conflict: Nose tackle executing the nasco middle-hook drop
    - Why It Works: Every intermediate crosser funnels directly into the vacated nose spot now occupied by a coverage defender, while four rushers attack a protection built for three.
    - Failure Mode / Defensive Counter: The guards recognize the nose bailing instantly, slide clean to the inside slants, and the QB attacks the boundary flat before MIKE arrives.

    [SEQUENCING & GAME-PLAN LOGIC]
    - Sets Up: fz-triple-inside-fire
    - Plays Off: None
    - Visual Tell Cue: The zero-tech nose takes a lateral first step away from the Center rather than a contact punch, revealing the drop before the mesh is sold.

    [TIMELINE COACHING BEATS]
      * [T=0.3s] 1. The Light-Box Bait: The offense snaps against a zero-tech nose flanked by two wide stand-up backers, reading it as a light run-fit box perfect for inside zone.
      * [T=1.0s] 2. The Nasco Retreat: The nose slides smoothly backward off the line instead of engaging, vacating the A-gap while carving a retreat path between the incoming rush lanes.
      * [T=1.7s] 3. The Interior Slant Storm: Both outside linebackers slant violently inside through the B-gaps and MIKE dogs the abandoned A-gap, sending four chargers into a five-man protection.
      * [T=3.0s] 4. Crosser Into the Vacuum: The QB trusts his deep crosser behind the linebackers, only to find the dropped nose sitting exactly where every crossing route must die.

>>> PLAY: Safety Blitz Smoke (ID: fz-safety-blitz-smoke)
    Personnel: Nickel 4-2-5 Smoke Package
    Formation: 11P Gun Spread 2x2 vs Single-High Smoke
    Situation: 3rd & 5, +45, money down
    Defensive Look: Cover 1 Smoke with Corner Curl-Bait Trap (Even Front Safety Smoke)
    Animation Duration: 4s
    Direct URL: https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=lebeau-fire-zone&play=fz-safety-blitz-smoke

    [SUMMARY & TACTICAL PURPOSE]
    - Motive: Force an instant throw with a disguised safety blitz while the corner manufactures and then steals the curl window the QB is trained to trust.
    - Key Defender Put In Conflict: Boundary corner executing the curl-bait jump
    - Why It Works: The smoke pressure eliminates time for a full progression, and the pre-snap soft corner picture steers the hot read straight into a defender breaking downhill on the route.
    - Failure Mode / Defensive Counter: The QB recognizes the single-high rotation, throws the slot option early, or hits the running back flare into the void vacated by the blitzing safety.

    [SEQUENCING & GAME-PLAN LOGIC]
    - Sets Up: None
    - Plays Off: fz-safety-rotate-fire
    - Visual Tell Cue: Both safeties align deep like shell coverage, but the strong safety has his inside foot back and eyes locked on the guard-center tandem instead of the receivers.

    [TIMELINE COACHING BEATS]
      * [T=0.4s] 1. The Smoke Trigger: The strong safety explodes downhill from a disguised two-high look while the four-man line slants away from his lane, attacking the offense before the slide protection can set.
      * [T=1.2s] 2. The Curl Bait: The boundary corner retreats with exaggerated cushion, convincing the QB that the ten-yard curl to X sits in a wide-open zone window.
      * [T=2.4s] 3. The Jump: The moment the receiver plants on his curl, the corner flips from fake-bail into a full-speed downhill break, closing the very window he manufactured.
      * [T=3.4s] 4. The Trap Sprung: With the safety blitz forcing an instant throw, the ball sails directly into the jumping corner, who intercepts with nothing but green grass ahead.

SCHEME FAMILY: TONY DUNGY'S TAMPA 2 [ID: tampa-2]
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Architect / Coach: Tony Dungy
Organization / Team: Tampa Bay Buccaneers (1996-2001)
Category: DEFENSE
Tree Branch: two-deep-shell
Core Philosophy: The defining middle-of-field-closed Cover 2 of its era: a penetrating four-man rush behind corners who squat in the deep halves with underneath-first eyes, and safeties splitting the field. The signature wrinkle is the Mike linebacker converting his hook-curl drop into a full sprint to the deep-middle hole, erasing the seams that normally kill Cover 2. Quick perimeter answers are contested instantly, forcing quarterbacks to hold for seam throws that sail straight into the sprinting Mike.

PLAYS IN THIS SCHEME:

>>> PLAY: Base Tampa 2 vs 2x2 (ID: t2-base-vs-2x2)
    Personnel: Base 4-3
    Formation: Tampa 2 Shell vs Gun 11 Personnel 2x2
    Situation: 2nd & 7 from the 25, standard down
    Defensive Look: Cover 2 Tub (Mike Deep Hole) (Under Front (1-Tech Nose, 3-Tech Under Tackle))
    Animation Duration: 4s
    Direct URL: https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=tampa-2&play=t2-base-vs-2x2

    [SUMMARY & TACTICAL PURPOSE]
    - Motive: Flood the deep zones with five defenders while rushing only four, baiting offenses into the seams and erasing them with the Mike linebacker’s unique deep-middle conversion.
    - Key Defender Put In Conflict: MIKE turning his hook-curl drop into the deep-middle hole — the only defender who can erase both seams
    - Why It Works: Underneath-first corners contest every quick throw instantly, forcing the QB to hold for seams — exactly where the sprinting Mike arrives.
    - Failure Mode / Defensive Counter: A fast deep-middle flood of post-seam combinations occupying the Mike before he can turn and run.

    [SEQUENCING & GAME-PLAN LOGIC]
    - Sets Up: t2-roll-cover3-trips
    - Plays Off: t2-cloud-boundary
    - Visual Tell Cue: Both corners squat at 10 yards staring at the QB instead of trailing receivers vertically — cloud keeps its boundary corner pressed at 1 yard.

    [TIMELINE COACHING BEATS]
      * [T=0.0s] 1. The MOFC Two-High Picture: Only four men rush while both corners squat at 10-plus yards and the safeties split the halves. The middle of the field belongs to one man: the Mike linebacker.
      * [T=1.0s] 2. Seams Attacked on Both Halves: Both slots stem vertically into the classic Cover 2 seams — the void between the squatting corner and the safety half — while the QB climbs his five-step drop.
      * [T=2.0s] 3. Mike Turns and Runs the Hole: Reading the lock-on, the Mike converts his hook-curl drop into a dead sprint toward the back-center hole, erasing the seam the coverage is built to bait.
      * [T=3.4s] 4. Back-Center Interception: The seam throw sails directly into the sprinting Mike’s dive at the landmark — the signature Tampa 2 moment that turned picks into points.

>>> PLAY: SLB Edge Blitz Variant (ID: t2-slb-edge-blitz)
    Personnel: Base 4-3
    Formation: Tampa 2 Shell vs Gun 11 Personnel 2x1 Right
    Situation: 3rd & 5, +35, passing down
    Defensive Look: Cover 2 Tub w/ Edge Pressure (Under Front, SLB Edge Blitz (Sam/Will Exchange))
    Animation Duration: 4s
    Direct URL: https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=tampa-2&play=t2-slb-edge-blitz

    [SUMMARY & TACTICAL PURPOSE]
    - Motive: Add a fifth rusher off the edge without weakening the Tampa 2 structure by having the Will exchange directly into the Sam’s vacated hook-curl window.
    - Key Defender Put In Conflict: SAM off the edge — the tight end must take the inside LE, leaving the rim completely bare
    - Why It Works: The offense’s hot rule sends its quickest answer straight into the zone the blitzing defender just abandoned — where the Will is now waiting.
    - Failure Mode / Defensive Counter: A max-protect shift or back releases the back to the edge, turning the free runner into a blocked hat and stranding the exchange.

    [SEQUENCING & GAME-PLAN LOGIC]
    - Sets Up: t2-cloud-boundary
    - Plays Off: t2-base-vs-2x2
    - Visual Tell Cue: The Sam linebacker stands upright at 4 yards staring at the tackle’s outside shoulder — the base Tampa 2 keeps him stacked over the tight end at 4.5.

    [TIMELINE COACHING BEATS]
      * [T=0.0s] 1. The Walk-Up Edge Threat: SAM stands walked wide at 4 yards off the tight end with the four-man shell otherwise untouched — one extra body the protection math cannot hide.
      * [T=1.2s] 2. Free Rusher Off the Rim: The LE pins the tight end low so SAM turns the corner unblocked while the interior trio keeps the pocket compressed from the middle.
      * [T=2.0s] 3. The Zone Exchange Behind It: WILL has slid across into SAM’s vacated hook-curl, eyes jumping instantly to the designed hot answer in that exact window.
      * [T=3.0s] 4. Hot Answer Picked: The panic throw into Sam’s old zone lands in the exchanging WILL’s hands — pressure and coverage trading places in one call.

>>> PLAY: Cover 2 Roll to Cover 3 Sky vs Trips (ID: t2-roll-cover3-trips)
    Personnel: Base 4-3
    Formation: Tampa Shell vs Gun Trips Right (3x1)
    Situation: 2nd & 8, +30, tendency-down vs trips
    Defensive Look: Cover 2 Roll to Cover 3 Sky (Under Front, Weak-Side Rotation)
    Animation Duration: 4s
    Direct URL: https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=tampa-2&play=t2-roll-cover3-trips

    [SUMMARY & TACTICAL PURPOSE]
    - Motive: Answer a trips overload by rotating out of the baited two-high shell into three-deep coverage, trading one deep half for a middle-third eraser without weakening the flood side.
    - Key Defender Put In Conflict: FS spinning from his weak half to the deep middle third — the rotation that turns a flood beater into a contested throw
    - Why It Works: The offense keys the frozen two-safety picture and attacks the strength half, but the sky rotation has already replaced it with a sinking corner over the corner route.
    - Failure Mode / Defensive Counter: Late motion that flips the strength call after the rotation, stranding the rolling safety on the wrong side of the new flood.

    [SEQUENCING & GAME-PLAN LOGIC]
    - Sets Up: t2-base-vs-2x2
    - Plays Off: t2-cloud-boundary
    - Visual Tell Cue: The free safety starts drifting toward the hash mid-cadence while the strong safety tilts flat-side — base Tampa 2 keeps both safeties perfectly still until the snap.

    [TIMELINE COACHING BEATS]
      * [T=0.0s] 1. The Two-High Trips Shell: Tampa 2 halves are shown to a trips formation — the exact picture offenses tag as a flood beater, with both safeties frozen deep.
      * [T=0.9s] 2. Sky Rotation Away From the Weak Side: At the snap the free safety spins to the deep middle third while the strong safety sprints down to the flat — corners sink over the top into thirds.
      * [T=2.2s] 3. Flood Into Rotated Threes: The trips flood climbs exactly on schedule, but the corner route now rises into a deep third that did not exist before the snap, with MIKE closing the intermediate wall.
      * [T=3.4s] 4. Broken Up Over the Top: The sinking RCB arrives with the rotating FS bracketing behind — the flood finisher is swatted loose at its highest point.

>>> PLAY: Cloud Boundary Call (ID: t2-cloud-boundary)
    Personnel: Base 4-3
    Formation: Cloud Shell vs Gun 2x1 Boundary Left

    - Key Defender Put In Conflict: SS flashing down from his disguised half alignment — he is the one waiting in the flat the QB was promised
    - Why It Works: The pre-snap picture shows a soft corner over the slot; the exchange means that window is actually the safest-covered spot on the field.
    - Failure Mode / Defensive Counter: A deep over route through the vacated intermediate zone behind the dropping safety before MIKE can widen.

      * [T=0.8s] 2. The Cloud Exchange: At the snap the corner spins and bails while the safety breaks downhill — they swap responsibilities so smoothly the QB’s key never changes color.
      * [T=2.0s] 3. Quick Out Into a Waiting Flat: The H out is thrown exactly where a soft corner should be, only to find the exchanging safety sitting on the flat landmark with eyes on the QB.
      * [T=3.0s] 4. Pick in the Boundary Flat: The interception is secured as the bailed corner caps the vertical behind it — both halves of the exchange cashing on one snap.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
SCHEME FAMILY: TOM LANDRY'S FLEX DEFENSE [ID: landry-flex]
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Architect / Coach: Tom Landry
Organization / Team: Dallas Cowboys (1960-88)
Category: DEFENSE
Tree Branch: landry-dallas
Core Philosophy: The original positional-defense blueprint that ran in Dallas for three decades. Both tackles align one yard off the ball in a staggered flex, trading penetration for patient gap-zone occupation: linemen hold their lanes, linebackers shift strength with motion, and a guaranteed three-defender convergence swallows every point of attack before it develops.

PLAYS IN THIS SCHEME:

>>> PLAY: Standard Weak-Tackle Flex vs Power Sweep (ID: flex-weak-tackle-power-sweep)
    Personnel: Base 4-3 Flex (Weak DT Flexed)
    Formation: 21P Offset-I Right Power Sweep Left vs Flex
    Situation: 2nd & 5, +30, base run down
    Defensive Look: Cover 3 Sky behind flex front (4-3 Weak-Tackle Flex)
    Animation Duration: 4s
    Direct URL: https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=landry-flex&play=flex-weak-tackle-power-sweep

    [SUMMARY & TACTICAL PURPOSE]
    - Motive: Use the one-yard flex alignment to occupy blockers passively while three defenders converge independently on the sweep point of attack without needing a blocked lane.
    - Key Defender Put In Conflict: The flexed weak-side tackle on his free lateral chase
    - Why It Works: Sweep blocking schemes assign the playside guard to reach a defender who starts beyond his reach window, so the flexed tackle runs free down the line as a fourth pursuer.
    - Failure Mode / Defensive Counter: A crack return block by the receiver on the forcing corner removes the third converger and lets the sweep bounce cleanly outside.

    [SEQUENCING & GAME-PLAN LOGIC]
    - Sets Up: flex-tackle-tackle-two-back
    - Plays Off: None
    - Visual Tell Cue: The weak-side tackle aligns a visible yard off the line of scrimmage with hands free, unlike his strong-side partner who stays shaded on the snap.

    [TIMELINE COACHING BEATS]
      * [T=0.4s] 1. The Flex Picture: The weak tackle lines up a full yard off the ball, denying the guard an immediate target while giving himself an unobstructed runway parallel to the line of scrimmage.
      * [T=1.2s] 2. Sweep Flow Meets the Free Lane: As the sweep launches, the flexed tackle chases laterally down the line untouched because no blocker can reach him in time, while WILL triggers downhill immediately.
      * [T=2.0s] 3. The Edge Holds: The fullback kick-out is absorbed square by the defensive end, who turns the ball carrier back toward the pursuing wave instead of letting him turn the corner.
      * [T=3.2s] 4. Three-Defender Convergence: The flexed tackle chasing from inside, the triggering linebacker from depth, and the forcing corner from the perimeter all arrive simultaneously for a no-gain stop.

>>> PLAY: Tackle-Tackle Flex vs Two-Back (ID: flex-tackle-tackle-two-back)
    Personnel: Base 4-3 Flex (Both DTs Flexed)
    Formation: 22P I-Form Power Right vs Double Flex
    Situation: 1st & Goal, +8, power run down
    Defensive Look: Cover 3 Sky behind double flex (4-3 Tackle-Tackle Flex)
    Animation Duration: 4s
    Direct URL: https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=landry-flex&play=flex-tackle-tackle-two-back

    [SUMMARY & TACTICAL PURPOSE]
    - Motive: Occupy both interior gaps passively with flexed tackles who split double teams without needing to win, funneling two-back power into a patient three-defender kill zone.
    - Key Defender Put In Conflict: The flexed strong tackle executing the patient shed
    - Why It Works: Power schemes need their interior double teams to climb to the linebackers; starting a yard off the ball makes that climb impossible while the flexed defenders stay fresh and square.
    - Failure Mode / Defensive Counter: The offensive line changes the point of attack to quick trap or counter, catching the flexed tackles still releasing from their passive blocks.

    [SEQUENCING & GAME-PLAN LOGIC]
    - Sets Up: flex-lb-strength-shift-motion
    - Plays Off: flex-weak-tackle-power-sweep
    - Visual Tell Cue: Both defensive tackles hover a full yard off the ball with hands free pre-snap, unlike any standard shaded or nose alignment in the same front.

    [TIMELINE COACHING BEATS]
      * [T=0.4s] 1. The Double-Flex Picture: Both tackles align a full yard off the ball, so every interior blocker must travel an extra yard forward just to make contact, surrendering the battle before it starts.
      * [T=1.2s] 2. The Double Team That Cannot Climb: The center-guard combo reaches the flexed weak tackle already at depth, but he fights the split with low pads and neither blocker can climb to the second level.
      * [T=2.2s] 3. Patient Shed at the Point of Attack: The flexed strong tackle takes the down block standing tall, reads the ball declaration, and sheds precisely as the back hits the line of scrimmage.
      * [T=3.2s] 4. Three-Defender Convergence at POA: The shedding tackle, boxing Mike linebacker, and alley-filling strong safety meet simultaneously, stuffing the power before it reaches the second level.

>>> PLAY: Linebacker Strength Shift vs Motion (ID: flex-lb-strength-shift-motion)
    Personnel: Base 4-3 Flex (Both DTs Flexed)
    Formation: 11P Gun Slot Motion Right vs Shifting Flex
    Situation: 1st & 10, +25, formation-strength down
    Defensive Look: Cover 3 Sky behind strength shift (4-3 Double Flex with Shifting Backers)
    Animation Duration: 4s
    Direct URL: https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=landry-flex&play=flex-lb-strength-shift-motion

    [SUMMARY & TACTICAL PURPOSE]
    - Motive: Answer offensive formation-strength motion with a synchronized linebacker shift so the defense is never caught flowing cross-eyed into a perimeter run.
    - Key Defender Put In Conflict: The Mike linebacker executing the strength shift
    - Why It Works: Most defenses lose leverage when strength flips; Landry’s shift keeps every defender aligned to declared strength, so sweeps meet pre-positioned pursuit instead of reactive flow.
    - Failure Mode / Defensive Counter: A quick snap immediately after the motion catches the shift incomplete, leaving the old strength side soft to an inside zone hit.

    [SEQUENCING & GAME-PLAN LOGIC]
    - Sets Up: flex-line-game-rush
    - Plays Off: flex-tackle-tackle-two-back
    - Visual Tell Cue: The Mike takes visible sprint steps parallel to the line during the motion rather than shuffling, showing the shift is coached as a sprint-to-landmark rule.

    [TIMELINE COACHING BEATS]
      * [T=0.2s] 1. The Motion That Moves Both Sides: The slot receiver carries the motion across the formation, flipping the offensive strength, but the Dallas linebackers begin sliding in perfect sync before the ball is snapped.
      * [T=0.6s] 2. The Synchronized Shift: Mike sprints his shift to stack over the new play-side guard, Sam walks to the apex of the motioned slot, and the safety rotates to the sky half, preserving strength leverage everywhere.
      * [T=1.8s] 3. Sweeping Into Prepared Strength: The offense launches its flank sweep directly into the freshly shifted strength, running straight at defenders who moved there voluntarily.
      * [T=3.2s] 4. The Strength-Side Swarm: The chasing flexed tackle, shifted Mike, and forcing corner converge at the perimeter landmark, holding the sweep to a token gain.

>>> PLAY: Flex Line Game Pass Rush (ID: flex-line-game-rush)
    Personnel: Base 4-3 Flex (Both DTs Flexed)
    Formation: Pro Set Gun Spread vs Flexed Line Game
    Situation: 2nd & 8, +35, passing down
    Defensive Look: Cover 3 Sky behind the line game (4-3 Double Flex with Tackle-Tackle Game)
    Animation Duration: 4s
    Direct URL: https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=landry-flex&play=flex-line-game-rush

    [SUMMARY & TACTICAL PURPOSE]
    - Motive: Manufacture a free-edge rusher without blitzing by running a staggered slant-and-wrap line game out of the flexed tackle alignments.
    - Key Defender Put In Conflict: The strong tackle executing the slant-and-wrap
    - Why It Works: The flex alignment gives the tackles a runway to slant with momentum, and slide protection has no answer for a rusher who changes gaps after the pass is set — someone always blocks air.
    - Failure Mode / Defensive Counter: The tackle refuses the passed-off slant and keeps outside leverage, forcing the wrap wide and letting the QB escape up the middle.

    [SEQUENCING & GAME-PLAN LOGIC]
    - Sets Up: None
    - Plays Off: flex-lb-strength-shift-motion
    - Visual Tell Cue: The strong tackle widens his stance and leans inward during the cadence rather than firing straight ahead, betraying the slant half of the game.

    [TIMELINE COACHING BEATS]
      * [T=0.4s] 1. The Flexed First Punch: Both flexed tackles fire on the snap with staggered aims: the weak tackle explodes into the A-gap to glue the Center and guard, buying the space the second-level game needs to develop.
      * [T=1.3s] 2. Slant, Pass, Wrap: The strong tackle slants the B-gap, draws the tackle’s block down, then wraps flat behind the rush while the end replaces him inside — the classic Landry line game that turns four rushers into five threats.
      * [T=2.5s] 3. The Passed-Off Trap: The tackle chases the slant he was taught to take, but the wrapping defender is already turning the corner behind him, and the guard is late finding his new inside rusher.
      * [T=3.4s] 4. Two-Man Convergence Sack: The QB climbs away from the free wrapper directly into the replaced interior rusher, and the flexed line game finishes with a two-defender sack born entirely from alignment.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
SCHEME FAMILY: BUM PHILLIPS' TWO-GAP 3-4 [ID: phillips-two-gap-34]
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Architect / Coach: Bum Phillips
Organization / Team: Houston Oilers (1975-80)
Category: DEFENSE
Tree Branch: phillips-two-gap
Core Philosophy: The original two-gap 3-4 that Bum Phillips brought to the Houston Oilers: a zero-tech nose and twin 5-tech ends who ENGAGE and hold two gaps apiece rather than penetrate, occupying all five blockers so both inside linebackers can flow untouched over the tops of engaged bodies. The stand-up outside linebacker duo serves as the front's rush weapons — walking wide on passing downs, stemming across tackles' faces, and attacking rims the anchored interior keeps bare.

PLAYS IN THIS SCHEME:

>>> PLAY: Base Two-Gap Fits vs 21 Personnel (ID: b34-base-two-gap-fits)
    Personnel: Base Two-Gap 3-4
    Formation: Two-Gap Front vs Under-Center 21 Strong Right
    Situation: 2nd & 5 from the 30, base run-down
    Defensive Look: Single-High, Soft Corners vs Run (Two-Gap 3-4 (Zero Nose, Double 5-Techs))
    Animation Duration: 4s
    Direct URL: https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=phillips-two-gap-34&play=b34-base-two-gap-fits

    [SUMMARY & TACTICAL PURPOSE]
    - Motive: Trade penetration for total gap ownership — let linemen engage and control two gaps each so linebackers can run free over the top to every ball carrier.
    - Key Defender Put In Conflict: RILB scraping over the top — he arrives as the unblocked tackler precisely because the line ate every block
    - Why It Works: Engaged linemen guarantee no blocker is ever left unaccounted for, so the ball carrier always runs toward a flowing linebacker rather than a blocked hat.
    - Failure Mode / Defensive Counter: Reach blocks: if a tackle hooks an end off the line, the two-gap chain collapses and the scraper runs into open space.

    [SEQUENCING & GAME-PLAN LOGIC]
    - Sets Up: b34-dual-edge-interior-anchor
    - Plays Off: b34-stack-slant-shift
    - Visual Tell Cue: All three linemen stand square reading blockers instead of charging gaps — slant fronts explode sideways off this exact patient stance.

    [TIMELINE COACHING BEATS]
      * [T=0.0s] 1. The Two-Gap Geometry: Three linemen stand squared between gaps rather than shaded into them — each one is responsible for two gaps and plans to win by engagement, not penetration.
      * [T=1.0s] 2. Engage and Hold the Point: The nose absorbs a full double team while the strong end eats the tight-end clamp — every blocker is accounted for and none are moving backward.
      * [T=1.9s] 3. Linebackers Run the Ladder: With the line holding its blocks, both inside linebackers scrape OVER THE TOP of the engaged bodies instead of fighting through them.
      * [T=3.0s] 4. Funneled Into the Scrape: The setting edge forces the cutback inside exactly where the scraping RILB has arrived — the carrier meets the defense’s cleanest tackler.

>>> PLAY: Dual Edge Rush w/ Interior Anchor (ID: b34-dual-edge-interior-anchor)
    Personnel: Base Two-Gap 3-4
    Formation: Two-Gap Front vs Gun 11 Personnel 2x2
    Situation: 3rd & 6, +35, passing down
    Defensive Look: Man-Free, Press Corners, Walked WILL on Slot (Two-Gap 3-4, Dual Edge Rush)
    Animation Duration: 4s
    Direct URL: https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=phillips-two-gap-34&play=b34-dual-edge-interior-anchor

    [SUMMARY & TACTICAL PURPOSE]
    - Motive: Weaponize the two-gap front in reverse — let the immovable interior eat every blocker while both stand-up edges attack the rim from clean angles.
    - Key Defender Put In Conflict: ROLB bending inside under the tight-end hinge — the blocker braces outward for a speed rush that never comes straight
    - Why It Works: A stationary interior forces the pocket to step up directly into the converging pursuit paths of both edges.
    - Failure Mode / Defensive Counter: Quick perimeter throws released before either edge turns the corner or dips under his blocker.

    [SEQUENCING & GAME-PLAN LOGIC]
    - Sets Up: b34-wildcat-walk-up-edge
    - Plays Off: b34-base-two-gap-fits
    - Visual Tell Cue: Both stand-up backers walk to 2 yards in sprinter stances while the interior sits patient and squared — base fits keep backers stacked behind the line at 4 yards.

    [TIMELINE COACHING BEATS]
      * [T=0.0s] 1. The Dual Edge Threat: Both stand-up linebackers walk wide in pure rush postures flanking an interior sitting flat-footed — protection must split its attention in two directions.
      * [T=1.0s] 2. The Interior Anchor Eats Blocks: The zero nose takes a full double team without shedding while each end glues his tackle head-up — five blockers occupied by three immovable men.
      * [T=2.0s] 3. The Pincer Closes: With tackles pinned inward, both edges bend off their rims simultaneously — the pocket shrinks into a circle with nowhere to climb.
      * [T=3.0s] 4. Stepped Up Into the Wall: The QB climbs away from the rims directly into the anchored interior wall, where the converging duo swallows him for the sack.

>>> PLAY: Stack Slant Shift (ID: b34-stack-slant-shift)
    Personnel: Base Two-Gap 3-4
    Formation: Two-Gap Front vs Under-Center 21 Strong Right
    Situation: 3rd & 1 from the 38, short-yardage run-down
    Defensive Look: Single-High, Soft Corners vs Run (Two-Gap 3-4, Interior Slant Shift)
    Animation Duration: 4s
    Direct URL: https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=phillips-two-gap-34&play=b34-stack-slant-shift

    [SUMMARY & TACTICAL PURPOSE]
    - Motive: Disguise instant penetration inside a patient two-gap stance, then send all three linemen across blockers’ faces at once so every combo chases while linebackers replace behind.
    - Key Defender Put In Conflict: NG shooting across center into strong A — he lands exactly in the lead-blocker geometry of any strong-side run
    - Why It Works: Simultaneous inward movement turns every committed down block into a chase, and replacing linebackers guarantee the abandoned gaps stay occupied.
    - Failure Mode / Defensive Counter: Reach blocks hooking the slanting ends outward, springing the exact gaps the slant walked away from.

    [SEQUENCING & GAME-PLAN LOGIC]
    - Sets Up: b34-base-two-gap-fits
    - Plays Off: b34-dual-edge-interior-anchor
    - Visual Tell Cue: The interior trio tilts and staggers its steps during the cadence before exploding inward — base two-gap fits sit flat-footed reading blocks.

    [TIMELINE COACHING BEATS]
      * [T=0.0s] 1. The Patient Stack Bait: The interior trio sits squared in two-gap stances inviting double teams — the offense commits its combos against defenders who are about to leave.
      * [T=0.7s] 2. Three Bodies Cross Inward: Nose and both ends explode across their blockers’ faces simultaneously, collapsing into the A and B gaps before any combo can climb or adjust.
      * [T=2.0s] 3. Linebackers Replace Behind the Slant: Both inside backers fill the gaps the slant abandoned — no vacated space ever exists even though three linemen just moved.
      * [T=3.0s] 4. Head-On in Strong B: The lead blocker arrives to find the slanting nose already in his aiming point while the squeezing edge funnels the carrier into the pile.

>>> PLAY: Wildcat Walk-Up Edge (ID: b34-wildcat-walk-up-edge)
    Personnel: Base Two-Gap 3-4
    Formation: Two-Gap Front vs Gun 11 Personnel 2x2
    Situation: 2nd & 8 from the 42, passing down
    Defensive Look: Man-Free, Press Corners, Walked WILL on Slot (Two-Gap 3-4, Wildcat Edge Stem)
    Animation Duration: 4s
    Direct URL: https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=phillips-two-gap-34&play=b34-wildcat-walk-up-edge

    [SUMMARY & TACTICAL PURPOSE]
    - Motive: Break the tackle’s pass-protection key by walking between alignments and stances across his face, then attack whichever gap his eyes abandoned last.
    - Key Defender Put In Conflict: ROLB stemming across the tackle’s face — every alignment change forces a reset the rusher never has to make himself
    - Why It Works: Pass protection keys off the widest alignment, so a defender who keeps changing it guarantees the blocker eventually guesses wrong once.
    - Failure Mode / Defensive Counter: Chip help from the back or tight end erasing the free inside lane the stem created.

    [SEQUENCING & GAME-PLAN LOGIC]
    - Sets Up: b34-base-two-gap-fits
    - Plays Off: b34-dual-edge-interior-anchor
    - Visual Tell Cue: The strong edge keeps switching between a two-point walk and a three-point sprinter stance across the tackle’s face — base fits park him stacked at 4 yards and leave him there.

    [TIMELINE COACHING BEATS]
      * [T=0.0s] 1. The Wildcat Walk Begins: The strong edge stands wide at 2.5 yards in a two-point stare, already moving — every alignment change he makes costs the tackle one mental reset.
      * [T=1.0s] 2. Stem Draws the Tackle Wide: A full-speed stem tight over the tackle drags the set outward, then the bounce back wide forces a second reset before the snap count even finishes.
      * [T=1.9s] 3. Inside Dart Through the Guess: On the next reset the walker darts inside instead — attacking the B-gap the tackle’s eyes abandoned while the interior anchors keep the pocket sealed.
      * [T=3.1s] 4. Flush and Finish: The free inside burst flushes the QB directly into the looping contain rusher — the walk created the sack without ever beating a block.

SCHEME FAMILY: JIMMY JOHNSON'S SPEED 4-3 [ID: jj-speed-43]
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Architect / Coach: Jimmy Johnson
Organization / Team: Dallas Cowboys (1989-93) / Miami Hurricanes
Category: DEFENSE
Tree Branch: landry-dallas
Core Philosophy: Undersized hyper-fast linemen who fire upfield at the snap instead of reading blocks, trading two-gap size for one-gap penetration chaos that wrecks blocking rules before they form. Behind the slanting front sits man-free or single-high coverage with pressed corners on islands, so every pressured throw has nowhere soft to land. The scheme finishes plays with the Miami chase rule: relentless, assigned pursuit angles that swallow ballcarriers from sideline to sideline.

PLAYS IN THIS SCHEME:

>>> PLAY: Penetration Slant Loop (ID: jj43-penetration-slant-loop)
    Personnel: Base 4-3 Speed
    Formation: 11P Gun Spread 2x2 vs Even Speed Front
    Situation: 3rd & 6, +42, passing down
    Defensive Look: Cover 3 Buzz behind the slant-loop game (Even 4-3 with Strong-Side Slant Loop)
    Animation Duration: 4s
    Direct URL: https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=jj-speed-43&play=jj43-penetration-slant-loop

    [SUMMARY & TACTICAL PURPOSE]
    - Motive: Win with pure penetration and staggered timing: tackles slant to occupy blockers while a delayed end loops through the gap their charge creates.
    - Key Defender Put In Conflict: The weak end executing the delayed loop
    - Why It Works: Slide protection must commit to the first visible threats, so the half-beat stagger guarantees one rusher arrives unblocked exactly where the protection has already left.
    - Failure Mode / Defensive Counter: The running back keeps eyes inside and picks up the looper, leaving the quarterback a clean three-step throw to the flat valve.

    [SEQUENCING & GAME-PLAN LOGIC]
    - Sets Up: jj43-man-free-will-dog
    - Plays Off: None
    - Visual Tell Cue: The looping end takes two visible upfield steps and visibly gathers himself before redirecting inside — pure slant teams never pull off the arc.

    [TIMELINE COACHING BEATS]
      * [T=0.4s] 1. The First Wave Slants: Both defensive tackles fire instantly into the strong A and B gaps with a deliberate half-beat stagger, gluing the sliding offensive line to blocks it was already preparing to make.
      * [T=1.2s] 2. The Delayed Loop Begins: The weak end sells two steps of edge rush to pin the tackle and back, then pulls off the arc and starts his loop — Jimmy Johnson’s signature stagger that separates this stunt from every standard slant.
      * [T=2.4s] 3. Protection Arithmetic Fails: The slide protection accounts for the two visible slants and the containment rusher; the delayed looper is the sixth man in a five-man math problem, arriving through the vacated weak A-gap.
      * [T=3.4s] 4. Loop Convergence Sack: The stepping-up quarterback walks directly into the looping end while the B-gap tackle pushes the guard backward, finishing the penetration-first philosophy in a single picture.

>>> PLAY: Man-Free Will Dog (ID: jj43-man-free-will-dog)
    Personnel: Nickel 4-2-5 Man-Free
    Formation: 11P Gun Slot Right vs Press Man-Free
    Situation: 3rd & 5, +25, must-have down
    Defensive Look: Cover 1 with A-gap Will Dog (Even 4-3 Nickel Dog Look)
    Animation Duration: 4s
    Direct URL: https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=jj-speed-43&play=jj43-man-free-will-dog

    [SUMMARY & TACTICAL PURPOSE]
    - Motive: Create guaranteed interior pressure with a single A-gap dog while man-free coverage eliminates every hot answer behind it.
    - Key Defender Put In Conflict: The Will linebacker triggering the A-gap dog
    - Why It Works: A mug-aligned blitzer covers five yards faster than a sliding lineman recovers, and pressed corners take away exactly the quick throws offenses use to beat dogs.
    - Failure Mode / Defensive Counter: The guard slide-releases to the dog instantly and the back protects the edge, giving the QB a free throwing lane to the slant.

    [SEQUENCING & GAME-PLAN LOGIC]
    - Sets Up: jj43-miami-chase-rule-pursuit
    - Plays Off: jj43-penetration-slant-loop
    - Visual Tell Cue: Will lines up in a true two-point mug stance with inside foot back, cocked to fire — the loop game shows a four-point rush posture instead.

    [TIMELINE COACHING BEATS]
      * [T=0.4s] 1. The Instant Trigger: Will fires at the snap from his mug alignment, splitting Center and guard before either can react — Jimmy Johnson’s speed defense turns a five-step protection call into a race the line has already lost.
      * [T=1.2s] 2. Mike Peels, Picture Flips: Mike showed the second dog all week’s film, then peels to the back at the snap, so every eligible receiver is matched and there is no soft spot in the man-free picture.
      * [T=2.2s] 3. The Hot Route Under Siege: The slot slant is the designed beater, but the pressed nickel reroutes it inside and the quarterback feels the dog arriving before his eyes finish the progression.
      * [T=3.4s] 4. Dog Finishes the Escape: The quarterback tries to climb away from the A-gap and Will runs him down from behind, completing the sack that pure coverage could never guarantee.

>>> PLAY: Miami Chase Rule Pursuit (ID: jj43-miami-chase-rule-pursuit)
    Personnel: Base 4-3 Speed
    Formation: Pro Set Wing Sweep Right vs Even Speed Front
    Situation: 1st & 10, own 35, first-quarter perimeter test
    Defensive Look: Cover 3 Sky with run-fit chase rules (Even 4-3 Flowing Front)
    Animation Duration: 4.2s
    Direct URL: https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=jj-speed-43&play=jj43-miami-chase-rule-pursuit

    [SUMMARY & TACTICAL PURPOSE]
    - Motive: Turn perimeter runs into short gains by having all eleven defenders execute assigned pursuit angles rather than chasing the football.
    - Key Defender Put In Conflict: The strong safety filling the alley as the second hat
    - Why It Works: Every defender has a geometric landmark instead of a ball target, so the convergence point forms ahead of the runner regardless of how fast the play gets to the edge.
    - Failure Mode / Defensive Counter: A single defender breaks his landmark and chases the ball, opening the cutback lane the cross-facing Will is counting on him to erase.

    [SEQUENCING & GAME-PLAN LOGIC]
    - Sets Up: jj43-goal-line-haley-edge-rush
    - Plays Off: jj43-man-free-will-dog
    - Visual Tell Cue: The backside end takes visibly flat steps down the line of scrimmage instead of angling upfield — the chase rule targets a spot, not the runner.

    [TIMELINE COACHING BEATS]
      * [T=0.5s] 1. The Chase Rule Declares: The moment sweep flow shows, every defender executes a pre-assigned pursuit rule — the backside end runs down the line of scrimmage through the tailback’s original spot, not to the football.
      * [T=1.4s] 2. Spill Forces Width: The playside tackle spills the drive block and the end holds the edge, forcing the ball carrier wider than his intended landmark and directly toward waiting pursuit angles.
      * [T=2.4s] 3. Three Angles, One Point: Sam takes the inside-out angle from the box, Mike runs deeper than the ball through the guard’s original alignment, and the corner locks inside-out force at the numbers.
      * [T=3.4s] 4. The Miami Swarm: Five defenders converge at one coordinate from five different angles, tackling with shared responsibility exactly as Jimmy Johnson taught at Miami — pursuit is a system, not effort.

>>> PLAY: Goal-Line Haley Edge Rush (ID: jj43-goal-line-haley-edge-rush)

      * [T=1.3s] The Interior Slants Pin Four Blockers: The tackles stagger their slants into strong A and strong B while the weak end crashes off the snap, gluing Center, both guards, and the snapping tight end to blocks they cannot leave.
      * [T=2.3s] Haley Wins the Solo Edge: The tight end snapped down instead of helping outside, leaving the right tackle alone against Charles Haley’s hand-down burst; one stab and a speed-bull later the edge is gone.
      * [T=3.5s] Corner Crush at the Stripe: The climbing quarterback steps away from the interior surge directly into Haley’s flatten, and the ball comes out at the goal line — penetration philosophy cashed into points.

SCHEME FAMILY: BILL BELICHICK'S OKIE/BEAR PACKAGE [ID: belichick-okie-bear]
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Architect / Coach: Bill Belichick
Organization / Team: New England Patriots (2003-19)
Category: DEFENSE
Tree Branch: belichick-flores
Core Philosophy: The compressed odd-front situational package Belichick deployed to bury Peyton Manning-era Colts offenses. A zero-tech nose flanked by double 4i tackles and stacked 5-tech ends gives New England five interior bodies against five interior blockers, while both inside linebackers mug over the A-gaps and the safeties crowd the box. Zero-nose geometry plus double-A mug threats stress every hot answer, bridging old goal-line fronts to modern mug-pressure packages.

PLAYS IN THIS SCHEME:

>>> PLAY: Goal-Line Bear vs Heavy Personnel (ID: bear-goal-line-heavy)
    Personnel: Okie/Bear Package (5 DL, 2 LB, 4 DB)
    Formation: Bear Front vs Goal-Line Heavy I-Form
    Situation: 4th & Goal from the 1, fourth quarter
    Defensive Look: Press Match, Safeties Near Box (Bear Front (0-Nose, Double 4is, 5-Tech Ends))
    Animation Duration: 4s
    Direct URL: https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=belichick-okie-bear&play=bear-goal-line-heavy

    [SUMMARY & TACTICAL PURPOSE]
    - Motive: Match heavy goal-line personnel with an extra interior body so every gap is two-gapped and no puller or kicker can find a clean block.
    - Key Defender Put In Conflict: NOSE on the zero — he alone erases both A-gaps and frees the linebackers to play downhill
    - Why It Works: Five-down interior fronts eliminate angle blocking; the FB lead arrives to find the linebacker already occupying his aiming point.
    - Failure Mode / Defensive Counter: Getting reached: if a combo moves a 4i off the line, the mugged backers are blocked and the goal-line math flips.

    [SEQUENCING & GAME-PLAN LOGIC]
    - Sets Up: bear-double-a-mug
    - Plays Off: bear-to-46-stem-disguise
    - Visual Tell Cue: Five defenders within one yard of the ball with safeties at just 4.5 yards — the okie nickel look spreads its safeties wider and deeper.

    [TIMELINE COACHING BEATS]
      * [T=0.0s] 1. The Goal-Line Bear Picture: A zero-tech nose flanked by double 4i tackles and both ends stacked at 5-technique gives New England five interior-body defenders against five interior blockers — no reach blocks are available anywhere.
      * [T=0.9s] 2. Mugged Backers Behind the Wall: Both inside linebackers stand directly over the A-gaps at 3.4 yards with the safeties bracketing them at 4.5. Every gap inside the tackles is doubled before the ball is snapped.
      * [T=2.0s] 3. Power Meets the Wall: The fullback leads into strong A but WILL has already shot the gap behind the fighting 4i; the tight-end kick is spilled by the squeezing end straight into the forcing safety.
      * [T=3.2s] 4. Stuffed Short of the Goal: The back hits the line to find the nose controlling both A-gaps, four defenders stacking in the hole, and no cutback lane — the Bear package wins its specialty snap.

>>> PLAY: Third-and-1 Double-A Mug Blitz (ID: bear-double-a-mug)

    - Why It Works: The Bear wall occupies all five blockers, so each mugged backer meets only one scanning back, and island press delays every perimeter answer past the pressure clock.

      * [T=0.9s] 2. Same-Gap Knives Behind the Wall: Both backers cross the guards’ inside shoulders simultaneously while the zero-nose drives the center and both 4is angle into the B gaps behind them.
      * [T=1.9s] 3. The Hot Window Never Opens: The designed hot slant to H demands the ball out in 1.5 seconds, but the scanning back took the wrong knife and WILL has already cleared the guard’s hands.
      * [T=3.0s] 4. Swallowed on Third-and-One: The free-runner hit from strong A buries the QB behind the line of scrimmage and forces the long field-goal unit onto the field.

>>> PLAY: Bear-to-46 Stem Disguise (ID: bear-to-46-stem-disguise)
    Personnel: Okie/Bear Package (5 DL, 2 LB, 4 DB)
    Formation: Okie Shell vs Gun 12 Personnel Compressed
    Situation: 3rd & 2, red zone, run-check down
    Defensive Look: Stem to Press Match, Eight-Man Box (Bear Front Stemming into Full 46)
    Animation Duration: 4.5s
    Direct URL: https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=belichick-okie-bear&play=bear-to-46-stem-disguise

    [SUMMARY & TACTICAL PURPOSE]
    - Motive: Show a light okie shell to invite an inside-run check, then complete a cadence-length stem into a full 46 eight-man box before the ball carrier can redirect.
    - Key Defender Put In Conflict: SS walking from 8.5 yards into a strong-B mug — his arrival converts a two-deep picture into nine bodies at the line
    - Why It Works: The offense commits its protection slide and aiming points against the pre-snap shell; by the time the box is revealed, the dive is already declared.
    - Failure Mode / Defensive Counter: A quick or silent count snapping the ball before the stem finishes, stranding walked safeties outside the box.

    [SEQUENCING & GAME-PLAN LOGIC]
    - Sets Up: bear-double-a-mug
    - Plays Off: bear-goal-line-heavy
    - Visual Tell Cue: Both safeties are moving downhill during the cadence with backers tightening behind them — the settled goal-line Bear never moves until the snap.

    [TIMELINE COACHING BEATS]
      * [T=0.0s] 1. The Disguised Okie Shell: Both safeties split at 8-9 yards with linebackers floating at 4 — the picture reads standard okie nickel spacing, not an eight-man box.
      * [T=0.9s] 2. Stemming Through the Cadence: Both safeties sprint downhill while the backers tighten behind them; eight defenders converge inside the tackles as the ball is snapped.
      * [T=2.2s] 3. The Eight-Man Box Revealed: The final picture is full 46 geometry — five linemen, tightened backers, and both walked safeties mugging the interior gaps with no numbers advantage anywhere.
      * [T=3.4s] 4. Dive Into a Wall: The checked dive hits strong A/B to find the walked safety and WILL stacked there — the stem converted a light shell into its specialty snap.
