SCHEME FAMILY: DAVE ARANDA'S TITE FRONT & PESO PACKAGE [ID: aranda-tite-peso]
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Architect / Coach: Dave Aranda
Organization / Team: LSU DC (2016-19) / Baylor HC
Category: DEFENSE
Tree Branch: college-defensive-fronts
Core Philosophy: A 4i-0-4i box that eliminates both B-gaps before the snap, forcing spread runs to bounce into walked-down hybrid defenders. Peso nickel/dime personnel blur the line between back-end and box — apex linebackers split the #2-receiver-to-tackle lines, split-field quarters pattern-matches every slot, and three-man simulated pressures occupy the quarterback’s escape lanes with defenders who were never rushing at all.

PLAYS IN THIS SCHEME:

>>> PLAY: Base Tite vs 11P Zone Read (ID: tite-base-zone-read)
    Personnel: Peso Nickel (4 DL + 2 LB + Hybrid DB-LB)
    Formation: 11P Gun, TE Strong Right (Zone Read)
    Situation: 2nd & 6, +30, spread run down
    Defensive Look: Split-Field Quarters (Cover 4) (Tite Front (4i-0-4i Box))
    Animation Duration: 4s
    Direct URL: https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=aranda-tite-peso&play=tite-base-zone-read

    [SUMMARY & TACTICAL PURPOSE]
    - Motive: Eliminate every interior gap with the 4i-0-4i box so a spread-run play must bounce to the perimeter, where the walked-down peso waits as the unblockable extra defender.
    - Key Defender Put In Conflict: PESO nickel — the DB-LB hybrid whose walk-down turns a blocked-even run picture into a plus-one box
    - Why It Works: Zone read rules force the offense to leave a 4i unblocked, but the tite spacing means the read key squeezes instead of chasing, and the pulling quarterback’s lane is owned by a defender the run game cannot account for.
    - Failure Mode / Defensive Counter: Pitch or perimeter constraint plays: once the box eats the interior, offenses flip to speed option and quick throws at the vacated nickel flat.

    [SEQUENCING & GAME-PLAN LOGIC]
    - Sets Up: tite-sim-pressure
    - Plays Off: tite-quarters-apex
    - Visual Tell Cue: Both interior defenders aligned INSIDE the tackles (4i shades) rather than head-up or wide — the pure tite picture has no defender in either C-gap pre-snap.

    [TIMELINE COACHING BEATS]
      * [T=0.0s] 1. The Tite Box Picture: Two 4i techniques sit on the guards’ outside shoulders with a head-up nose between them — both B-gaps are doubled before the snap. The apex linebackers split the tackle-to-#2 lines while the peso nickel hovers ready to walk down.
      * [T=1.0s] 2. Zone Flow Meets Two Squeezing 4is: As the line reaches right, both 4is attack inside shoulders rather than chasing flow. Neither guard can reach a defender who refuses to be widened, so the reach blocks are already failing at the second step.
      * [T=2.2s] 3. Nose Anchors, Peso Becomes the Plus-One: The nose splits the center-guard double team while the walked-down peso defeats the tight end’s arc. The offense left the 4i unblocked expecting numbers; the nickel walking down erases that math.
      * [T=3.3s] 4. The Pulled Ball Runs Into the Nickel: The quarterback pulls on the squeeze exactly as coached, but his keep lane now belongs to the peso with WILL scraping behind. The read was honest — the front simply had an extra hat the offense could not block.

>>> PLAY: Tite 4 Simulated Pressure (ID: tite-sim-pressure)
    Personnel: Peso Nickel (4 DL + 2 LB + Hybrid DB-LB)
    Formation: 11P Gun, TE Weak Left (Slant-Flat Right)
    Situation: 3rd & 4, +38, obvious pass down
    Defensive Look: Sim Pressure — Man-Free With Hole Dropper (Tite Front (4i-0-4i Box, Mug Mike))
    Animation Duration: 4s
    Direct URL: https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=aranda-tite-peso&play=tite-sim-pressure

    [SUMMARY & TACTICAL PURPOSE]
    - Motive: Flash a five-man pressure from the tite box, rush only three, and occupy the quarterback’s scramble lane with a defensive end who replaces the blitzing Mike before dropping into the hook.
    - Key Defender Put In Conflict: LE — the 4i whose fake rush converts a blocked pass-rusher into the hook-zone dropper sitting exactly where the quarterback escapes
    - Why It Works: Protection counts the walked Mike and the charging interior trio, so five blockers chase four threats; when pressure forces movement, the only soft area already belongs to the replacing end.
    - Failure Mode / Defensive Counter: Rhythm quick throws released before the cross develops — if the ball is out on time the defense rushed three and played light everywhere else.

    [SEQUENCING & GAME-PLAN LOGIC]
    - Sets Up: tite-bear-condensed
    - Plays Off: tite-base-zone-read
    - Visual Tell Cue: Both Mike and dime mugged over the weak A-gap while neither 4i widened — the walk-up says blitz, but no edge defender moved, the signature of a three-rush sim.

    [TIMELINE COACHING BEATS]
      * [T=0.0s] 1. The Mug Show: The Mike and the dime are both walked to a yard over the weak A-gap while the tite box stays compressed — the picture screams five-man fire. The offense slides protection left and puts the back on the walked defenders.
      * [T=1.0s] 2. Three Go, One Replaces: Only three rushers actually come: the Mike fires the weak A-gap while the nose and 4i squeeze interior. The other weak 4i slants two steps behind the blitz, then stops — he is not rushing at all.
      * [T=2.2s] 3. The Replace Drop: The end settles exactly where the blitzing Mike came from, turning the vacated rush lane into an occupied hook zone. Every escape lane the quarterback was taught to climb into now has a body in it.
      * [T=3.3s] 4. Escape Lane Erased: Flushed by the three-man rush, the quarterback steps up into the replaced hook and his throw is tipped at the line of the drop. The defense rushed fewer men than the offense blocked for — and still won the down.

>>> PLAY: Quarters Apex Adjustment vs 2x2 (ID: tite-quarters-apex)
    Personnel: Peso Dime (4 DL + 2 LB + Rover + 4 DB)
    Formation: 10P Gun 2x2 Spread (Mesh Concept)
    Situation: 3rd & 5, midfield, spread passing down
    Defensive Look: Split-Field Quarters With Apex Match (Tite Front (4i-0-4i Box, Apex Overload))
    Animation Duration: 4s
    Direct URL: https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=aranda-tite-peso&play=tite-quarters-apex

    [SUMMARY & TACTICAL PURPOSE]
    - Motive: Give every slot receiver both an underneath apex defender and a matching quarter safety so a two-by-two mesh concept can never isolate anyone or occupy both deep halves.
    - Key Defender Put In Conflict: SS — the strong quarter whose carry rule converts the seam into a double team the moment Y goes vertical
    - Why It Works: Quarters pattern-match rules answer every #2 route automatically: vertical gets carried, underneath gets sunk behind, and the apexes play man through the middle while the rover robs the mesh point.
    - Failure Mode / Defensive Counter: Attacking the light box before routes develop — only three linemen and two apex defenders stand between the quarterback and an inside run or quick pressure.

    [SEQUENCING & GAME-PLAN LOGIC]
    - Sets Up: tite-base-zone-read
    - Plays Off: tite-sim-pressure
    - Visual Tell Cue: Both linebackers aligned directly OVER the slots at apex depth instead of stacked in the B-gap boxes — the pure quarters-overload picture reserved for two-by-two.

    [TIMELINE COACHING BEATS]
      * [T=0.0s] 1. Apex Overload on Both Twos: Against two-by-two, both apex backers align directly over the slots rather than in B-gaps, giving each #2 receiver an underneath defender plus a matching quarter safety. The tite box stays intact behind them.
      * [T=1.0s] 2. Seam Meets the Carry Rule: The strong slot releases vertical and the strong quarter immediately carries — quarters means the safety takes all vertical #2s. MIKE walls the seam from underneath, building an instant double team.
      * [T=2.2s] 3. Underneath #2 Sinks the Weak Quarter: The weak slot drags under, flipping the weak quarter’s read: #2 under means sink, not chase. He drops to the deep quarter while the apex turns and runs with the crosser man-to-man.
      * [T=3.3s] 4. The Crosser Runs Into the Rob: The quarterback forces the drag a beat late and the ball arrives into a three-defender convergence: trailing apex, robbing peso, sinking quarter behind. Every window the mesh tried to create already had a name on it.

>>> PLAY: Bear Adjustment vs Condensed Twins (ID: tite-bear-condensed)
    Personnel: Peso Dime (4 DL + 2 LB + Hybrid Walk-Downs)
    Formation: 11P Gun, Condensed Twins Strong Right
    Situation: 2nd & 4, red zone top, condensed-run down
    Defensive Look: Man Under With Single-High Post (Bear Adjustment (Condensed Tite Box))
    Animation Duration: 4s
    Direct URL: https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=aranda-tite-peso&play=tite-bear-condensed

    [SUMMARY & TACTICAL PURPOSE]
    - Motive: Answer condensed splits by tipping the tite box into a bear look, doubling every interior gap and walking hybrid defenders onto the twins so gap-scheme runs die at the line and quick game gets pressed.
    - Key Defender Put In Conflict: EDGE — the head-up end whose inside slip of the kick-out turns the puller’s lead block into an empty lane for MIKE
    - Why It Works: Condensed formations invite gap runs with kick-out logic; the bear tip spills every kick, funnels the ball carrier into the filled apex, and puts pressed defenders on the twins to erase the perimeter answers.
    - Failure Mode / Defensive Counter: Horizontal detachment: jet sweep, wide pin-pull, and quick screens test whether the walked-down hybrids can scrape fast enough to defend space outside the compressed box.

    [SEQUENCING & GAME-PLAN LOGIC]
    - Sets Up: tite-quarters-apex
    - Plays Off: tite-base-zone-read
    - Visual Tell Cue: Both 4is slid OUTSIDE their base shades with apexes cheated to 3.5 yards — four hats within a yard of the LOS versus three in the pure tite picture.

    [TIMELINE COACHING BEATS]
      * [T=0.0s] 1. Condensed Twins Demand a Bear Answer: The offense compresses its splits, so the tite box answers by tipping into a bear look: four linemen within a yard of the ball, both apexes cheated down, and peso plus dime walked onto the twins. Eight defenders live between the tackles.
      * [T=1.0s] 2. The Puller Meets a Squeezing Edge: The guard pulls into a hole that is already closing. The tight end fires his kick-out but the head-up end slips it inside rather than taking the block head-on — classic bear-front spilling that turns the puller’s lead into decoration.
      * [T=2.2s] 3. Walked Peso Forcing From the Condensed Side: On the perimeter, the walked peso triggers downhill and defeats the slot’s crack, while dime shields the alley safety. The condensed-side quick-game answers are jammed before they can threaten.
      * [T=3.3s] 4. Power Dies in the Eight-Man Box: The back hits the line exactly where the design wanted — and finds the spilled kick, the funneling 4i, and the filling Mike stacked in one gap. The alley safety arrives as the ninth hat for a tackle at the line.

SCHEME FAMILY: ROCKY LONG'S 3-3-5 STACK [ID: rlong-335-stack]
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Architect / Coach: Rocky Long
Organization / Team: San Diego State (2011-19) / New Mexico
Category: DEFENSE
Tree Branch: college-defensive-fronts
Core Philosophy: Three down linemen with all three linebackers stacked directly behind them at identical depth, so no offense can read gap responsibility pre-snap. Five defensive backs play every down against any formation. The call is pressure-by-committee: slant-exchange games move all six box defenders one gap at a time, edge storms fire from both C-gaps, safeties and corners cross-dog through vacated lanes, and empty sets meet an all-out zero with straight man coverage behind.

PLAYS IN THIS SCHEME:

>>> PLAY: Base Stack Slant Exchange (ID: stack335-slant-exchange)
    Personnel: Base 3-3-5 Stack (3 DL + 3 LB + 5 DB)
    Formation: Pro I-Form Strong Right vs Stack
    Situation: 1st & 10, +30, base run down
    Defensive Look: Cover 3 Behind the Exchange (3-3-5 Stack (Slant-Exchange Call))
    Animation Duration: 4.2s
    Direct URL: https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=rlong-335-stack&play=stack335-slant-exchange

    [SUMMARY & TACTICAL PURPOSE]
    - Motive: Hide every gap responsibility behind identical stacks, then move all six box defenders one gap at the snap so blockers chase a pre-snap picture that no longer exists while every gap stays owned.
    - Key Defender Put In Conflict: MIKE exchanging to weak A — the stacked backer whose late fill owns the gap the slanting nose abandoned
    - Why It Works: Blocking rules are built from pre-snap alignment; when all three linemen slant and all three backers exchange simultaneously, double teams form on empty spots and the puller kicks air.
    - Failure Mode / Defensive Counter: Perimeter option and quick toss attack the loop side mid-exchange — if the timing slips even one beat, an edge goes unowned and the keeper hits daylight.

    [SEQUENCING & GAME-PLAN LOGIC]
    - Sets Up: stack335-double-edge-storm
    - Plays Off: stack335-cross-dog-fire-zone
    - Visual Tell Cue: All six box defenders in perfect single file — each linebacker exactly behind his lineman, a picture no four-man front can show.

    [TIMELINE COACHING BEATS]
      * [T=0.0s] 1. Six Hats in a Single File: Three linemen align across the formation with all three linebackers stacked exactly one yard behind them at identical depth. The offense cannot tell who owns which gap — the whole point of the picture.
      * [T=1.0s] 2. All Three Slant Strong: At the snap every lineman moves one gap toward strength as a single unit. The weak end crosses the tackle’s face, the nose attacks strong A, and the strong end darts under the tight end — three blockers suddenly chasing ghosts.
      * [T=2.0s] 3. Backers Exchange Into Vacated Gaps: Behind the slant, each stacked backer fills the gap his lineman just abandoned: Sam spills outside, Mike takes the weak A, Will loops to strong C. Every gap stays owned while every blocker’s rule breaks.
      * [T=3.2s] 4. Handoff Into a Moving Wall: The fullback kicks at air where the looping Will was supposed to be, and the tailback runs straight into the slanting nose with the strong end stacking behind him. Tackle for loss inside a wall that moved.

>>> PLAY: Double-Edge Storm Dog (ID: stack335-double-edge-storm)
    Personnel: Base 3-3-5 Stack (3 DL + 3 LB + 5 DB)
    Formation: 11P Gun Spread 2x2 vs Stack
    Situation: 3rd & 6, own 40, must-pass down
    Defensive Look: Man-Free Behind the Dog (3-3-5 Stack (Double-Edge Storm))
    Animation Duration: 4.2s
    Direct URL: https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=rlong-335-stack&play=stack335-double-edge-storm

    [SUMMARY & TACTICAL PURPOSE]
    - Motive: Storm both C-gaps with the stacked backers while the ends slant inward, so the protection must choose an edge while the anchoring nose erases any interior answer.
    - Key Defender Put In Conflict: JACK — the weak stack backer whose outside burst arrives exactly after the tackle chases the slanting end inside
    - Why It Works: The four-man weave scrambles every slide call, the back can only take one storming edge, and man coverage behind removes all hot answers while the nose makes climbing the pocket impossible.
    - Failure Mode / Defensive Counter: Rhythm throws released before the weave develops, or max protect with two backs — the dog needs a standard five-man protection count to manufacture its free runner.

    [SEQUENCING & GAME-PLAN LOGIC]
    - Sets Up: stack335-cross-dog-fire-zone
    - Plays Off: stack335-slant-exchange
    - Visual Tell Cue: Pre-snap it reads like plain Cover 3 stack — no walk-ups anywhere; every rusher hid directly behind a lineman until the snap.

    [TIMELINE COACHING BEATS]
      * [T=0.0s] 1. Stacks Hide the Storm: Nothing about the pre-snap picture says blitz: three linemen across, three backers hidden directly behind them at identical depth, one safety high. Four potential rushers are invisible inside that single file.
      * [T=1.0s] 2. Ends Slant In, Edges Storm Out: The call fires as a four-man weave: both ends dart inside to the B-gaps while Jack and Spur burst outward through the C-gaps their linemen just vacated. Every blocker’s first target is already moving the wrong way.
      * [T=2.0s] 3. The Nose Anchors While Protection Tilts: The nose swallows the guard-center combo and refuses both A-gaps, so nobody can slide to help. The running back commits to the strong stormer — which means the weak edge now belongs to nobody.
      * [T=3.2s] 4. Free Edge Off the Blind Side: The tackle chased the slanting end inside and the left edge stands empty. Jack rounds it untouched and buries the quarterback as he climbs — the price of blocking rules written against a static front.

>>> PLAY: Safety-Corner Cross-Dog Fire Zone (ID: stack335-cross-dog-fire-zone)
    Personnel: Base 3-3-5 Stack (3 DL + 3 LB + 5 DB)
    Formation: 11P Gun Spread 2x2 vs Stack
    Situation: 2nd & 7, +45, spread passing down
    Defensive Look: Fire Zone (3 Under / 3 Deep) (3-3-5 Stack (Safety-Corner Cross-Dog))
    Animation Duration: 4s
    Direct URL: https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=rlong-335-stack&play=stack335-cross-dog-fire-zone

    [SUMMARY & TACTICAL PURPOSE]
    - Motive: Disguise a five-man fire zone behind a stacked single-high shell so spread protections commit to the wrong crosser while the safety-corner exchange manufactures interior heat.
    - Key Defender Put In Conflict: RCB darting inside — the blitzer whose delayed inside path arrives after the protection has fully committed to the widened safety
    - Why It Works: The cross scrambles counting rules, the back can only block one dog, and the fire-zone rotation has occupied every hot window before the quarterback finishes his hitch.
    - Failure Mode / Defensive Counter: Hot throws released on rhythm before the cross develops — if the ball is out early, only three linemen rushed and the vacated zones are still empty.

    [SEQUENCING & GAME-PLAN LOGIC]
    - Sets Up: stack335-zero-empty
    - Plays Off: stack335-slant-exchange
    - Visual Tell Cue: Pre-snap it reads single-high Cover 3 with stacked backers — the tell is only the safety creeping to nine yards without any linebacker moving with him.

    [TIMELINE COACHING BEATS]
      * [T=0.0s] 1. The Stacked Disguise: Single-high shell, three backers stacked directly behind three linemen, corners playing soft — it reads like plain Cover 3. Nothing in the picture announces that two defensive backs are about to rush.
      * [T=1.0s] 2. Safety and Corner Begin the Cross: The walked safety widens his rush lane toward the edge while the corner darts inside off it. Their paths swap mid-rush — whoever the protection assigns to each will be blocking the wrong man.
      * [T=2.2s] 3. Fire Zone Floods Behind: Three deep thirds rotate behind three under-zone droppers, and every quick window fills before the quarterback finishes his hitch. The drag hits Mike’s wall, the checkdown dies in Sam’s flat.
      * [T=3.2s] 4. Hot Window Belongs to the Hook: The running back slides to the darting corner, leaving the widened safety unblocked — so the hot throw comes out early, directly into Will’s flooding hook zone. Tipped at the catch point.

>>> PLAY: All-Out Zero Pressure vs Empty (ID: stack335-zero-empty)
    Personnel: Base 3-3-5 Stack (3 DL + 3 LB + 5 DB)
    Formation: Empty Gun 5-Wide vs Stack
    Situation: 4th & 3, opponent +38, do-or-die down
    Defensive Look: Zero Man (No Deep Help) (3-3-5 Stack (All-Out Zero Committee))
    Animation Duration: 4s
    Direct URL: https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=rlong-335-stack&play=stack335-zero-empty

    [SUMMARY & TACTICAL PURPOSE]
    - Motive: Punish empty-protection math with a six-man committee so five blockers always face one extra rusher while every receiver is stranded alone in zero man coverage.
    - Key Defender Put In Conflict: MIKE mugged over the A-gap — the free runner up the middle whose arrival coincides exactly with the forced throw
    - Why It Works: An empty backfield removes every extra protector and checkdown outlet; six rushers versus five blockers guarantee a free hat, and straight man coverage leaves no soft zone for hot throws to escape into.
    - Failure Mode / Defensive Counter: Quick stick-and-slant throws released on rhythm beat the rush before it lands — if the line slides correctly both ways, the defense has gambled everyone with nobody behind.

    [SEQUENCING & GAME-PLAN LOGIC]
    - Sets Up: None
    - Plays Off: stack335-double-edge-storm
    - Visual Tell Cue: Both safeties AND a linebacker aligned at LOS-level depth against empty — pure zero has nobody deeper than seven yards except the corners.

    [TIMELINE COACHING BEATS]
      * [T=0.0s] 1. Six Hats Walk Up Against Empty: The offense empties the backfield, and the answer is immediate: Mike mugged over the A-gap at a yard, both edge backers walked to three, safeties creeping. Six potential rushers stand inside eight yards of an unprotectable quarterback.
      * [T=1.0s] 2. Zero Call: All Six Go: No dropper, no exchange, no disguise — every box defender fires his gap at once. The ends slant inside, the edges storm outside, the nose charges between the guards and the mugged Mike shoots behind them.
      * [T=2.2s] 3. Five Blockers Cannot Match Six: The math was settled at the snap: with no back to help, five linemen must handle six rushers moving in four different directions. The interior pinches around the nose while both edges bend toward the quarterback.
      * [T=3.2s] 4. Hit As He Throws: The hot slant comes out on time — and still dies, because zero man means the weak safety is sitting on it with inside leverage while the free-hitting Mike arrives through the A-gap. Pressure and coverage arrive together.

SCHEME FAMILY: MARVIN LEWIS' COVER 2 MAN-UNDER [ID: cover2-man-under]
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Architect / Coach: Marvin Lewis
Organization / Team: Baltimore Ravens DC (1996-2001)
Category: DEFENSE
Tree Branch: two-deep-shell
Core Philosophy: The red-zone answer of Lewis' Baltimore defenses: two safeties splitting the deep halves at full depth while five defenders play straight man underneath. Press-trail corner leverage turns every compressed release and every fade attempt into a contested footrace, with the deep halves standing as pure insurance behind the trails. When the structure needs teeth, a walked safety converts it into max pressure with one man swallowing the entire deep zone.

PLAYS IN THIS SCHEME:

>>> PLAY: Red-Zone 2-Man vs Compressed Twins (ID: twoman-red-zone-compressed-twins)
    Personnel: Nickel 2-Man Package (4 DL, 3 LB, 4 DB)
    Formation: 2-Man Shell vs Gun 21 Personnel Compressed Right
    Situation: 2nd & Goal from the 8, red zone
    Defensive Look: Cover 2 Man-Under (Safeties Splitting Halves at 12) (Under Front, Four-Man Rush)
    Animation Duration: 4s
    Direct URL: https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=cover2-man-under&play=twoman-red-zone-compressed-twins

    [SUMMARY & TACTICAL PURPOSE]
    - Motive: Squeeze the red zone with straight man coverage under deep-half insurance so every route must beat a trail technique with no room to separate.
    - Key Defender Put In Conflict: LCB playing press-trail on the compressed X — his leverage alone decides whether the beater exists
    - Why It Works: Compressed alignments surrender release space, and trail technique converts every breaking route into a contested race with a safety waiting behind it.
    - Failure Mode / Defensive Counter: A true stack release beating the press cleanly in one move — then only the single deep half stands between the receiver and six.

    [SEQUENCING & GAME-PLAN LOGIC]
    - Sets Up: twoman-fade-beater-demo
    - Plays Off: twoman-edge-blitz
    - Visual Tell Cue: Both corners are pinned to their receivers at 1.5 yards while safeties sit at a full 12 — Cover 2 zone keeps its corners squatting at 10 with eyes on the QB.

    [TIMELINE COACHING BEATS]
      * [T=0.0s] 1. The Red-Zone 2-Man Picture: Five defenders are pinned to five eligibles at the line while both safeties split the halves at a full 12 yards — every route must individually beat its trail.
      * [T=0.9s] 2. Compression Meets Press: The tightened splits surrender all release space — both receivers are jacked at the line before their stems can build any momentum.
      * [T=1.9s] 3. Trail Technique Rounds Everything: With outside leverage the corners ride each breaking route upfield, turning slants into footraces the receivers run alongside defenders.
      * [T=3.1s] 4. Window Closed Over the Top: The forced slant is swatted at the catch point while both halves stand ready to cap anything that sneaks through — zero points from the trip.

>>> PLAY: Fade Beater Demo (ID: twoman-fade-beater-demo)
    Personnel: Nickel 2-Man Package (4 DL, 3 LB, 4 DB)
    Formation: 2-Man Shell vs Gun 12 Personnel Solo Left
    Situation: 3rd & Goal from the 6, red zone
    Defensive Look: Cover 2 Man-Under (Press-Trail Corners) (Under Front, Four-Man Rush)
    Animation Duration: 4s
    Direct URL: https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=cover2-man-under&play=twoman-fade-beater-demo

    [SUMMARY & TACTICAL PURPOSE]
    - Motive: Demonstrate why the classic red-zone fade fails against press-trail — the isolation throw offenses covet is exactly what this structure invites and erases.
    - Key Defender Put In Conflict: LCB playing outside-leverage press — his jam converts the fade into a footrace along a sideline he already owns
    - Why It Works: Outside leverage narrows the route before it develops, while the deep half erases anything that somehow clears the trail.
    - Failure Mode / Defensive Counter: A clean inside-to-outside stack beating the jam in one move — then only the safety’s angle stands between the fade and six.

    [SEQUENCING & GAME-PLAN LOGIC]
    - Sets Up: twoman-edge-blitz
    - Plays Off: twoman-red-zone-compressed-twins
    - Visual Tell Cue: The corner is at 1 yard with pure outside leverage staring through the receiver — soft-squat Cover 2 sits at 7 yards with eyes on the QB.

    [TIMELINE COACHING BEATS]
      * [T=0.0s] 1. Why the Fade Tempts: An isolated receiver with the end zone behind him is the throw every coordinator wants — but this island comes pre-loaded with an outside-leverage press corner.
      * [T=0.8s] 2. The Jam Steals the Release: A fade needs a clean stack from step one; the two-hand punch converts the release into a shoving match that kills the route’s spacing.
      * [T=1.9s] 3. Trail Rides It to the Sideline: With no room to stack, the receiver runs the fade alongside the corner, narrowing himself against the boundary he cannot escape.
      * [T=3.2s] 4. Half Safety Erases the Shot: The back-shoulder launch sails over both trail and receiver and out of bounds — the defense gambled nothing and lost nothing.

>>> PLAY: 2-Man Edge Blitz (ID: twoman-edge-blitz)
    Personnel: Nickel 2-Man Package (4 DL, 3 LB, 4 DB)
    Formation: 2-Man Shell vs Gun 11 Personnel 2x1 Right
    Situation: 3rd & 6, +38, obvious passing down
    Defensive Look: Cover 1-Man Rob (Lone Free Safety Deep) (Under Front, Walked-Safety Edge Blitz)
    Animation Duration: 4s
    Direct URL: https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=cover2-man-under&play=twoman-edge-blitz

    [SUMMARY & TACTICAL PURPOSE]
    - Motive: Convert the 2-man structure into maximum pressure by walking a safety off the edge while the lone free safety swallows the entire deep zone by himself.
    - Key Defender Put In Conflict: SS blitzing off the edge — the scanning back is his only blocker and arrives a full second late
    - Why It Works: Press coverage underneath buys exactly the extra beat of time the fifth rusher needs, and the center-field safety removes all fear of a shot over the top.
    - Failure Mode / Defensive Counter: An instant perimeter RPO thrown before the edge walker clears the tight end’s hinge block.

    [SEQUENCING & GAME-PLAN LOGIC]
    - Sets Up: twoman-goal-line-double-robber
    - Plays Off: twoman-red-zone-compressed-twins
    - Visual Tell Cue: The strong safety stands at 2 yards beside the tight end while the free safety roams alone at 13 — base 2-man keeps both safeties splitting halves at 12.

    [TIMELINE COACHING BEATS]
      * [T=0.0s] 1. The Walked-Up Safety Tell: The strong safety stands at 2 yards beside the tight end while the free safety roams completely alone at 13 — the five-man count is betrayed before the snap.
      * [T=0.9s] 2. Five-Man Protection Math: Five blockers must handle five rushers, and the only true blocker for the walking safety is a running back starting four yards away from the rim.
      * [T=1.7s] 3. Hot Windows Pressed Shut: Every quick answer is pressed underneath while the lone free safety removes any fear of a shot — the QB has nowhere to go with the ball early.
      * [T=2.8s] 4. Free Runner Off the Rim: The safety bends off the vacant tight-end spot into the escaping QB’s lap — five-man pressure cashing because coverage never had to help.

>>> PLAY: Goal-Line Double Robber (ID: twoman-goal-line-double-robber)
    Personnel: Nickel 2-Man Package (4 DL, 3 LB, 4 DB)
    Formation: Double Robber Shell vs Goal-Line Heavy I-Form
    Situation: 3rd & Goal from the 4, red zone
    Defensive Look: Cover 2 Man Rob (Safeties at 8, Corners Over Top) (Under Front, Four-Man Rush)
    Animation Duration: 4s
    Direct URL: https://schemedb.harlanljones.com/?scheme=cover2-man-under&play=twoman-goal-line-double-robber

    [SUMMARY & TACTICAL PURPOSE]
    - Motive: Protect the goal line without pressing by aligning corners over the top and converting both safeties into eye-keyed robbers who attack every throwing window in front.
    - Key Defender Put In Conflict: FS as the weak-side robber — he sits on the exact lane the goal-line slant must occupy
    - Why It Works: Run action freezes the linebackers but changes nothing for chest-keyed robbers, and over-the-top corners remove any fear of a shot behind the robbery.
    - Failure Mode / Defensive Counter: A true max-protect flood with four verticals stretching the over-the-top corners before the robbers can converge.

    [SEQUENCING & GAME-PLAN LOGIC]
    - Sets Up: twoman-red-zone-compressed-twins
    - Plays Off: twoman-fade-beater-demo
    - Visual Tell Cue: Corners line up 9 yards deep directly over their receivers instead of pressed at the line — base 2-man never surrenders that much cushion.

    [TIMELINE COACHING BEATS]
      * [T=0.0s] 1. The Over-the-Top Shell: Both corners align 9 yards deep directly over their receivers while both safeties sit at 8 as robbers — nothing is pressed, everything is watched.
      * [T=1.1s] 2. The Fake Moves Linebackers, Not Robbers: The dive action pulls both linebackers downhill for a beat, but the safeties key the QB’s chest and eyes instead of the backfield.
      * [T=2.2s] 3. Double Robbery Reads: On the shoulder turn both safeties break simultaneously — one to the seam window, one to the slant lane — while the over-the-top corners erase anything deeper.
      * [T=3.3s] 4. Slant Picked at Its Break: The goal-line slant lands directly in the weak robber’s hands with zero risk taken behind it — the double-robb structure cashes its specialty call.

================================================================================
PART 2: COACHING LINEAGE TREES & COACH PROFILES
================================================================================

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
COACHING TREE: SHANAHAN / KUBIAK WIDE-ZONE TREE [ID: shanahan-kubiak]
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Patriarch: Bill Walsh → Mike Shanahan & Gary Kubiak
Category: OFFENSE
System Summary: The most influential offensive lineage in modern NFL football. Stemming from Bill Walsh’s West Coast spacing and Mike Shanahan & Gary Kubiak’s legendary Denver Broncos zone-stretch run game. Powers today’s elite offenses led by Kyle Shanahan, Sean McVay, Klint Kubiak, Matt LaFleur, and Mike McDaniel through horizontal stretch runs, play-action deep shots, and disguise meshes identical for the first 1.2 seconds.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
COACHING TREE: ANDY REID WEST COAST / SPREAD RPO TREE [ID: reid-west-coast]
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Patriarch: Bill Walsh → Andy Reid
Category: OFFENSE
System Summary: A pillar of modern offensive innovation. Blends classic West Coast rhythm and pass spacing with modern college Spread RPOs, empty/bunch formations, Mesh shallow crosses, jet shovel screens, and 13-personnel tight-end power mismatches.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
COACHING TREE: POWER GAP & DUO / QB RUN-GAME TREE [ID: power-gap-duo]
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Patriarch: John Harbaugh → Greg Roman
Category: OFFENSE
System Summary: The downhill gap-scheme lineage: power, duo, counter, and pin-and-pull runs married to genuine quarterback run threat. Built on heavy personnel, play-action off identical run pictures, and forcing light boxes into unblockable run-pass conflicts.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
COACHING TREE: PETE CARROLL / ROBERT SALEH WIDE-9 & MATCH TREE [ID: carroll-saleh-wide9]
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Patriarch: Pete Carroll → Robert Saleh
Category: DEFENSE
System Summary: A defensive system defined by pure physical dominance and gap-integrity. Employs wide-9 defensive end splits and penetrating 3-techniques to create organic 4-man pressure, backed by disciplined Cover 3 Rip/Liz Match, split-field Cover 6 bracket coverages, and A-gap cross-dog fire zones.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
COACHING TREE: MIKE MACDONALD SIM-PRESSURE & HYBRID DISGUISE TREE [ID: macdonald-pressure]
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Patriarch: John Harbaugh → Mike Macdonald
Category: DEFENSE
System Summary: The cutting edge of NFL defensive design. Built on pre-snap ambiguity, Double-A mug and Amoeba fronts, 4-man Simulated Pressures (Creepers) dropping interior linemen into throwing windows while sending DBs, post-snap split safety spins, and Cover 0 peel blitzes.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
COACHING TREE: VIC FANGIO TWO-HIGH SHELL & QUARTERS TREE [ID: fangio-two-high]
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Patriarch: Vic Fangio
Category: DEFENSE
System Summary: The defensive system that forced modern offenses to adapt. Shows a static two-high safety shell before the snap to disguise Cover 6, Cover 8, and Quarters match calls, paired with light 3-man Penny fronts to stifle explosive downfield crossers and force long, mistake-prone drives.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
COACHING TREE: BILL BELICHICK / BRIAN FLORES PSYCHO BLITZ TREE [ID: belichick-flores]
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Patriarch: Bill Belichick → Brian Flores
Category: DEFENSE
System Summary: A radical, highly aggressive defensive philosophy based on extreme binary pressure looks: either sending 6-7 rushers in all-out Cover 0 house blitzes, or bluffing everybody and dropping 8 into muddy coverage zones.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
COACHING TREE: AIR CORYELL / RUN AND SHOOT VERTICAL PASSING TREE [ID: coryell-vertical]
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Patriarch: Don Coryell → June Jones
Category: OFFENSE
System Summary: The ancestor of every modern vertical passing attack. Don Coryell’s one-back Air Coryell route tree forced defenses to defend the entire depth of the field for the first time; June Jones’ Run and Shoot made receivers into live read-routes who converted their patterns on the fly against coverage leverage.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
COACHING TREE: AIR RAID SPACING TREE [ID: air-raid]
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Patriarch: Hal Mumme → Mike Leach
Category: OFFENSE
System Summary: The college game’s great equalizer: a handful of mesh, shallow, and stick spacing concepts repped thousands of times from empty and five-open formations, weaponizing distribution over play design and turning any coverage into a numbers problem.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
COACHING TREE: COLLEGE OPTION & SPREAD REVOLUTION TREE [ID: option-spread]
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Patriarch: Paul Johnson / Urban Meyer / Chris Ault / Art Briles
Category: OFFENSE
System Summary: Four parallel college revolutions that reshaped the run-pass interface: the flexbone triple option’s mathematical pitch geometry, Meyer’s spread-option zone read, Ault’s Pistol downhill physics, and Briles’ vertical choice shots off run action.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
COACHING TREE: DELAWARE WING-T DECEPTION TREE [ID: delaware-wing-t]
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Patriarch: Tubby Raymond
Category: OFFENSE
System Summary: Guard-pull buck sweep series with counter crisscross fakes and wingback motion — the gold standard of ball-handling deception, making three base plays look like nine through backfield choreography alone.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
COACHING TREE: BUDDY RYAN 46 PRESSURE TREE [ID: buddy-46]
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Patriarch: Buddy Ryan
Category: DEFENSE
System Summary: The most radical base defense ever fielded: an eight-man box with zero deep-middle help, isolated press corners, and unblockable edge overload combinations that broke protection rules by arithmetic. Its DNA survives in every modern Bear front and mug pressure.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
COACHING TREE: LEBEAU ZONE BLITZ FIRE ZONE TREE [ID: lebeau-zone-blitz]
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Patriarch: Dick LeBeau → Dom Capers
Category: DEFENSE
System Summary: The invention that changed defensive math forever: send five while dropping a lineman behind a fire zone, breaking slide-protection assignments without sacrificing zone integrity. The direct ancestor of today’s creeper and sim-pressure worlds.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
COACHING TREE: LANDRY FLEX / DOOMSDAY FRONT TREE [ID: landry-dallas]
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Patriarch: Tom Landry → Jimmy Johnson
Category: DEFENSE
System Summary: From the inventor of the 4-3 to its speed evolution: Landry’s staggered Flex alignments strangled sweeps with patient gap-zone convergence; Jimmy Johnson rebuilt Dallas with undersized penetration chaos that prefigured the modern attacking front.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
COACHING TREE: PHILLIPS TWO-GAP 3-4 TREE [ID: phillips-two-gap]
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Patriarch: Bum Phillips
Category: DEFENSE
System Summary: The revival of the modern 3-4: zero-tech nose two-gapping to free athletic linebackers, stand-up edge rushers as designated weapons, and second-level flow speed built specifically to counter Pittsburgh-style power football.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
COACHING TREE: TWO-DEEP SHELL / TAMPA 2 TREE [ID: two-deep-shell]
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Patriarch: Tony Dungy → Lovie Smith / Marvin Lewis
Category: DEFENSE
System Summary: Two safeties splitting the deep field as a committed identity: Tampa 2’s zone sink with the Mike running the deep hole, and Marvin Lewis’ red-zone 2-Man with pure man underneath — opposite underneath logic under an identical shell.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
COACHING TREE: MODERN COLLEGE HYBRID FRONT TREE [ID: college-defensive-fronts]
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Patriarch: Dave Aranda / Rocky Long
Category: DEFENSE
System Summary: The current college counter-punch to spread offense: Aranda’s tite front (4i-0-4i) played from peso hybrid personnel to erase B-gaps against zone read, and Rocky Long’s 3-3-5 stack where every box defender is a potential blitzer behind total pre-snap ambiguity.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
